Title: Brandade
Description: Classically in France, this is served over toasts or in mounds next to a frisee salad. In Spain and Italy, it is also served as fritters or stuffed into zucchini blossoms. In Spain and Italy, the cream is often left out, replaced by more olive oil. The flavor is stronger.

Ingredients.Name: Salt cod filets (about 1” at its thickest)
Garlic cloves, peeled and smashed to a paste (in mortar is best).
Red potato about 3 oz. peeled, boiled til soft and mashed.
Crispy breadcrumbs (in olive oil or butter)

Instructions: Rinse the salt from the surface of the cod. Soak in a large bowl of cold water (about 2-3 Qts.) – changed 2 or 3 times every day – for 2 to 3 days.

Place onions and bay leaves in a large pot with about 2 quarts of the water. Bring to boil and add the cod. Reduce to simmer and cook for 10-12 minutes. Taste the fish from the thickest part and if it is still very salty, break it up a bit and return to the pot for another few minutes. Drain well and discard onions and bay leaves.

Place olive oil in a heavy pot, about 2 ½ qt. saucepan works well. Heat the oil gently and add the cod. Stir the cod with the oil (a wooden spoon or other stiff spoon is best) increasing the speed and pressure of the stirring so that the cod begins to breakup and become fibrous. It’s done when the entire mass is fibrous and not lumpy. Mix the cream with the garlic and mix into the cod. Add the lemon juice and then taste and adjust seasoning if necessary (more lemon, pepper).

Fluff the mixture with a spoon and serve warm. If you do not want to use it right away (that day), do not add the garlic/cream as the garlic may overpower the cod if it sits. It remains good for several days. You can also freeze the cod mixture (without cream and garlic) until ready to serve. Reheat gently and add the garlic/cream and lemon juice and re-fluff.
Optional: This is great served with crispy breadcrumbs (toasted in olive oil or butter) sprinkled over the top.

Title: Goat Cheese Souffle
Description: This serves 6 easily if served with a salad of frisee or other chicories and a scoop of soufflé. For a heartier first course, it serves 4.

Ingredients.Name: Crumbled, creamy but tart goat cheese

Instructions: Preheat the oven to 400.
Butter a large (6 cup) soufflé dish. Coat it with 1-2 Tbsp. of the parmesan.
Warm the milk with the bay leaf, shallot, and 3 sprigs thyme until hot but not boiling. Remove from heat and let steep for 20 minutes.

Melt the butter in a heavy small saucepan or small skillet. Stir in the flour and cook until the flour is no longer raw and just about to start to color. Drain the milk, removing the solids, and whisk into the flour. Over medium-low heat, whisk the béchamel until it is thickening. Add ¾ tsp of salt, a few grinds of fresh pepper and then the cayenne.
Remove pan from heat and beat in the 4 egg yolks one at a time. When fully blended, add the goat cheese in crumbles and the remaining parmesan. It may be lumpy at this point and that’s o.k.

In a mixer, beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt until they can hold firm peaks. Stir 1/3 of them into the cheese mixture to lighten it and then fold in the rest. Pour into the soufflé dish. Run your finger around the inside edge of the rim of the dish. Sprinkle the remaining thyme leaves over the top (removed from the stems) and place in oven. Lower heat to 375 and bake for about 30 minutes or until very golden, puffed, but a little flexible when moved. Serve right away.

Title: Fresh Figs w/ Pepper Goat Cheese & Honey
Description: This can be very sweet, depending on your figs. Adjust seasoning to keep it from being cloying if you use this as a first course or hors d’oeuvres. It could be a great cheese course.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh ground black pepper + a little more to taste

Instructions: Warm the honey in a small saucepan or in the microwave with the ground pepper and pinch of salt to taste. Cut the figs into quarters but keeping ½” at the base so you can open them like a flower. Put about ½ tsp of cheese in each and drizzle with the pepper honey.

Title: Poached Tuna in Anchovy Sauce
Description: From Marcella Hazan.

Ingredients.Name: Yellowfin tuna, fresh, cut into 1" thick steaks

Instructions: Use a large saute pan or shallow wide pan that can hold the fish and veggies. Put in the celery, carrot, onion, vinegar, pinch of salt and enough water to cover the fish later. Bring to a boil for 10 minutes over med-high heat. Add tuna and when the water resumes a boil adjust to a simmer. Cover and cook for 8 minutes.

While fish is cooking, put the garlic, anchovies, capers, olive oil and lemon juice in a small bowl. Blend and then add the mustard and salt and liberal grindings of black pepper. Stir with a fork to combine really well.
When the tuna is done, retrieve it with a slotted spoon or spatula, pat dry and cut into slices 1 1/2 inches long.

In a ceramic or glass dish, large enough to accommodate the tuna in one layer without overlapping, Lightly smear the bottom with some of the caper and anchovy mixture. Lay in the tuna and cover with more of the spread. Smooth it with a spatula so it is fairly even. Cover well with plastic wrap. Let it set at room temperature for 6-8 hours. Refrigerate for 1-2 days, return to room temp and serve.

Title: Baked Pasta Bites
Description: Yield will vary, depending on size of pasta pieces and number per pound.

Ingredients.Name: Small stuffed pasta (fresh) such as tortellini or raviolini -
Chopped herbs such as basil or thyme depending on flavor of filling

Instructions: Preheat oven to 450*.
Bring large saucepan of water to boil. Line a medium baking sheet with parchment paper.

Add salt to boiling water. Add pasta and cook until just tender about 3-5 mins. depending of size of pasta. Drain well. Divide in half and place in 2 bowls. Toss each with butter. In one bowl, toss with poppy seeds. In other, toss with herbs and sea salt.

Spread pasta on baking sheet and sprinkle with parmesan. Bake about 5 minutes until golden brown. Turn pasta once and bake again about 3 minutes. Transfer to paper towel, transfer to platter and serve warm.

Title: Lamb Skewers w/ Mustard Sauce
Description: From Food & Wine Magazine (6/98).

Ingredients.Name: Lamb Loin, boneless, trimmed, halved lengthwise

Instructions: In a blender or small processor, combine oil, onion, wine, rosemary, garlic and dijon mustard and blend til smooth.
Put in resealable plastic bag with the lamb and refrigerate overnight.
In a small bowl, blend the whole grain mustard, crème fraiche, honey and a pinch of cayenne and black pepper. Whisk til smooth.

Remove lamb from bag, scrape off marinade and season with salt and pepper. Heat oil in non-stick skillet and add lamb to skillet when hot. Cook over high heat til browned about 3 minutes per side for medium rare. Remove from heat and cover with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes. Slice thinly, fold each slice and skewer. Serve warm with the dipping sauce. These are also good at room temperature if need be. Just keep covered with foil until serving time.

Title: Crab Salad w/ Celery
Description: This is intended as hors d'oeuvres. You can also serve as a first course by chopping the celery into the crab mixture and serving atop a bed of greens.

Ingredients.Name: fresh lump crabmeat, well picked over for shell and then drained
Fennel bulb, finely chopped, with fennel fronds saved for garnish
Sea salt and fresh black pepper

Instructions: Trim best 8 wide celery ribs. Clean well. Lay flat on cutting board and trim on a diagonal into 1-11/2" slices or a little longer if the celery isn't too wide. You should get at least 5 per rib

In a medium bowl. Combine the cream cheese, mayonnaise, lemon juice and zest, tarragon and parsley until well blended. Add remaining ingredients reserving fronds of fennel. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Spoon about 1 tsp. of salad into the celery ribs and garnish with snips of fronds. Keep cold until serving. Salad keeps one day if refrigerated but it is best to add the crab at the last minute though.

Title: Caponata for Hors d'oeuvres
Description: This makes about 2 toasts for 20 people, depending on how you mound it on the toasts.

Ingredients.Name: Plump garlic cloves, finely minced or pressed.
Garnishes - basil leaves, parsley or other herbs
Optional - parmesan cheese, high quality grated.

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350*.
In a small skillet, warm oil with the garlic cloves and cayenne. Heat until garlic is just translucent.
Place baguette slices on baking sheet and using a pastry brush, coat with the spiced oil.
Toast the slices in the oven for about ten minutes, turning once until they are crisp and golden but not dry.
Remove from oven and let cool completely. These can be made ahead and stored in an airtight contained once completely cooled. They'll keep at least one week.
Chop the ratatouille in a food processor by pulsing until just coarsely chunky. Don't over process.
Mound w/ a teaspoon a small amount on each toast. Garnish if desired with strips of basil, parsley, etc. Serve at room temperature.
Or for a special treat, leave the toasts on the baking sheet. Dust each with parmesan cheese and return the baking sheet to the broiler and cook until cheese is melted and bubbly. Serve warm.

Title: Armagnac Chevre
Description: Serve on small ultra-thin slices of toasted walnut bread. From Patricia Wells.

Ingredients.Name: Several drops of Armagnac or cognac
Goat cheese - very fresh and bright tasting

Instructions: In a small bowl, combine sugar and a few drops of alcohol, stirring to dissolve the sugar. In another small bowl crush the goat cheese lightly with a fork and add the sugar-alcohol mixture. Crush again. Taste. Gradually add more sugar and alcohol to taste. transfer to a ramekin and smooth top. Prepare in advance but bring to room temperature for full flavor. Makes about 1/2 Cup.

Title: Smoked Trout for Canapés
Description: Serve on cucumber slices, endive spears or on small toasted bread slices. This is based on a recipe by Patricia Wells

Ingredients.Name: Fennel fronds, chopped or other herbs such as dill, parsley or chives

Instructions: Trim fish of any bruised or ugly edges, skin or bones. Lay flat on the cutting board and cut into tiny cubes - don't mash or the texture will be unappealing. Toss with the cream and herbs in a small bowl. Spoon small amount onto cucumber rounds or other canapé base. Garnish with more herbs.

Title: Tuna a la Doppo
Description: I made this up from a great appetizer we had at Dopo restaurant in Oakland. It resembles their dish but is my own variation. They serve this over roasted sweet peppers but it is delicious with a small side of tender bitter greens very lightly dressed.

Ingredients.Name: Salt (sea) and fresh gr. Black pepper
Roasted red sweet peppers or 1 cup of tender bitter greens such as frisee or arugula.

Instructions: Cube the tuna into 1/3” cubes. Chop shallot finely and mellow in the vinegar for 15 minutes. Toast the pine nuts in a small skillet on the stove over medium heat until fragrant and just beginning to turn golden. Remove from heat and cool on a cutting board. Chop and reserve. Slice about half the fennel bulb into 1/8” slices and then cut again into dice. Chop the mint very fine.

In a medium size bowl, combine the tuna with the nuts, fennel, pecorino and toss. Whisk the champagne vinegar with the olive oil and drizzle about 2 Tbsp. over the tuna mixture. Toss gently and taste. The flavor should be bright and not too oily and slightly moist. Adjust the vinaigrette to your liking. Then, toss in the mint sparingly at first and taste again. The mint should not be assertive, just a fresh counter note to the cheese and nuts. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve over roasted sweet pepper (mounded on the pepper) or alongside a very lightly dressed salad of tender greens.

Title: Celery & Walnut Salad

Ingredients.Name: Fresh mozzarella, bufala or cows milk
Extra Virgin Olive Oil - Best Quality
Sea Salt and fresh ground black pepper

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350*
In a small ovenproof skillet scatter the walnut. Heat in the oven for approx. 5-8 minutes or until the nuts are fragrant and just beginning to brown. Let cool.

Wash celery and select 8 of the best spears of celery - tender and not bitter. Slice them at an extreme angle, very thin so they are long and almost noodle like. Place in a medium size bowl. Cut walnuts into quarters and mix with celery. Cut the mozzarella into small cubes, just slightly larger than the walnut. Add to the bowl and combine. Sprinkle with parsley to taste and toss with 2 Tbsp. olive oil. All the ingredients should be lightly coated with oil and parsley. Taste and add salt and pepper to taste. Place on salad plates and drizzle each with a little remaining oil.

Title: Anchovy-Garlic Crisps

Ingredients.Name: Plump, fresh garlic cloves, peeled & minced
Whole wheat bread, crust removed and cut into 1" slices

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375*.
Rinse anchovies well and remove bones. Pat dry and chop finely. Place in a small bowl with the milk. Set aside for 15 minutes. Drain and discard milk.
In a small skillet, combine anchovies, garlic and oil and cook over moderate heat just until the mixture is well blended and the garlic and anchovies melt into the oil - 2 to 3 minutes.

With a pastry brush, brush the slices of bread all over with the mixture. Place on a nonstick baking sheet and toast until well browned, turning the bread once for about 5 minutes. Remove from the sheet and cool on a rack. They are good warm or at room temperature.
Store in an airtight container for up to one week.

Title: Arugula & Braesola
Description: This is an adaptation of an appetizer I had in a small wine bar in Siena. They used a deer braesola which was delicious but I've never seen it here.

Ingredients.Name: Italian Braesola (German or Swiss is o.k. if you can't find Italian), thinly sliced
Extra Virgin Olive Oil - best quality (Tuscan if possible)
Parmigiana Reggiano, in large piece to be shaved
Sea Salt and fresh ground pepper

Instructions: Arrange the braesola on a serving platter in concentric circles.
In a large bowl, toss the arugula with the oil, controlling the amount of oil until the leaves are gently coated. Toss with the vinegar and salt and pepper until well distributed.
Cover the braesola with the arugula in gently mound.
Shave parmesan over in 1" wide shavings. Adjust for salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.

Title: Roquefort Dip

Ingredients.Name: Chopped chives or substitute other herbs
Roquefort cheese, imported French, at room temperature Sea salt and fresh pepper to taste

Instructions: Blend cottage cheese in the bowl of a food processor or blender until smooth. Add the cheese and herbs, breaking up the cheese into chunks. Pulse briefly to blend. Pulse until the herbs are distributed. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Make this at least 1 day in advance to let the flavors mellow.

Title: Spiced Nuts for Cocktails
Description: These go quickly so you might want to make a double batch.

Ingredients.Name: Cayenne Pepper or more if you like it hot

Instructions: Preheat oven to 325*.
Mix chili powder, cumin, curry, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper in a small bowl.
In a nonstick skillet, heat the oil and add the spice mixture. Stir well while simmering the spices to mellow and blend the flavors. This should take only a couple minutes.
Remove from heat.

In a medium bowl, pour in nuts and then the spices and mix well until all the nuts are coated. Toss in the sugar, again mixing until well blended. Spread on baking sheet in a single layer and so they're not all lumped together. Bake for 12-15 minutes until fragrant and toasty.

Remove from oven and return to medium bowl, scraping any spices that have fallen off back over the nuts. While still warm, toss with the sea salt and taste. Add more salt if necessary. Let cool completely for at least one hour and store in an airtight jar. Keeps for several weeks if stored well.

Title: Roasted Mushrooms

Ingredients.Name: Garlic clove, finely minced or pressed

Instructions: Preheat oven to 450*
In a bowl, combine lemon juice, thyme, garlic, Tabasco, salt and pepper. Stir in oil and then toss in mushrooms.

Spread mushrooms on baking sheet and bake for 30m minutes. Turn over and bake for another 15 minutes until tender. Let cool before serving. These keep for up to 4 days refrigerated. Return to room temp before serving.

Title: Stuffed Artichokes

Ingredients.Name: Fresh Fava Beans - Removed from pod, blanched and removed from tough shell.
Sea salt and fresh ground black pepper

Instructions: Prepare artichokes - remove tough outer stems, trim tops and stems and peel off extra tough leave ends. Cut in half, remove chokes and drop into a pot of acidulated water with the juice of 4 lemons. Bring to boil and cook until chokes are tender. Drain well.
Preheat oven to 375*.
Peel potatoes and cut into small cubes.

In a large skillet, heat 4 tbsp. olive oil with the chopped garlic. Add potatoes and cook over med high heat until golden. Add the fresh fava beans. Cut whites and light green of scallions into 1" pieces and add to the pan. Toss well and add a little more olive oil if necessary. Continue to saute until well cooked and season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat, toss in bread crumbs and chopped parsley to taste.
Stuff each artichoke half. Lay artichokes in a baking dish, sprinkle with extra stuffing, and extra olive oil. Bake until golden on top and fully heated through, approx. 20 minutes.
Serve drizzled with Extra Virgin Olive oil and some additional parsley.

Title: Mushroom/Goat Cheese

Ingredients.Name: Mixed wild mushrooms, chanterelles, shitakes, etc.
Cloves garlic, smashed with salt to make a paste

Instructions: Toss all ingredients and roast at 425* for 15 minutes. Drop goat cheese around top and roast again for 7-8 minutes until cheese is melted. Drizzle with chili oil and fresh thyme. Serve.

Title: Yogurt Cheese
Instructions: Place yogurt in a coffee filter and drain over a pot until the liquid is gone and the yogurt is thick like soft cream cheese. You should empty the pot/cup frequently so you can tell how much is draining. Sprinkle well with salt, and cover with a thin layer of olive oil. serve.

Title: Spiced Yogurt Muffins

Ingredients.Name: Unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
Unsweetened applesauce or finely tart apples chopped fine in a food processor

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Fill muffin tins with aluminum foil muffin cups.
In a processor, mix the flours, brown sugar, flax seed, baking soda, baking powder, 1 tsp. of cinnamon, and other spices.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs with the butter, applesauce, yogurt and vanilla.
Pour the dry ingredients into the bowl with the liquids and mix until just blended and no dry areas.
Divide among the 18 muffin tins.
Bake for 18 minutes until the tops are springing back when pressed and cool for about 5 mins.

Title: Oatmeal Buttermilk Biscuits
Description: This are incredibly delicate, buttery and good with any jam or honey. Also, can be used as a shortcake for berries.

Ingredients.Name: Butter, unsalted, chilled and cut into cubes

Instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Pulse the oatmeal in the bowl of a food processor until finely ground. Add the ﬂours, salt, baking powder, and baking soda and pulse a few times to blend. Add the chilled butter and pulse several times, until the mixture is course and the pieces of butter are about the size of small peas. Do not overprocess; the dough should not come together – it is better to underdo this step than overdo. Transfer the dough to a large bowl and make a well in the center of the ﬂour mixture. Pour in the buttermilk. Stir the mixture with a large spoon, gently lifting and working the ﬂour into the buttermilk. The dough should almost come together but not form a solid mass. Do not keep working but stop and pour out onto a work surface dusted with flour. Gently bring the dough together and pat into a ½” – ¾ ” thick circle. Using a 2 to 2 ½” round cutter, cut out the biscuits. (If the cutter sticks to the dough, dip the cutter in ﬂour before cutting.) Place the biscuits on the baking sheet. Take the remaining dough scraps and gently bring them together, pat out again, and re-cut, being careful not to the dough. Brush the tops of the biscuits lightly with buttermilk. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through baking, until a rich golden brown. Serve warm.

Title: Buckwheat Pepper Crisps

Ingredients.Name: Egg, at room temp for at least 30 min
Optional – substitute 1 cup whole milk for skim and cream

Instructions: Preheat to 350.
Blend dry ingredients in a bowl. In a blender, put the egg, butter and milk/cream. Blend the wet ingredients until blended and add the flour mixture until smooth.
On a non-stick baking sheet, drop teaspoon size mounds of batter about 4” apart (or use an oiled baking sheet, regular).
Bake for 8-10 minutes until just golden along the edges. Transfer to wire rack carefully.
Keep cooking batches of crisps until done. They will keep in an airtight container for a week or so. Layer with waxed paper or parchment to keep from sticking.

Title: Blueberry Muffins

Ingredients.Name: Unsalted butter, softened at room temp.

Instructions: Preheat over to 400 and butter 15 muffin cups
Beat the 1/2 stick butter with the sugar in a large bowl with electric mixer until well blended. Pour in the milk, add the egg, and beat well.

Sift the 1-3/4 cups flour with the baking powder and salt into a bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just moistened. Toss the blueberries with the remaining tablespoon flour in another bowl and stir into the batter. Fill the muffin cups halfway with the batter. Bake for 15 minutes or until lightly browned on top.
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes

Title: Yogurt Scones
Description: These scones are light and fluffy - more like biscuits and perfect alone or with honey and/or jam!
Instructions: Preheat oven to 425*

In the bowl of a food processor, combine dry ingredients and pulse until incorporated. Add butter and pulse until coarse meal consistency - not uniform. Add the egg and pulse a couple times. Add yogurt and pulse a few times. Add milk and pulse until fully incorporated.

On a floured work surface, pat dough together and knead gently, adding flour to keep it from sticking to your hands and the surface, for a minute or two until smooth. Pat into a circle about 1/2 - 3/4 inch thick. Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with sugar. Cut into 12 wedges and place on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 10-12 minutes until golden, watch to prevent bottom from browning too much. Serve immediately is best but they keep well for a day. You can always rewarm them before serving - but too much and they will dry out.

Title: Buckwheat Crepes
Description: Makes 8 crepes
Instructions: In a blender process egg, milk, flours, salt and oil until smooth. Refrigerate 2 hours or overnight. In a crepe pan over medium heat, heat 1 tsp butter to coat pan evenly. With pan at a slight angle, pour in about 1/4 c. batter into center tilting and spreading evenly over the entire surface. Cook until golden 1-2 minutes, transfer to plate and cover. Repeat.
If holding for more than a few minutes, separate crepes with parchment or waxed paper.

Title: Foccacia Dough (Pizza )
Description: These are simple to make and very versatile. They freeze well so make the entire batch.

Ingredients.Name: All-purpose flour, plus some for kneading
Extra Virgin Olive Oil for bread

Instructions: In a glass measuring cup or deep small bowl, sprinkle the yeast over the warm water. Stir in the sugar and let stand for approx. 5 minutes or until foamy.
In a large mixing bowl, mix 2 cups of the flour with the salt. Add the yeast mixture and stir until smooth. Add the remaining flour and stir until a stiff dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes. Brush a large mixing bowl with olive oil and transfer the pizza dough to it.

Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm and draft-free location. When doubled in bulk (about 1 hour), punch down and knead it three times. Divide the dough into six equal pieces and roll into small balls.
Prepare bread or wrap dough balls individually in plastic wrap and freeze in freezer bags. They'll keep for up to one month in the freezer. To use defrost in the refrigerator and use.
To make bread:
Preheat oven with pizza stone for at least 30 minutes at 500 degrees.
Press dough out on a floured surface into small 6-8 inch rounds or ovals. Brush with Extra Virgin Olive

sprinkle with salt and chopped rosemary. Make small slits in the dough across surface so it doesn't puff too much. Bake on the hot stone for approx. 5 minutes until golden. Repeat for each dough ball.

Title: Best Granola
Instructions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees. Prepare a large cookie sheet lined with parchment paper.

Crumble almonds slightly and mix all the dry ingredients together. Heat oil and honey until they foam up completely, whisk quickly to incorporate them fully. Quickly add extracts to liquid mixture, whisk, and pour liquid mixture over dry ingredients and mix well until all dry ingredients are coated with the mixture. Place on a cookie sheet and spread evenly. Bake for 20 min, remove from oven and mix, particularly pulling the edges inward so they don’t brown too fast. Rotate pan and Bake another 5 minutes. Check for browning and keep watch closely for another 3 to 8 minutes to get the oats lightly golden all over. Do not let it get too brown or the mix will taste burnt. Leave the mixture on the cookie sheet to cool (this is what makes the clusters and ensures a crispness). If you think you’ve hit or exceeded its proper browning, remove the mixture from the pan right away by lifting the parchment onto a cool counter to stop the cooking.
Note:
* I like wildflower or orange blossom honey but feel free to try different flavors of honey.
**This can be adjusted with a different combination of nuts but you’ll likely need to adjust the size of the chopped nuts so they roast well without browning too quickly.

Title: Buttermilk Pancakes
Description: If you love pancakes, double this. These are great with real maple syrup and some tart fresh berries...

Ingredients.Name: Buttermilk, 1% (plus a little extra if needed)

Instructions: Mix together oatmeal and buttermilk in a large bowl. Let sit while you prepare the rest.
Warm butter in microwave until just melted. Cool
Whisk egg into oatmeal buttermilk mixture until incorporated.
In a medium bowl, mix together dry ingredients with a fork until combined well.
When cool, mix butter into wet ingredients.
Heat a large skillet with the vegetable oil. When hot, smear oil into a thin film all over.
While the pan heats, quickly mix dry and wet ingredients until no dry lumps. Add more buttermilk if too thick from standing. The consistency should be thick but loose and not stiff.

In the hot skillet, test a tablespoon. If it sizzles, cook it for one or two minutes and check to see if the pan is too hot or too cool but checking how the underside is cooking it should be golden but not too dark.

Cook all pancakes without crowding, usually in groups of 2 to 3. Optimum size is about 1/3 cup for each cake. Cook on one side until edges look firm and bubbles form in the center. Turn and cook about 1-2 minutes longer and serve immediately. Both sides should be just golden.
The center of these cakes should be cooked through but very moist and creamy.

Title: Berry Bread Pudding
Description: This is delicious for breakfast but it also makes a hearty dessert. You can substitute a variety of fruit - just adjust the sugar for the fruits' sweetness.

Ingredients.Name: Cubed 1" bread, preferably country sourdough- with crusts removed if they are very heavy.
Press bread into the cup to measure - err on more bread rather than less
Fennel bulbs, green parts trimmed, and washed,

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375.
Toss bread cubes with 2 Tbsp. of the butter and place on baking sheet. Toast for approx. 10 minutes or until golden.

Meanwhile, Whisk eggs with sugar in a large bowl. Place milk in small saucepan and scrape vanilla bean into the milk. Heat until almost beginning a boil. Slowly whisk into eggs. Rinse and drain berries.
Use remaining butter to butter a large soufflé dish or other deep baking dish.

Layer thinly bread then berries, ending with berries. Pour hot custard over and place in hot oven. Reduce heat to 350 and bake for approx. 45 minutes to 1 hour until puffed and tester comes out clean.
In last 20 minutes, combine sugar with cinnamon and sprinkle on top for a crispy sweet crust. If serving for dessert, increase amount of cinnamon and sugar.
* Substitute apples for berries and reduce sugar in recipe by 1/4 C. Other fruit can be substituted, such as peaches, adjusting the sugar depending on sweetness of fruit.

Title: Summer Corn Cakes
Description: These can be made in winter without the fresh corn.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh corn kernels from 1 large ear

Title: Plum Caramel Coffee Cake

Ingredients.Name: Vanilla bean, seeds scraped into the topping

Instructions: Sprinkle the yeast over the warm water and allow to rest 5 minutes until it dissolves.

Put the milk and shortening in a small pan and heat, stirring together until the shortening melts. Transfer to a mixing bowl and stir in the sugar and salt until blended. Let the mixture cool, then add the dissolved yeast. Add the egg and mix well. Stir in the flour and mix until the dough is smooth. The dough should be slightly sticky; if it isn't, add 2 or 3 tablespoons milk.
Grease the baking pan or dish. Spread the dough out in the pan by dipping your fingers in cold water (so the dough doesn't stick to your hands) then pat the dough evenly into the pan.
For the topping: stir together the brown sugar, yogurt, and vanilla in a small bowl. Cover the dough and let rise for about 11/2 hours, or refrigerate overnight and bake in the morning.

Bake in a preheated oven (350F) for 15 minutes, and then spread the topping over the cake. Bake an additional 20 minutes if the dough has risen at room temperature or bake an additional 30-35 minutes if the dough is chilled from resting overnight in the refrigerator.

Title: Oatmeal Buttermilk Pancakes
Description: This recipe makes a creamy, light pancake with a touch of tang from the buttermilk which is great with maple syrup.

Ingredients.Name: Milk - a few tablespoons, if needed

Instructions: Blend oatmeal with buttermilk in large bowl and let stand for a few minutes. Add egg and butter and blend well. In another bowl, blend dry ingredients well. Add to the wet ingredients and blend well. If too thick, add a tablespoon or two of milk. As the mixture sits, the oatmeal will absorb the moisture and you may need to add a little milk again.

Heat a large skillet spread with a tablespoon or two of vegetable oil until hot. Drop about 1/4-1/3 Cup batter onto hot skillet. Cook one pancake for about 3-minutes on one side. When the edges begin to firm, flip. The pancake should be golden brown. Continue cooking for another minute or two, modulating the heat to prevent it from browning too much. Continue in batches as large as your pan will allow. Serve with fresh berries and real maple syrup.

Title: Eggs w/ Shitakes & Goat Cheese

Ingredients.Name: Large shitakes, stems removed and cleaned

Instructions: Melt the butter in a sauté pan over low heat. While butter is melting, slice the mushrooms fairly thin and toss in the butter. Cook until the mushrooms are tender. Beat the eggs with a fork and add to the pan, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and keep cooking gently on low-medium heat, lifting the eggs that cook on top of the liquid so they cook evenly. Before fully cooked, crumble the goat cheese over the top and toss gently until the eggs are cooked through. Sprinkle on the parsley and serve with a sprinkling of salt

Title: My Scrambled Eggs #2

Ingredients.Name: Same ingredients as in #1 but substitute
Greens, washed and sliced into ribbons (use spinach or chard)

Instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet with the bacon until the bacon is golden brown. Add the shallot and cook until translucent. Add the greens and cook until fully wilted. If using chard, cook for about 3-5 minutes until tender. Add the eggs and mix well until the greens are fully incorporated. Continue to cook and when almost cooked, add the cheese.

Title: My Scrambled Eggs #1
Instructions: Melt the butter gently over medium low heat and add the shallot, and cook until the shallot is translucent. Beat the eggs with a fork until well combined and add to the skillet, sprinkle with a little salt and pepper. Gently scramble the eggs, lifting the cooked part up over the liquid until the eggs are almost cooked, but still very moist. Sprinkle the cheese over the eggs and continue to heat until the eggs are cooked but moist. Sprinkle with herbs and a little more salt. Serve immediately.

Title: Crispy Waffles
Instructions: Preheat oven to warm, approx. 200*
Prepare waffle iron.
In a large bowl, mix dry ingredients, except sugar and whisk.
In a small bowl or large measuring cup, blend buttermilk, milk, oil and egg yolk.

In a small bowl, whip egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form, sprinkle sugar a little at a time over the egg whites and continue beating until all is incorporated and the peaks are glossy and stiff.
Mix wet ingredients into the dry and whisk until incorporated, don't worry about small lumps. Add egg whites and fold in with a spatula. Beat in vanilla, if using.
Heat waffle iron, oil well and cook until golden and crisp, according to the instructions on your particular waffle iron.
Keep waffles warm in the oven, directly on the rack until all are ready to serve.
Substitutions:
Cornmeal waffles - substitute 1/4-1/2 Cup cornmeal for flour.

Title: Joe’s Meyer Lemon Panna Cotta

Ingredients.Name: Combine the cream, milk, sugar, and salt in a large saucepan and cook, stirring frequently, over medium heat. Put the yolks in a heat-proof bowl and whisk lightly. When the cream mixture is starting to steam and tiny bubbles have formed along the edge, whisk a cup or so, ¼ cup at a time, into the yolks. The idea here is the raise the temperature of the eggs so they won’t curdle when added to cream. Once the eggs are tempered, slowly whisk them into the cream mixture. Stirring constantly, cook over low heat roughly 5 minutes, or until the cream mixture has thickened enough to coat the back of a wooden spoon. Turn off heat and stir in the bourbon and vanilla extract. Pour into a large bowl, cover, and chill for a long time–5 hours or more is optimal (For the best chill, place the bowl of custard over a bowl of ice water.). Then process according to your ice-cream maker’s instructions, noting that the ice cream could be quite runny after 20 – 30 minutes of churning. Spoon ice cream out of ice cream maker and freeze for as long as you can, preferably overnight for a well-cured scoop.
Non-fat or reg. fat Greek Yogurt
Sweet butter, very cold & cut into cubes
Fresh ultra ripe figs, washed and tops trimmed
Mild flavored honey & ¼ tsp. lemon zest or red jam – plum, current, berry, etc.

Instructions: In a large fluted tart pan, line the bottom with parchment, cut to fit.

Pulse all the dry ingredients in the processor briefly until blended. Add the butter and pulse until the butter is fairly evenly incorporated in small bits. Add the rosemary and the egg white and pulse together until the dough just begins to form a large ball in the processor with some crumbly bits around it. Remove and working quickly so the crust stays cool, press the dough into the tart pan bottom so you have an even layer and then work up the sides pressing the dough into an even, and slightly thicker than the bottom, edge. Keep a small ball – like a round quarter for patching. Place in refrigerator and chill for about 30 mins.

Heat the oven to 400degrees. Place the tart pan in the center and bake for 20 minutes. Remove and if the crust has opened up large cracks, gently press tiny amounts of the dough into the cracks – it usually works best with a gently sliding motion so you don’t break the fragile edges. Return to the oven and continue cooking another 5 – 10 minutes until the crust is evenly golden brown. Remove from oven and cool.

When the tart is cool, whisk together the filling ingredients. Slice the figs in half. Spread the filling in the pan evenly and lay the figs in concentric circles around the tart. No need to overlap them. If your figs are not super sweet and jammy, you can glaze them with a mixture of honey and lemon zest. Just warm the honey in the microwave so it is easy to brush on, add the zest, and brush the figs lightly. Alternatively, you can also use some kind of rose colored jam to give the figs a pretty color.

Title: Lemon Curd Tart

Ingredients.Name: Partially pre-baked short pastry shell cooled

Instructions: Oven at 375 degrees.
Grate lemon peel into small bowl. Juice the lemons and strain the juice into the same bowl. Force as much of the juice and pulp through the strainer making sure the seeds don’t go.

Beat the eggs and egg yolks with the sugar in a heavy non-corroding saucepan until just mixed. In a small bowl or cup, place the cornstarch and then gradually add the milk to the starch stirring well. Stir in the juice mixture. It may look curdled but it’s o.k. Cut the butter into pieces and add to the mixture with the salt. Cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened like crème anglais. Cook 5 mins off the heat to thicken more, and whisk a little to smoothi it.
Make sure your tart shell is cool and then pour in the mixture and smooth the top. Bake for 30-35 mins until just beginning to speckle with little brown spots. Cool and serve.
** If you omit the cornstarch, the tart will be fine – just will not brown.

Title: Bourbon Ice Cream
Instructions: Combine the cream, milk, sugar, and salt in a large saucepan and cook, stirring frequently, over medium heat. Put the yolks in a heat-proof bowl and whisk lightly. When the cream mixture is starting to steam and tiny bubbles have formed along the edge, whisk a cup or so, ¼ cup at a time, into the yolks. The idea here is the raise the temperature of the eggs so they won’t curdle when added to cream. Once the eggs are tempered, slowly whisk them into the cream mixture. Stirring constantly, cook over low heat roughly 5 minutes, or until the cream mixture has thickened enough to coat the back of a wooden spoon. Turn off heat and stir in the bourbon and vanilla extract.

Pour into a large bowl, cover, and chill for a long time–5 hours or more is optimal (For the best chill, place the bowl of custard over a bowl of ice water.). Then process according to your ice-cream maker’s instructions, noting that the ice cream could be quite runny after 20 – 30 minutes of churning. Spoon ice cream out of ice cream maker and freeze for as long as you can, preferably overnight for a well-cured scoop.

Title: Honey Fig Ice Cream
Description: This is based on my Adriatic Honey Figs which are super big and super sweet. If you use other figs, make sure they are very ripe and you’ll need to adjust the sugar to your taste. This is great with blackberries or brandied sour cherries, carmelized almonds or hazelnuts, etc.

Ingredients.Name: Large Honey Figs (approx. 2 lbs) – if using other figs, you might need as many as 20.
Sugar or other sweetener (honey and Agave work well)
¼ tsp. Vanilla or 1 Tbsp. Brandy
Juice of 1 small Meyer lemon, or ½ a regular lemon.

Instructions: Cut off the stem ends of figs, and cut into 6-8 pieces each. In a medium large saucepan, add ½ cup water and the figs. Heat until gently boiling, reduce heat and cook about 10 mins, until the figs have released their juices. Add the citrus zest and juice and sugar and cook about 20-30 mins until very jammy and thick. Watch so it doesn’t stick and scorch. Remove from heat and cool.

When cool, blend in a blender with the cream until very smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning. Add more citrus if it’s flat but not so much that it is overbearing. You can also add vanilla or a little brandy.
Freeze in an ice cream maker until firm and creamy. This keeps really well and is delicious with a range of sauces.

Title: Blackberry Chile Sauce
Description: This is amazing over ice cream. You can thicken it further by cooking it more once the syrup is made. It’s also good as a syrup for cocktails or to glaze meats or chicken. If you cook it down, it becomes jam and you can use it for other things too.

Ingredients.Name: Sugar (add more if blackberries aren’t very sweet)
Blackberries – if they are large, you may want to use a few more.

Instructions: Discard stems from chiles. Break them into pieces with the seeds and add to the water in a medium saucepan. Add the sugar and lemon juice and bring to boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Boil gently for about 15 minutes until reduced to about 2 cups. Let cool off heat for a few minutes until warm but not hot.

Puree blackberries in blender, and then force them through a sieve to remove seeds. Pour chile mixture into the blender and puree, thensieve all solids out, pressing with the spoon to push all the liquid through. Add to the chile mixture and blend well with a whisk. Cool to room temperature.
Keeps refrigerated for one month.

Title: Les’ Favorite Cookies
Description: These are from our friend Joe – Yummy crispy chocolate chip cookies.

Ingredients.Name: Special flour – flavor of your choice – or add ¼ cup more all-purpose flour

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees and make sure rack is in the middle.
Line 2 baking sheets with parchment.
On a piece of parchment, sift flour, salt, baking soda and special flour if using.

In bowl of standing mixer, with paddle attachment, beat butter with sugar until blended and add the corn syrup and yolk, milk, and vanilla and blend on low for about 1 more minute, scraping bottom and sides until fully incorporated. Add the dry ingredients slowly by shaking the parchment gently. When fully incorporated, stop – don’t overbeat. Gently beat in the chocolate until just well distributed.

Using a small ice cream scoop – about 1 tbsp. in volume – drop on parchment lined sheets at least 2-3” apart. Bake one sheet at a time for 12 mins. Let cool completely so they get crisp before storing them.

Title: Summer Ice Plain

Ingredients.Name: Vanilla bean or 1 tsp vanilla extract

Instructions: Blend sugar, yoghurt and buttermilk in large bowl. Keep very cold. Scrape the vanilla bean into mixture. Stir in salt. Process in Donvier or other ice cream maker. Freeze until firm - at least 2 hours before serving. This melts quickly so serve immediately.
This recipe doubles easily to make a quart.
Variation: Lime Ice: Substitute 1/4 C. fresh lime juice and 1 tsp zest for fruit. Omit vanilla.

Title: Chevre Fondant
Description: This is an Eric Ripert recipe that he serves with Bacon Ice Cream but we love it just by itself with the wine caramel **You’ll need to make some traditional crème anglais for this. I serve this with poached pears and marinated figs for a special dessert.

Ingredients.Name: Plain chevre, softened to room temp
Gelatin softened in cold water or 1 tsp powdered

Instructions: For the Chevre:
Make the crème anglais and while it is still warm, add the gelatin to dissolve.
In the bowl of a mixer with a paddle attachment, combine the chevre and sugar on medium speed until smooth, light and fluffy.
Combine the chevre and crème anglais mixtures. Whip the cream and fold it into the mixture.

Transfer the mixture to the selected dishes – use either 1 ½” square molds set on a baking sheet, or decorative individual glasses, or in a large pan for scooping later. Set into freezer allowing 2-4 hours to set completely depending on size of dishes.
Caramel:

Combine sugar and water in a heavy small saucepan. Over high heat, cook the sugar until it turns a medium amber color. While the sugar is caramelizing, heat the wine in another saucepan. When sugar reaches the desired color, remove immediately from the heat and slowly add the red wine. Return to the heat and stir until the hardened bits of sugar dissolve. Continue to reduce until a slightly thickened consistency is achieved.

Title: Goat Cheesecake w/ Lemon
Description: From Mario Batali’s Babbo Cookbook

Title: Tea & Honey Crisps
Description: I got this from a magazine many years ago.

Ingredients.Name: Decaf Earl Grey tea leaves (2-3 bags)

Instructions: Special equipment: disposable Styrofoam plates; a small sharp knife such as an X-Acto; a 17- by 11-inch nonstick bakeware liner such as Silpat; a small offset spatula

Draw desired shape of cookie on a Styrofoam plate, then cut out shape with X-Acto knife and discard shape. If desired, cut out additional shapes from same plate. Trim plate, leaving a 1-inch border around stencil(s). Make more stencils with more plates if desired.
Put oven rack in middle position and preheat oven to 350°F. Line a large baking sheet with nonstick liner.

Beat together butter, confectioner’s sugar, honey, and tea leaves in a large bowl with an electric mixer at medium speed until combined well. Add egg whites 1 at a time, beating well after each addition. Reduce speed to low, then mix in flour until just combined.

Place stencil on liner and spread batter with spatula over stencil to completely cover opening. Carefully lift stencil from liner and stencil more cookies in same manner about 1 inch apart. Bake until edges are deep golden brown, 6 to 9 minutes. Cool cookies 1 minute on sheet, then transfer with spatula to a rack to cool completely. (To curl cookies, drape while hot over handles of wooden spoons or rolling pins to cool.) Stencil and bake more cookies with remaining batter.

Title: Blackberry Crisp
Description: This is my adaptation of a recipe I think may be from Marion Cunningham

Ingredients.Name: Sugar – adjust to sweetness of fruit

Instructions: 1. Preheat the oven to 375°. Generously butter an oval or square baking dish, about 8" × 8"× 2".

2. For the crust: Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, almonds and salt in the bowl of a processor and process until almonds are ground. In a large mixing bowl, make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and add the beaten egg. Stir mixture with a fork until it gets crumbly, the consistency of cornmeal. If mixture is too dry, first, try to really work the egg into the dry mixture. If that doesn’t work, add a little more of another beaten egg.
3. For the filling: Place the berries into another large mixing bowl. Stir the sugar and flour together, then sprinkle over the fruit and carefully toss until it coats the fruit thoroughly.
4. Pour the berries into the buttered baking dish and spread evenly, and pat them gently with your hands.
5. Sprinkle the crumbly flour mixture evenly over the top of the fruit. Drizzle the melted butter evenly over it. Place in the oven and bake about 40 minutes, or until the topping is golden.
6. Serve warm with whipped cream or ice cream. Or serve at room temperature, and the crust will have absorbed even more of the berries' juices.

Title: Salted Caramel & Yogurt Ice Cream

Ingredients.Name: Greek Yogurt (2% is best but 0% is o.k.)
Sea Salt, flaky (not fine or coarse)

Instructions: Heat sugar and water in a stainless saucepan over medium high heat. When the sugar melts, continue boiling at a medium boil until the sugar begins to turn golden. Watch it carefully, and remove it from the heat when thoroughly golden – it will continue to cook so don’t let it get too dark or it will be bitter. Place pan in sink and very carefully add ½ the cream. It will bubble up so be cautious. Stir it to incorporate the cream. If sticky on the bottom, set on fire again and melt the thick caramel into the cream. Do not boil. Remove from heat and add the rest of the cream. Transfer to small metal bowl and set in freezer to cool.

Stir greek yogurt in a medium large bowl until it is smooth. When the caramel is cool, stir into the yogurt. Add ¼ tsp of the salt, and taste. Add more salt to taste. Churn in ice cream maker, by hand or in an electric maker.

Title: Galettes
Description: There is no end to what you can fill these with. The best of course are summer fruits but fall apples and pears work well too! Just make sure you don’t fill with anything too juicy or loose. Add some flour to runny fruits to prevent a messy oven or soggy pastry.
Instructions: Combine flour, sugar and salt in large bowl. Cut the butter into ½” pieces. Add ½ the butter to the dry ingredients, and using your hands, work in the butter until the bits of butter and flour have the texture of oatmeal. Then work in the balance of the butter until the larges pieces are like medium sized beans. These pieces of butter will help the dough be flaky so don’t overwork.

Drizzle in ice water a small amount at a time, about ¼ cup at first mixing with a fork until well blended. Then keep adding water, usually about another ¼ cup until the dough is shaggy but not entirely wet. Gather the dough into two balls and wrap in plastic wrap and flatten into disks. Let rest in the fridge for two to three hours or as long as overnight.
Roll out to about a 14” circle and use right away or refrigerate for about 30 minutes. You can freeze overnight but use the next day and no later.
To bake, heat oven to 400. Butter or line a baking sheet with parchment and lay the dough on the sheet.
Peach – about 2 Tbsp. Sugar plus 1 tsp. and pinch of salt, about 1-2 Tbsp. melted butter

Combine flour, sugar and salt in large bowl. Cut the peaches into ¼” slices and toss with the dry ingredients. If the peaches are very ripe and juicy, add 1 Tbsp. flour as well. Arrange in concentric circles over the dough, leaving a 2” border. Fold dough over the edge of the fruit and crimp. Brush rim with butter and sprinkle with sugar.

Bake for 45 mins. in the bottom 1/3rd of the oven until golden all over and fruit is juicy and bubbly. You can glaze the fruit with a little jam if you want but it isn’t necessary. Let cool about 20 mins before cutting and serving. Great with ice cream.
This is best served right away.

Title: Greek Yogurt Ice Cream
Description: This recipe can be made with all kinds of fruit – strawberries, peaches, plums, and other berries. If the fruit is not very sweet like at the height of summer, you might want to adjust the sugar up a bit.

Ingredients.Name: Rinsed, hulled or pitted, and sliced into small pieces.

Instructions: Toss the fruit in a bowl with the sugar and vodka or kirsch (if using) until the sugar begins to dissolve. Cover with plastic wrap and let stand at room temperature for 2 hours, stirring every so often.

Transfer the fruit and their juice to a blender or food processor. Add the yogurt and fresh lemon juice. Pulse the machine until the mixture is smooth. If you wish, press mixture through a mesh strainer to remove any seeds if applicable.
Chill for 1 hour, then freeze in your ice cream maker according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Title: Milk Gelato
Instructions: Bring cream and 2 cups of the milk to a simmer in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Meanwhile, dissolve sugar and cornstarch in the remaining milk in a small bowl.

Remove pan from heat and stir in milk–cornstarch mixture. Return pan to medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil and thickens slightly, about 10 minutes. Stir in preserves, strain into a bowl, and set aside to cool. Cover and refrigerate until well chilled, 2–3 hours.
Process mixture in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer's directions.

Title: Chocolate Gelato
Instructions: Bring 2 cups of the milk to a simmer in a medium saucepan over medium heat, then remove from heat. Combine remaining 1 cup milk, sugar, cornstarch, and cocoa in a bowl, add to hot milk, and cook until sugar and cocoa dissolve.
Set aside to let cool, then cover and refrigerate overnight. Process mixture in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer's directions.

Title: Torta di Mandorla
Description: This is from Gina La Palma, Babbo’s pastry chef.
Instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a 9-inch round cake pan or springform pan and set aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, almond flour, baking powder and salt to thoroughly combine them and set aside.

Crack the eggs into a large mixing bowl and whisk them lightly to break up the yolks. Add the sugar to the bowl and whisk it in thoroughly in both directions for about 30 seconds. Add the olive oil and whisk until the mixture is a bit lighter in color and has thickened slightly, about 45 seconds. Whisk in the extracts and zest, followed by the orange juice.
Add the dry ingredients to the bowl and whisk until they are thoroughly combined; continue whisking until you have a smooth, emulsified batter, about 30 more seconds.

Pour the batter into the prepared pan, and bake the cake for 30 to 45 minutes, rotating the cake pan halfway through the cooking time to ensure even browning. The cake is done when it has begun to pull away from the sides of the pan, springs back lightly when touched, and a cake tester inserted in the center comes out clean.
Allow the cake to cool for ten minutes in the pan, then gently remove it from the pan and allow it cool completely on a rack.

While the cake cools, make the glaze. Melt the butter over medium heat in a small, heavy saucepan. When the bubbles subside, lower the heat and watch the butter carefully, swirling it in the pan occasionally to distribute the heat. When the butter begins to turn a light tan color and smells slightly nutty, turn off the heat and let the butter sit. It will continue to darken as it sits.

While the butter cools, sift the confectioner's sugar into a medium bowl. Whisk in the milk until completely smooth but thick, then slowly whisk in the butter. Taste the glaze and add a few drops of lemon juice to balance the sweetness. Stir in the toasted almonds. Spread the almonds and glaze onto the top and sides of the cake and let it sit until set and dry.

Title: Pumpkin Bread
Instructions: Preheat oven to 350.
Sift dry ingredients.

In a large bowl, beat eggs with sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in applesauce, then the oil. Lower speed and add the pumpkin and blend well. Beating slowly, add the dry ingredients until just blended. Stir in the chopped prunes.
Butter 2 small or 1 large loaf pan and then flour well.
Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour or until a tester comes out clean. Cool on rack for 5 minutes and then turn out of pan to cool further on rack. Let it cool til just warm before slicing.

Title: Apple & Panettone Pudding
Description: Because the panettone has so many eggs, it makes a lighter bread pudding.

Ingredients.Name: Panettone or brioche loaf, sliced 1 inch thick

Instructions: Butter a 9” x 13” ceramic or glass baking pan. Preheat oven to 350°F.

Warm 1 Tbsp. brandy or or Calvados with ¼ Cup water and soak currents for about 10- 15 minutes, until plumped, then drain. Butter panettone lightly and toast in an oven until golden brown on both sides. Whisk together remaining ingredients in medium bowl. Cut or tear panettone into bite-size pieces and spread evenly in baking dish. Melt remaining butter (about 2-3 Tbsp.) in medium skillet and toss in apples, cook over medium heat until they release some juices. Add the sugar and cook a couple minutes until syrupy and apples are tender. Toss with the ¼ Cup brandy/calvados and cook for about a minute or two until hot and syrupy. Scatter apples over bread and toss, then scatter the currants over top, then pour in egg mixture. Let stand 20-30 minutes until almost entirely absorbed.
Bake in the middle of the oven until pudding is golden and just set, 35 to 40 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature with whipped cream (optional).
Bread pudding can be made 2 days ahead and chilled. Reheat before serving.

Title: Cranberry Pear Gelee
Instructions: Rinse pan and shake out the water but don’t dry it. Line the pan with plastic wrap, pressing it well into the corners. The water helps it stick.

Core and cut pears into ½” pieces. Do not peel. Bring pears, cranberries, water and 2 ½ cups sugar, and butter to boil over medium high heat in a large heavy pot (4-6 Qts.). Reduce heat so the mixture simmers and stir occasionally until the cranberries pop and pears are tender, about 10 minutes. Transfer mixture to food processor and process to a puree. Be very careful with the hot mixture. Strain through a fine mesh sieve, pressing on all the solids. Put the mixture back in the pot. Meanwhile, place a small plate in the freezer to chill. Put the pot back on the heat and bring to a boil. Add pectin and reduce heat until it simmers. Stir well until the mixture becomes very thick and forms a paste. This takes 30-45 minutes.

To test for doneness, drop a teaspoon onto the cool plate and return to freezer for 1 minute. Take plate out and tilt. Mixture should retain its shape, rounded mass, and not run. Return to pot and cook for a few more minutes and test again.

When done, pour mixture into prepared pan. Gently tap the sides to settle the mixture, smooth top. Cool at room temp for at least one hour. Cover with plastic right on top of the mixture and chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours and up to one week.

To serve, cut into 1” squares using a very sharp thin knife. Rinse knife in hot water periodically to prevent sticking. Right before serving, pour remaining sugar into a dish or plate and gently coat all the squares and transfer to a serving platter.

Title: Blackberry Gelee

Ingredients.Name: *make sure the seeds are strained out
Note: Most people prefer substituting pectin – about 2 3-oz packets LIQUID per recipe seems to work

Instructions: Lightly oil baking pan.

Sprinkle gelatin over water in a 2-quart heavy saucepan and let stand 4 minutes to soften. Heat gelatin over medium-low heat, stirring, until dissolved. Stir in 2 cups sugar until dissolved, then stir in lemon juice.

Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, washing any sugar crystals down side of pan with a pastry brush dipped in cold water. Reduce heat to medium-low and boil, uncovered, without stirring, 13 minutes (watch carefully so that mixture does not boil over). Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes for bubbles to dissipate. (Skim any foam that remains after 5 minutes.) Stir in passion-fruit purée (do not scrape bottom of pan; leave any dark bits that stick). Pour into baking pan and let stand at room temperature until set, at least 12 hours.

Run a sharp knife around edge of gelatin and invert onto a cutting board. Cut into 1/2-inch-wide strips, then cut strips into 1-inch pieces. Just before serving, gently toss gelées in a bowl of sugar to coat, brushing off excess.

Title: Passion Fruit Gelee
Description: You can substitute any fruit puree – just be sure to cook down fruits like pineapple and kiwi into a jammy mixture first or it will not set
Instructions: In a small, nonreactive saucepan, stir together the passion fruit concentrate and sugar. Add the sugar by tablespoonfuls until the sweet/tart balance reaches your preference. Whisk in the gelatin until well mixed and set aside to soften for 2 minutes.
Prepare an ice water bath by emptying a tray of ice cubes into a pan of cold water.
Line a 9-by-12-inch baking pan or baking sheet with plastic wrap. Place the saucepan with the passion fruit mixture over low heat and whisk gently while the mixture comes to a boil, about 4 minutes.
Move the saucepan off the heat and hold it in the ice water bath. Whisk until the mixture has cooled to about room temperature. Skim off any remaining foam with a shallow spoon.
Pour the gelee onto the prepared baking pan and tilt and smooth the mixture into an even layer. Refrigerate until set, about an hour.

Title: Morbidezze al Cioccolato
Description: This is a classic soft centered chocolate cake/pudding. Follow the timing exactly.

Ingredients.Name: European style sweet butter at room temp

Instructions: Preheat 425* oven.
Butter six 1/2 Cup ramekins or other small baking dishes.

Break chocolate into pieces and melt over warm water or in microwave. When completely melted and warm, add the soft butter in small pieces, blending with a whisk. Separate yolks and whites in medium bowls. Add sugar to the yolks and whip with an electric beater until it is very fluffy and white. While continuing to beat, add the sifted flour and cocoa. Add the butter and chocolate mixture.

With a clean whisk or beater, whip the egg whites until they form peaks and fold gently into the chocolate mixture. Divide among baking dishes and bake for 8 minutes. Remove from oven and wait 2 minutes exactly before unmolding onto dessert plates. Serve immediately with custard sauce, vanilla ice cream or a little lightly sweetened cream. Garnish with fresh berries.

Title: Blood Orange Syrup
Description: This can be made with many things – plain oranges, Meyer lemons, limes, etc. It can be used to drizzle over yogurt, cake, or even roasted meats for a nice glaze. It is sweet so a little goes a long way.

Ingredients.Name: Muscat wine or other sweet preferably orange scented wine

Instructions: Place the orange juice and sugar into a small sauté pan and heat over medium high heat until it begins to boil and stir the sugar until dissolved. Turn down to a strong simmer and add the zest and wine. Let bubble until the alcohol is cooked off about 1-2 minutes, then turn down to a mild simmer. Let simmer about 20 minutes until the mixture thickens and has reduced until about ¾ cup remain. Remove from heat and cool.
Drizzle over cake, ice cream, etc.

Title: Blood Orange Olive Oil Cake
Description: This is a variation on the Meyer Lemon Cake but more unusual flavor.

Ingredients.Name: Granulated sugar – a little extra for pan
Extra virgin olive oil plus a little for the pan

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350*
Prepare a spring form pan with a thin coat of olive oil and a dusting of granulated sugar.

In a large bowl blend the cake flour, baking soda, salt and ½ cup sugar. In another bowl, mix the egg yolks, yogurt, olive oil and vanilla until incorporated. In a standing mixer or with a hand mixer, begin blending on med-low, the dry ingredients and adding the wet ingredients slowly until incorporated and you don’t see any dry areas. Zest the 4 oranges and add all the zest to the cake mixture. Juice one of the oranges and add 4 Tbsp. of juice to the batter. Mix until all is incorporated.

In a clean bowl with clean beaters, beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Add the ¼ cup sugar and beat until very stiff peaks form and the mixture is very glossy. Incorporate ½ the cake batter into the egg whites using a large whisk. Then repeat with the remaining batter, scraping down the sides to make sure you get all the zest.
Pour into prepared pan and bake in the center of the oven for 45-50 minutes or until a tester comes out clean. Cool on rack for 15 minutes and then remove from pan. Let cool and serve.
You can serve this with many things – whipped cream, ice cream, etc. but I like to serve it with a dollop of the unsweetened yogurt and a drizzle of orange flavored syrup.

Title: Fig Jam Tart with Thyme

Ingredients.Name: very ripe black Mission figs (1lb, 9 ounces)
unsalted butter, chilled but not hard-cold

Instructions: Prepare the short crust: In a bowl, mix the four, sugar, salt, and lemon peel. Cut the butter into 1/2-inch slices and work it into the flour mixture with your hands, until it is mostly incorporated in cornmeal-size pieces and the mixture just begins to hold together. Avoid overworking the mixture. Combine the water and vanilla and work it into the flour and butter mixture until the pastry is just blended and will hold together if you press it. Gather into a ball, divide it in half, wrap it in plastic, and allow it to rest for 30 minutes. Half the pastry will be used to line the tart pan, the other half to form the latticework top. Press half the pastry into a 9-inch tart pan, making sure that it is of an even thickness over the bottom and sides. Prick the bottom of the tart with a fork. Before baking the tart shell, set it in the freezer, wrapped in foil, for 30 minutes or overnight. Bake, unwrapped, in a preheated 375F oven for 25 minutes, or until the shell is a light golden brown and baked all the way through. Cool on a rack.

Prepare the fig jam: Trim the tips off the figs, cut the figs into small pieces, and put them in a saucepan. Add the thyme. Cook over medium heat until the figs are hot and begin to boil. Reduce the heat to low and cook for approximately 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, to prevent the figs from burning. As they cook, the figs will first appear watery, and then, as they reduce, the mixture will begin to thicken. The jam is finished when it is a dark purple color and very thick. Set aside to cool.

Assemble the tart: Roll the remaining short crust dough into a circle approximately 10 inches in diameter and 1/8 inch thick. Put it on a baking tray and let it rest in the refrigerator for 10 minutes. Fill the prebaked tart shell with the fig jam, spreading it evenly. Remove the rolled dough from the refrigerator and let warm slightly, for a minute or so. Using a knife, cut the dough into 1/4-inch-wide strips for the lattice top. Arrange the strips on top of the jam in the following way: Place one strip vertically on the tart shell about 1 inch from the left side. Then place one strip diagonally across the tart at a 45-degree angle to the vertical and diagonal strips, maintaining 1- inch spaces between. It should take 12 strips in all. Be sure the strips are evenly spaced. Trim the ends of the strips so they touch the edge of the tart shell. Where the strips touch the shell, brush with a dab of water and press each strip gently onto the edge of a shell. Preheat the oven to 375F. Beat the egg yolk with the cream. Brush the egg wash carefully onto the lattice strips. Bake the tart at 375F for approximately 45 minutes, until the pastry is cooked. Cool on a rack. Serve by itself, or with unsweetened mascarpone.

Title: Panforte (Chocolate)
Description: Dense rich "cake" almost a confection of fruit and nuts. Plan ahead so this can mellow its flavors.

Ingredients.Name: Dutch process cocoa plus a little more for dusting
Whole hazelnuts, toasted and skins rubbed off in a kitchen towel
Soft dried figs, cut into 6 sections each

Instructions: Preheat oven to 300 degrees.
Line a 9 inch spring form pan with parchment, on the sides and bottom, using a round for the bottom and strips for side.
Butter the paper well and dust with cocoa powder, knocking out excess.
Whisk together flour, spices salt and cocoa in a large bowl. Stir in fruit and nuts and chocolate chips.

In a 2 quart saucepan, over moderate heat, stir together sugar and honey until it reaches 238-240degrees without stirring, about 2 minutes. Immediately pour mixture over fruit and nut mixture and stir quickly - it will be thick and sticky.
Immediately pour into pan and press down to make it even. Dampen fingers to keep from sticking.
Bake in the middle of the over for 50-55 minutes until edges become matte and begin to rise slightly.
Cool on a rack completely and then remove from pan and from paper.

NOTE - the flavors develop with time so it is best to make this about one week before serving and seal in a plastic back. Chill and then bring to room temp before serving. Cake will keep for a month if chilled.

Title: Apple Crisp
Description: This is my version of a classic. I use fewer apples when it is just the three of us and save 1/2 the topping for another day. It keeps well in the fridge for a week.

Ingredients.Name: Granny Smith, Pippin or other tart cooking apples, cut into 1/4" slices or cubes 1/2" sq.
Almonds (I use whole ones but you can use just about any type you have on hand

Instructions: Pre-heat oven to 375 degrees.

Mix cut up apples with lemon juice, sugar and cinnamon and place into a large deep baking dish, such as a soufflé baker. You can also use a deep gratin dish but the ratio of fruit to topping will be different. Pack the apples into the dish and even the top.

In the bowl of a food processor, put the brown sugar, flour and almonds and pinch of salt. Process for a few seconds to chop almonds into large pieces. add butter in chunks and process until almonds are chopped and the butter incorporated so that the whole thing looks like chunky meal. Add the oatmeal and process a few more pulses so that it is chopped but not fine.
Press handfuls of the mixture onto the top of the baking dish with apples and cover apples completely so no holes are apparent. This prevents juices from making the topping soggy.
Bake for 35-45 minutes until topping is golden and the apples juicy and fragrant. Do not let the topping get too brown.
Let rest about 10 minutes.
Serve hot, warm or at room temp - it is good all ways.

Title: Walnut Tart w/ Chocolate Lace
Description: This is a crowd pleaser. Small pieces go a long way.

Ingredients.Name: Short crust tart shell. rested in refrig for 1 hour, and pre-baked for about 15-20 min until golden

Instructions: Preheat oven to 400*

Scald cream in pot over medium high heat. In another saucepan, combine sugar and water and cook over low heat until dissolved, raise heat to medium high and continue to cook until caramelized light golden brown. Remove from heat and gradually whisk in hot cream. Be very careful as the mixture can foam up. Place back on med-high heat for about 3 minutes. Cool 15 minutes. Coarsely chop walnuts and toast gently til fragrant.
Stir in vanilla. Whisk eggs and then add to cooled caramel mixture with butter. Stir in walnuts.
Pour mixture into tart and bake at 400* for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 375* and continue to cook approx. 15 minutes. Cool on rack for 30 minutes.
Melt chocolate over warm water or in microwave. Drizzle all over to create a detailed lacy pattern.

Title: Butternut Squash Tart
Instructions: 400* Preheat
Cut squash and remove seeds. Place on parchment lined baking sheet, cut side down. Roast approx. 45 minutes or until very tender.
Remove skin from 1/2 squash. Reserve other half for another use.
Raise heat to 425*

In the bowl of a food processor, place the squash and the buttermilk and process until smooth. Add the 1/3 Cup sugar and the spices and process again. Taste and adjust seasoning, adding the extra sugar if necessary. Process in the eggs and pour into the shell. Place in center of oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 and continue another 15 minutes or until the center is firm to the touch.
Cool and serve at room temp.

Title: Panna Cotta
Description: Use 8 - 1/2 C ramekins or I use small coffee cups. In the winter, I like to garnish this with mandarin oranges. In the summer, blackberries are outstanding.
Instructions: Butter ramekins and place on a tray.
In a large cup or small bowl, place 1/4 Cup milk. Sprinkle the gelatin over the milk and stir gently. Let rest for 2-3 minutes or until the gelatin completely absorbs the milk.

In a saucepan, stir the remaining milk with the cream and the sugar. Place over moderate heat and whisk to dissolve the heat while bringing the mixture to a boil. As soon as it boils, remove from the heat, whisk in the gelatin/milk mixture and the vanilla. Strain through a fine sieve into a large measuring cup with spout. Gently pour the mixture among the ramekins. Cover the entire tray with plastic and refrigerate until set, at least 4 hours. It can be prepared one day in advance.

To serve, run a sharp knife around the edge of each ramekin to loosen the panna cotta. Dip the bottom of the ramekin into a small bowl of hot water and twist gently to loosen the cotta further. Invert onto chilled or cool plates and garnish with fresh fruit.
* Many recipes use whole milk for a creamier consistency. We like the lightness of this but if you prefer the richness, try it.
VARIATION: Many traditional panna cottas are flavored with almond. To do that, reduce the vanilla to 1 tsp and add 1/4 to 1/2 tsp of almond extract depending on your preference.

Title: Pear Soufflé
Description: For a really decadent treat, add brandy to the custard sauce or shave dark chocolate over the hot soufflé.

Ingredients.Name: Pear Sauce, warm or room temperature
Granulated sugar, plus some for the pan
Cream Anglais or other custard sauce

Instructions: Preheat oven to 400* and position rack at the bottom of the oven.

Generously butter a 6-cup soufflé dish, 7 1/2" diameter. Sprinkle with sugar and tap out excess. Make a collar by folding aluminum foil lengthwise in half. Butter one side of foil and wrap around the dish, buttered side in so that collar extends about 3-4 inches above the rim of the dish. Tie foil in place with string.

Beat egg yolks with 2 Tbsp. of the sugar until they are light in color and forms a ribbon when beater is lifted. This takes approximately 10 minutes. Stir in pear sauce, vanilla, lemon zest and nutmeg.

Beat egg whites in another bowl with a pinch of salt and a pinch of cream of tarter until soft peaks form. slowly beat in remaining sugar and continue beating until they hold stiff peaks. Fold 1/3 of the egg whites into the yolks to lighten them and then fold in the rest of the whites.
Gently put mixture in soufflé dish.
Bake on lowest rack for 15-20 minutes, longer time for a stiffer center. Carefully remove collar and serve immediately. Gently pour light cream anglais or other custard sauce around the soufflé.

Title: Pear Sauce

Ingredients.Name: Large Comice pears, pealed, cored and sliced

Instructions: Place pears in a non-reactive saucepan, large enough to hold them easily. Sprinkle and toss with the lemon juice. Place pan on medium heat and cook, stirring consistently until the juices begin to exude from the fruit. Stir in the sugar and cook, stirring and mashing the fruit, until the sauce is the consistency of applesauce. Serve warm with ice cream or chill and reserve for another use.

Title: Summer Fruit "Slump"
Description: This is like a cobbler but with a less stiff dough that melds into the fruit a little more. It's easy and great with just about any fruit, particularly ripe blackberries. Adjust sugar to sweetness of fruit

Ingredients.Name: Fresh ripe blackberries, blueberries or other summer fruits
Sugar (less if using blueberries and even less if using really sweet fruits like peaches)
Non-fat milk or low-fat buttermilk for a tangy taste

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375*

Put cleaned and drained berries or other fruit in a 6 Cup gratin dish or other baking dish (ceramic or glass). Sprinkle evenly with 3/4 Cup sugar. Sift together dry ingredients and 1/4 C sugar. Add milk and butter and whisk until just incorporated and almost smooth. Pour evenly over berries but don't worry if they aren't covered completely. Bake in middle of oven for 40 minutes until crust is light golden brown. Transfer to rack and cool for 10 minutes or longer. Best served warm but o.k. at room temperature. Don't hold too long. Serve with a little vanilla ice cream if you like.

Title: Miniature Florentines
Instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Boil sugar, butter, honey, and cream in a 1-quart heavy saucepan over moderate heat, stirring constantly, until creamy and slightly thickened, about 5 min. Remove from heat and stir in almonds and flour. Drop level 1/2 teaspoons of batter about 2 inches apart on parchment-lined baking sheets. Bake in batches in middle of oven until golden brown and bubbly, 8 to 10 min. Cool cookies on sheets on racks until firm enough to be lifted, about 2 min. then transfer with a metal spatula to racks to cool completely . Melt chocolate in a double boiler, stirring occasionally, then remove top of double boiler from heat. Dip about one third of each cookie into chocolate, and then transfer to a parchment-lined tray. Let stand until chocolate is set, about 1 hour.

Title: Ginger Crackles
Description: This are outstanding, last a long time, and everyone loves them.
Instructions: heat the oven to 350 degrees F. In a large bowl, combine the flour, ginger, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. In another large bowl, beat the butter, shortening, and 1 cup of the sugar with a mixer or a wooden spoon until well combined. Add the egg and molasses to the butter mixture; beat well. Add the dry ingredients and mix until well blended, scraping down the bowl often (set a mixer on low speed). Shape the dough into 1-inch balls. Roll each in the remaining sugar. Put the balls 2 inches apart on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake until the cookies are lightly browned around the edges and puffed, about 13 min. Let the cookies sit for 5 min. and then transfer them to a rack to cool completely.

Title: Double Chocolate Chews
Description: Keep for 1 week
Instructions: In a medium mixing bowl, stir together flour, baking powder, and salt and set aside. Combine oil and chocolate in a medium sized heavy saucepan and warm over lowest heat, stirring occasionally, until chocolate melts. Remove saucepan from heat and stir in sugar using a large wooden spoon. Add eggs, one at a time, and stir until well blended. Stir in vanilla and almond extracts.

Pour chocolate mixture into dry ingredients and stir until very thoroughly mixed. Add chocolate chips and stir until evenly distributed. Cover dough and refrigerate for at least 1 1/2 hours or up to 48 hours, if desired. If refrigerated for more than 2 hours, let dough warm and soften slightly before shaping and baking.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease several baking sheets and set aside.
Roll chilled dough between palms to form 1 1/4 inch diameter balls. Space them about 2 inches apart on greased baking sheets.

Place in upper third of the oven and bake for 11 to 13 minutes or until just beginning to firm in the center. Reverse baking sheets from front to back halfway through baking to ensure even cooking. Remove from oven and let stand for 1 minute, and then transfer cookies to wire racks to cool. Lightly dust cookies with powdered sugar shortly before serving.

Title: Cornmeal Cake w/ Rosemary Syrup
Description: This is a lighter cake than the Italian Cornmeal Cake with a hint of almond. Serve this with sweet summer peaches dressed in the rosemary syrup. Other summer fruits will work well also, particularly apricots and blackberries.

Ingredients.Name: Small summer peaches, very ripe and sweet

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350*
Butter and flour a 9" round cake pan.

In a large bowl, combine the butter and sugar. Beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Add remaining dry ingredients, eggs, and milk and combine well. Beat on high until light and fluffy. Pour into prepared pan and bake for approximately 40 minutes in the center of the oven until lightly golden and until a tester comes out clean (little granules of cornmeal is o.k.).

While cake bakes, make syrup by blending sugar and water in a sauce pan on high heat. When it begins to boil, add the rosemary and simmer for approximately 10 minutes until the syrup begins to thicken a bit. Add lemon juice and vanilla. Cool for 10 minutes and strain.

When cake comes out of oven, cool 10 minutes. Invert onto a plate with top up. Using a pastry brush, brush the top of the cake with the syrup. Let soak in and continue adding syrup being careful not to disturb the tender top crust. Continue until approx. 1/3 Cup of syrup has soaked in.
