Slice peaches and toss with about 1/4 cup of the syrup. Serve remaining syrup with the cake, peaches and whipped cream if desired.

Title: Meyer Lemon Olive Oil Cake
Description: This is a delicate light sponge cake with a fresh taste.

Ingredients.Name: Light Olive Oil plus a little extra for the pan
Granulated Sugar plus a little extra for the pan

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350*
Prepare a spring form 9" pan with a thin coat of olive oil and a dusting of granulated sugar.
In a large bowl blend the cake flour, baking soda, salt and 1/2 Cup of sugar.
In another bowl, blend the buttermilk, olive oil, vanilla & almond extracts and the egg yolks.
With a hand electric mixer or in a standing mixer, beat the dry ingredients on low to medium while slowly adding the liquid ingredients. Stop when just blended and no dry spots remain.
Grate the zest from the three lemons and squeeze one of the lemons.
Add all the zest to the cake mixture and 2 Tbsp. of the juice. Beat on medium until well blended and no lumps remain.

In a clean bowl with cleaned beaters, beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Slowly add the remaining 1/4 Cup sugar and beat until very stiff peaks form and the whites are glossy with no sugar visible.

Using a large whisk, pour 1/2 the cake batter into the whites and blend until incorporated. Add the remaining and whisk again until incorporated. Pour into cake pan and bake for 45-50 minutes until a tester comes out clean. Cool on a rack for 10 minutes and remove from pan. Let cool and serve.

Title: Summer Buttermilk Ice 1
Description: This is very versatile - you can use almost any kind of fruit.

Ingredients.Name: Ripe, flavorful fruit puree - Peaches, Nectarines and strawberries are particularly good

Instructions: Blend sugar and buttermilk in large bowl. Keep very cold. Stir in cold fruit puree and scrape the vanilla bean into mixture. Stir in salt. Process in Donvier or other ice cream maker. Freeze until firm - at least 2 hours before serving. This melts quickly so serve immediately.
This recipe doubles easily to make a quart.
Variation: Lime Ice: Substitute 1/4 C. fresh lime juice and 1 tsp zest for fruit. Omit vanilla.

Title: Queen of Nuts Cake
Description: Make this cake one day ahead if possible. It gets better after 12-24 hours. It keeps for several days. For special occasions, dress the cake with whipped cream or even some fruit compote.

Ingredients.Name: Mixed shelled whole nuts (almonds, walnuts & pecans or any combination of these)
Large eggs, separated, at room temperature

Instructions: Preheat Oven to 350. Butter a 9" round cake pan, line the bottom with a round of parchment, and sprinkle sides evenly with the bread crumbs.
In a food processor, chop the nuts fine. In a bowl, mix the nuts with the sugar, chocolate, vanilla and beat in the egg yolks well. The mixture will be dense and hard to turn.

In a clean bowl, whip the egg whites until they are smooth and shiny, being careful not to over beat them. You don't want them dry. Stir a few spoonfuls of the egg whites into the chocolate-nut mixture to lighten it and fold the nut mixture into the whites.

Pour batter into prepared cake pan and bake in preheated oven for 35-40 minutes or until the top is firm to the touch. Let cake cool in the pan on a rack for 15 minutes. Remove from pan and cool completely on rack. Cover until an hour or two before serving. Dust with confectioner's sugar.

Title: Gingerbread Cake
Description: Great classic gingerbread!!
Instructions: Pre-heat oven 350*
Butter 8" cake pan.

Sift flour, baking soda, spices and salt together in large bowl. In the bowl of an electric mixer, cream room temperature butter until light and fluffy. Add sugar and beat again until light and fully incorporated. Scrape down bowl several times to ensure even distribution. Add egg and beat until well blended. Add molasses in steady stream while mixer is beating. Stop now and then and scrape down sides. Add 1/3 dry ingredients and mix well, add 1/3 dry ingredients and mix well and then add the final dry ingredients. Scrape sides and slowly add water while blending and blend until well incorporated.

Pour batter in pan and place in oven immediately. Do not mix the cake in advance of cooking or it will not rise properly. Bake 35-40 minutes until tester comes out clean. Sprinkle with confectioner’s sugar. Garnish with whipped cream or lemon syrup.

Title: Ultimate Pear Tart
Description: The pastry is very tender and rich and is a perfect backdrop for the pears

Ingredients.Name: Large Comice Pears - ripe but not soft
Unsweetened butter , very cold, cut in pieces

Instructions: Make pastry: In the bowl of a food processor, chop almonds fine. If they get sticky, add a few tablespoons of the flour and continue to chop. Add balance of flour, c. sugar, scraped vanilla bean seeds and process until well blended. Add egg yolk and process until it just begins to form ball. Line tart pan (9") with parchment and press the dough into the bottom and sides of the pan, working quickly, using flour to keep your hands from sticking. If the weather is warm, you may need to stop and chill the pastry before continuing. When done, cover with plastic wrap and chill in refrigerator for at least one hour.
When pastry is ready, preheat oven to 375*. Pre-bake empty shell for about 12 minutes until lightly golden. Cool.

Slice 3 pears into nice even slices and arrange in the concentric circles, using the smaller pieces for the middle. Sprinkle with a teaspoon of the sugar, and bake for about 30 minutes until pastry is golden and fruit is tender. Glaze with a little melted butter, if you wish or with some melted fruit jelly or even honey while still hot.
Make Pear Caramel Sauce:

While tart is cooking, chop up one-half (1/2) pear into small pieces and put in saucepan with a little water (2-3Tbsp.) and heat on medium. Cook pears until tender, adding more water to keep them from sticking or browning. Try to keep several Tbsp. of liquid in the pan at all times. When done, transfer pears with a slotted spoon to the food processor and puree. Add sugar to the liquid and let it dissolve. Add a little more water if you need it. Heat sugar on medium high heat until it begins to caramelize and turn golden. Remove from heat and carefully pour in cream. It will lump up. Return to heat and stir continuously until it remelts and it is a smooth caramel. Add the pear puree - it may lump again, but keep cooking and stirring until it is reabsorbed - there will be some lumps from the pears. Remove from heat.
Serve tart slices drizzled with crème anglais and the pear caramel sauce.

Title: Rhubarb Crisp
Description: This topping works well with a lot of fruit – peaches, berries, etc. Just reduce the sugar that’s tossed with the fruit if you use a sweeter fruit like peaches or blueberries.
Instructions: Preheat Oven 350 degrees.
Clean rhubarb and slice into ½ inch slices. In a large bowl, toss the rhubarb with flour and sugar.
In the bowl of a food processor, process the flour, almonds, brown sugar and butter until almonds are well chopped. Toss in the oatmeal and pulse briefly.

If working without a processor, you’ll need the butter to be room temperature then chop the almonds first and blend the ingredients together, breaking up the butter with your fingers until it is well incorporated into pea sized bits.

Put the rhubarb in a deep lasagna pan, press it down, and then sprinkle the topping over it as evenly as possible. Place it into the oven and bake for 30-40 minutes until the rhubarb is bubbling around the edges and the top is getting golden.

If you want to make a smaller amount, cut the rhubarb to 1 lb, and cut the sugar and flour in half. Use only ½ the topping and save the other half for another time. It keeps easily for a few weeks in the fridge if it is well sealed.

Title: Peach/Nectarine Upside Down Cake
Description: This can be made with most any fruit – although best if it has some acidity. Make this with tart apples, cranberries (add more sugar) or a mix of fruits!

Ingredients.Name: Peaches or nectarines, sliced approx. 1/4" thick

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350*

In a large bowl, cream 6 Tbsp. of the butter with 1/2 Cup of the sugar. Beat until light and fluffy. Add egg and continue to beat until incorporated and fluffy. In another medium bowl, sift dry ingredients.
Add flour mixture to the butter in small amounts (1/3 mixture each time), alternating with milk. Beat until smooth and beat in vanilla and brandy.

In a 9" skillet, preferably heavy (like calphalon), melt the remaining 2 Tbsp. butter over moderate heat and sprinkle remaining sugar over the butter. Take off heat and lay fruit in decoratively, in a swirl around pan. Heat over medium heat for a few minutes just to warm fruit and release juices. Remove from heat and spoon batter over fruit. The batter can be a little thick so drop it by Tbsp. all around to get good coverage over the fruit.
Bake 30-40 minutes until a tester comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes and invert it. Some fruit may stick to the pan. That's o.k., just lift them gently off and patch the cake.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
Dollop with ice cream or whipped cream for an extravagant treat.

Title: Low Fat Chocolate Cake

Ingredients.Name: Optional – use 1 Cup cake flour and ¼ cup flax seed meal for a healthier richer cake.

Instructions: Preheat Oven to 350*
Oil a 9" cake pan and line with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, sift the flour with the cocoa and baking soda. In a small saucepan, combine the sugar, chocolate and 1/2 C. water. Cook over med. high heat until the sugar dissolves and the chocolate melts. The chocolate may not fully integrate and that is okay. Transfer to a large bowl and add the butter and stir until it dissolves. Add buttermilk and vanilla extract. Beat in the eggs and egg white and then the flour mixture until fully incorporated.

Pour into prepared cake pan and bake for approx. 35 minutes or until a tester comes out clean. Cool pan on rack and after 15 minutes, invert and put on platter. Continue cooling and dust with confectioners' sugar before serving.

Title: Rustic Plum Pie
Instructions: Make dough:

Cut butter into bits and in a bowl with a pastry blender or in a food processor blend or pulse together with, flour, sugar, and salt until mixture resembles coarse meal. Add 2 tablespoons ice water and toss or pulse until incorporated. Add enough remaining ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing with a fork or pulsing to incorporate, to form a dough. Gather dough into a ball. On a work surface smear dough with heel of hand in 3 or 4 forward motions to make dough easier to work with. Form dough into a ball and flatten into a disk. Chill dough, wrapped in plastic wrap, 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°F.
Make filling:
Halve and pit plums. Cut plums into 3/4-inch-thick wedges and in a bowl toss with sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice.

On a lightly floured surface with floured rolling pin roll out dough into an 11-inch round (about 1/8 inch thick). Transfer dough to a 9-inch (1-quart) glass pie plate. (Do not trim overhang.) Spoon filling into shell and fold edge of dough over filling, leaving center uncovered. Bake pie in middle of oven 35 minutes. Brush crust with milk and sprinkle with sugar. Bake pie 10 minutes more, or until filling is bubbling and crust is golden. Cool pie on a rack.

Title: Italian Cornmeal Cake - The Best
Description: This cake is a sunny buttery cake - great with fresh berries and softly whipped cream. For a special treat, add a fruit sauce to compliment the berries - I especially like rhubarb sauce with strawberries.

Ingredients.Name: Unsalted butter - softened at room temp

Instructions: Preheat oven to 325*.
Butter well a saddle of venison pan (the traditional shape) or an 8 1/2" x 4" loaf pan and line with parchment paper.

Combine flour, cornmeal and salt in a medium bowl. In a large bowl, beat the butter and sugar until very light and fluffy. Mix in the brandy and scrape in the seeds of the vanilla. (*Or, substitute vanilla extract and omit the brandy).
Add eggs, one at a time and beat well after each addition. Gradually add the dry ingredients and mix until just blended. Spoon batter into pan and smooth the top with a spatula until even.
Bake approx. 1 hour or until a tester comes out clean. Cool in pan on rack for 10 minutes and turn cake out onto rack. Cool the cake completely and wrap it very tightly in plastic wrap to keep fresh.
To serve, dust with confectioners' sugar, and present with fresh berries and softly whipped cream.

Title: Best Gingerbread

Ingredients.Name: 5 Tbs. butter, softened at room temp
Superfine sugar plus a little more if necessary depending on size and juiciness of lemon.

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Butter an 8 x 8 " cake pan or a 9" round pan.
Sift together the dry ingredients onto a piece of wax paper. Set aside.
In the bowl of a large mixer, beat the butter until light and creamy. Add the sugar and continue beating until light and fluffy.

Add the egg and continue until well combined. Scrape down the sides and pour in molasses slowly, beating all the while. Add half the dry ingredients and mix just until combined. Scrape down sides and add remaining dry ingredients. Slowly pour in cold water and stir until well incorporated.

Pour batter into prepared pan and bake until a skewer inserted in center comes out clean - about 35 to 40 minutes. Cool before removing from pan and serve with sweetened whipped cream and/or lemon glaze

Make glaze: Juice lemon and stir in superfine sugar. Stir to dissolve and heat gently in the microwave for 1 minute or in a small sauce pan until just slightly thickened and hot. Poke holes in top of cake with toothpick or small skewer and brush the glaze over the top with a pastry brush or small spoon, letting the glaze drip into holes. Glaze will also provide a nice sheen for the top. You can also add extra glaze to the whipped cream when you whip it instead of sugar.

Title: Joe’s Bubbly Rose
Description: This is an adjusted recipe – less sweet – than the Bubbly Rose.

Ingredients.Name: Simple Syrup or a little more if needed to taste
Tonic (200ml) Water or 14 oz. from larger btl.

Instructions: Combine gin, rose water, syrup and lemon juice in a pitcher large enough and chill. Chill tonic and Prosecco.
Right before serving, stir gin mixture and add the tonic and prosecco. Adjust sugar syrup to taste. Serve over ice.

Title: Jamaica Cooler
Description: This makes about 8 glasses of “tea.”
Instructions: Bring 1 ½ Qts. Water to a boil

Pour over the flowers and sugar in a large non-reactive bowl. Steep at room temp for one hour and not more than 2. Taste after one hour and if you want it sweeter, add more sugar. I like mine very tart so adjust it to your taste.
Cool completely, pour into a pitcher and refrigerate.
Serve with lime wedge in a tall glass with lots of ice.

Title: Market Shot (Fall)
Description: This is a Melissa Periello recipe

Ingredients.Name: Ripe Bartlett pears, washed, peel & quarter
White wine, dry, such as Sauvignon Blanc
White wine, dry, such as Sauvignon Blanc

Instructions: 1. For the pear puree combine white wine, vinegar, sugar, and water in a saucepot over medium-low heat. Bring to a simmer for 2 minutes, and then add the pears. Simmer over low heat until the pears are tender and almost translucent, 10-15 minutes. Be mindful to monitor the pears periodically.

2. When the pears are sufficiently poached, remove them from the stovetop. Allow the pears and syrup to cool to room temperature. Then blend all of the liquid and pear together using a blender or handheld immersion blender. Strain the puree through a fine mesh strainer and chill over an ice bath or overnight in your refrigerator.
3. To make the shots, add the wine, vermouth, and lemon juice. Stir well, chill for 30 minutes, and serve.

Title: Sazerac
Description: Thanks to Joe and John for introducing us to the Sazerac. This is for one large one (a double).
Instructions: Chill an old-fashioned glass by filling with crushed ice or refrigerate or freeze for at least 30 minutes.
Add the absinthe to the glass; swirl it around to coat the entire sides and bottom of the glass. Discard the excess.
In a cocktail shaker, add sugar syrup, rye whiskey, and bitters, stir and then add ice and stir well for about 30 seconds; strain into the prepared old-fashioned glass.

Title: Scofflaw
Description: Original from Harry’s Bar Paris, modified to our taste

Ingredients.Name: Grenadine, pomegranite grenadine, cherry syrup, or other thick syrupy red fruit such as Cassis

Instructions: Blend and stir, garnish with a twist

Title: Fogerty
Description: From Baretta Restaurant, SF, Ryan Fitzgerald
Instructions: PREPARATION:Add all the ingredients to a mixing glass and fill with ice. Stir, and strain into a chilled cocktail glass. Garnish with orange peel.

Title: Cucumber Ginger Martini
Instructions: In a small bowl, dissolve the sugar in the hot water. Press the grated ginger through a fine strainer set over the bowl, releasing the juice.

In a cocktail shaker, muddle the diced cucumber with the 2 torn basil leaves. Add the ginger syrup, gin, lime juice and a handful of ice. Shake well, then strain into a martini glass. Garnish the martini with the cucumber slice and the remaining whole basil leaf and serve.

Title: The Promissory Note
Description: From Daniel Hyatt, the Alembic Bar, San Francisco
Instructions: 1. Place all the ingredients with ice in a mixing glass and stir 30 times. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.2. Squeeze a lime zest over the top, then discard the zest. Sprinkle lightly with cinnamon. Garnish with a thin, round radish slice.

Title: Tangerine Kiss
Instructions: To make the lemon vodka: Place rind of Meyer lemon in litre of vodka for one week and then remove.
Tangerine Kiss for a Group
1 liter Campari
1 liter Meyer lemon (or other citrus-flavored) vodka
1 gallon tangerine juice.
Combine the three ingredients in a punch bowl, float some lemon and tangerine slices on top and serve. Ice ring is optional.

Title: Summer Mojitos
Instructions: Muddle the sugar with the rum in the bottom of the glasses. When they are fragrant and crushed, add the lime juice. Fill glass with ice and top off with a little bubbly water. Stir and serve with extra mint sprigs…

Title: Pomegranite Martinis – 2 ways

Ingredients.Name: POM (already sweetened so you don’t need anything further)
Sugar syrup – agave is good too
Fresh pomegranate seeds or lime zest for garnish

Instructions: Mix all ingredients in a shaker with lots of ice until icy cold. Serve in cold martini glasses with the garnishes.

Title: Orange Things from Birmingham

Ingredients.Name: Triple Sec or other orange flavored liquor

Instructions: Mix ingredients in a shaker with lots of ice until icy cold. Serve in martini glasses. Garnish with orange peel

Title: Agave Margarita
Instructions: Combine ingredients in shaker with lots of ice and shake until very cold. Serve in glasses dipped in crusty salt.

Title: Antica Martini
Description: The best!

Ingredients.Name: High Quality Vodka, such as Kettle One

Instructions: Combine in a shaker, add lots of ice and shake until icy cold. Pour into cold glasses and garnish with orange peel.

Title: Manhattan - original
Instructions: 2 oz. blended whiskey
1/4 - 1/2 oz. sweet vermouth
dash Angostura bitters

Title: Les' Margaritas

Ingredients.Name: Rose's Lime Juice or 4 oz Agave for a more pure taste which we prefer – add a little more lime if necessary

Instructions: mix until perfect
Drink as much as necessary

Title: Elderflower Martini
Instructions: Over ice, shake the vodka, liquor and fruit juice until very cold. Pour into cold glasses and garnish with a 2 inch thin strip of lime peel. Serve immediately.

Title: Herzog & de Meuron
Description: Same as the Antica Martini.
Instructions: Over ice, shake the vodka and vermouth until very cold. Pour into cold glasses. Trim some of the orange peel into long strips of orange (no pith) and rub about a 2inch long piece around the rim of each glass and twirl around your finger and drop into the glass. Serve immediately.

Title: Spanish Garbanzo Stew
Description: This serves 4 with some left over as a main side to grilled meats. It serves 6 easily if served along side other vegetables or starters. This is my re-working of a traditional Spanish tapa.

Ingredients.Name: Tomatoes, fresh, coarsely chopped or 1/3 cup canned drained
Garlic cloves, peeled and chopped fine
Sea salt and fresh ground pepper

Instructions: Heat 2 Tbsp. of the olive oil in a large deep skillet and saute the onion and tomatoes until the onions are translucent over medium heat. Add 2/3rd of the chopped garlic, and spices and saute til the garlic is translucent. Add about 1/3 cup of the bean water to mix the spices well into the vegetables. Add the drained beans, broth and sherry and cook for about 10 minutes. Add a little water to the mixture if needed to keep it slightly soupy. Add the vinegar and cook about 1 minute. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more sherry, vinegar and salt and pepper until the flavor is balanced. Turn off the heat and let rest for about 30 minutes to let the beans absorb the flavors. If the mixture is dry add a little more broth or bean water, it should be loose but not brothy.

When about ready to serve it, heat again til bubbly. The beans should be very moist with a thick sauce that coats them. Add a little more liquid if needed. Then heat a large skillet with 2 Tbsp. olive oil, and when hot, add the remaining garlic, toss til translucent and add the spinach, tossing well to coat the spinach in the oil until it just wilts. Season the spinach with salt and pepper.
In a large open bowl ring the bottom with the spinach, leaving a well in the center, and fill with the bean mixture. Serve immediately.

Title: Lentil Cheese Casserole
Description: This is both a good meatless meal main and a good side for roasted meats.
Instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.

Stir all ingredients together in a large soufflé dish or deep casserole. Bake for 1 and ½ hours to 2 hours until tender. Stir it a couple times during cooking. About 5 mins before taking out of the oven, cover the casserole with the grated cheese and let melt. Serve hot.

Title: Lentil Cheese Gratin

Ingredients.Name: Chopped fresh yellow or white onion
Chicken broth, homemade or low sodium, zero fat canned

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Combine the ingredients in a deep small gratin or soufflé dish.
Bake for 1 and ½ hours, stirring a couple of times. About 5 minutes before ready, sprinkle cheese on top and cook until fully melted.

Title: Twice Cooked Polenta
Description: This is great because it allows you to make the polenta in advance and then roast it shortly before you plan to serve it. I got this recipe from Zuni cookbook.
Instructions: Boil water, 1 tsp salt, and then add polenta in a thin stream, whisking constantly. Reduce heat so that polenta simmers very gently. Whisk regularly and cook until tender. For the coarse grain polenta, this could take up to one hour. For ordinary polenta, it takes about ½ hour and for regular corn meal, only about 5 minutes (but the texture will be lacking). Taste for salt and add some if needed. Add 1 Tbsp. sweet butter, swirling until incorporated.
Pour into a small sheet pan with sides, lined with parchment paper, and spread into an equal layer about 1 inch. Cool until firm.
Heat oven to 275 degrees.

Cut polenta into squares, rectangles or triangles. I like to use triangles about 2”x3” so they get really crispy. Brush with olive oil or melted butter and place on a cookie sheet well spaced apart. Roast for about 30 minutes until golden crispy.

Title: Spelt Risotto
Instructions: 1. Place the spelt in a large fine-mesh sieve and rinse it thoroughly under cold running water. Transfer it to a large bowl, cover with cold water, and soak for 2 hours. Rinse again, drain, and set aside.

2. In a large deep skillet, combine the oil, butter, onions, shallots, and a pinch of sea salt. Sweat--cook, covered, over low heat without coloring--until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the spelt, chicken stock, bay leaves, and 1 teaspoon sea salt. Bring to a boil over high heat; then reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook, uncovered, until tender, about 30 minutes, stirring from time to time to keep the grain from sticking to the pan.

3. While the spelt is cooking, whip the cream: In the bowl of a heavy-duty mixer fitted with the whisk (or with a handheld mixer), whip the cream at moderate speed until soft peaks form. Gradually increase the speed to high, whisking until stiff peaks form, Scrape down the sides of the bowl. Set aside.
4. When the spelt is cooked, place a large sieve over a large bowl and drain the spelt in the sieve, discarding the cooking liquid.
5. At serving time, return the cooked spelt to the skillet and saute over moderate heat to toast it lightly, 2 to 3 minutes. Add sea salt to taste. Stir in the whipped cream, and serve.

Title: Fresh Shell Beans
Description: Cranberry beans are delicate and earthy. Others are wonderful too - whatever is fresh will work. If the beans are bigger, increase the simmer time.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh shelled cranberry beans (picked over also)
Carrot, peeled and cut into 6 or 8 pieces

Instructions: Place beans in 2 1/2 Qt. heavy pot with lid. Add water, 2 Tbsp. of the oil, half the thyme, and remaining ingredients, except fennel, if using. Cut fennel tops off, leaving just the bulb. Trim root end and cut into half. Save one half for another use. Cut one half into half again and add quarters to pot. Bring to gentle boil and reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes. Taste and the beans should be tender on the outside and just a little too firm on the inside. Add the salt and continue cooking for another 10 minutes or until the beans are fully tender but not falling apart. Drain and remove vegetables and herbs. Toss hot beans with remaining 2 Tbsp. of olive oil. Pull leaves off stems of remaining thyme and toss with beans and oil. Add sea salt to taste.

Title: Couscous w/ Roasted Vegetable Stew
Description: I usually make this the day after I make roasted vegetables, using 1/2 the recipe for this. This is no ordinary left-over dish though - it deserves to be an important dish! If you like hot dishes, increase the peppers by 2.

Ingredients.Name: Recipe Roasted Vegetables or about 3-4 cups
Black pepper - fresh grind and Sea Salt to taste

Instructions: In a large heavy saucepan, saute shallot in oil over medium high heat til just beginning to turn clear. Add spices and cook in oil til very fragrant and shallots are clear. Add chicken broth, tomatoes and saffron and cook over high heat until just beginning to boil. Add vegetables and turn down to medium. Cook gently just at a simmer for about 1/2 hour until the flavors have blended. Test for seasoning. The broth should have a hint of spice and heat. The curry flavor should not dominate but be there subtly - add more if not.
To serve, mound couscous in large open rimmed bowls and surround with vegetables and broth.

Note: I like to use roasted fennel, onions, butternut squash and green beans but it’s great to experiment with other combinations. Other root vegetables work well and you can add greens to the sauté pan with the shallots and cook until they are about ½ way to tender before adding the broth.

Title: Red Beans & Rice

Ingredients.Name: Beef broth (low or non-fat) or 15 oz can
Chicken broth (low or non-fat) or one 15 ounce can

Instructions: Bring water to a boil and pour over the beans in a med. bowl and let rest for 2 hours. Drain and reserve beans.

Preheat oven to 350. Coarsely chop bacon and saute or med. high heat in a Dutch oven until just beginning to brown. If the bacon throws off a lot of fat, skim of absorb with paper towel. Coarsely chop shallots and add to bacon.
Saute for a minute or two. Do not let the bacon get too brown.
Add broths, garlic, tomatoes, Worchester and beans. Add enough water to the reserved tomato juice to make 1 cup and add. Over med. heat continue heating.
Add seasonings and adjust. When liquid just begins to boil.

Place in pre-heated oven and bake for 1& 1/2 hours to 2 hours until beans are tender and liquid is very reduced. They should not be entirely dry however with some liquid for the rice. Serve over long grain white rice.

Title: Couscous – The Best
Description: This is my lighter and less salty version of Patricia Well’s recipe. I find it more flexible but the technique is the same.
Instructions: In a large open bowl, stir the couscous with the salt and then add the oil and fluff the grains separating them from clumping. Add the water and fluff some more. Let the couscous rest and stir it occasionally about 10 to 15 minutes or until the water is all absorbed. If you are serving it right away, cover with plastic wrap and microwave for 1 to 2 minutes and fluff. If you are going to hold it, just wait to microwave it until you are ready.

Title: Chicken Farro w/ Veggies
Description: This is a great one dish meal and can be made with a great variety of vegetables.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh cherry tomatoes or cubed regular tomatoes
Chicken, cooked (left over) and cut into cubes
Shallots or equivalent amt of onion, chopped roughly
Red pepper, cubed in ½ in. squares
Zucchini, cubed in ½ in squares or ½ fresh peas or ½ cup asparagus in 1 inch lengths

Instructions: Saute shallots in the olive oil over medium heat until translucent and then add the chicken and toss. Add the red pepper and whatever green vegetable you choose. Saute until veggies are tender. Add cherry tomatoes and cook until they begin to crack open. Add the chicken broth and heat until hot throughout. Add the basil and toss. Season with salt and pepper. Use a little more pepper than you might normally. Add cheese and butter and let it melt into the broth. It should be very brothy.

Title: Farro w/ Favas and Peas

Ingredients.Name: Recipe basic farro (1 cup raw, cooked).
Shallots cut in half lengthwise and sliced
Favas, shelled, blanched and skins removed

Instructions: Saute shallots in olive oil over medium heat. Add pepper flakes and then toss shallots. Add the favas and heat for a minute or two (longer if they are large) and then the peas. Add the farro and mix well. Add the chicken broth and fresh basil with salt and pepper to taste. The mixture should be very moist and a little liquid should run when the pan is tilted. If too dry, add a little broth. When hot all through, add the butter until melted and then the cheese. Serve when the cheese melts into the sauce. You can sprinkle a little fresh basil over the top if you want.

Title: Farro - Basic
Instructions: Rinse the faro in cold water. Put in a medium saucepan and cover with cold water with about ½ inch over the faro. Bring to a boil, cover and reduce heat to simmer. The farro will take about 20 minutes to 30 minutes. Taste the farro. It should be firm and nutty but not hard. Salt to taste. Don’t overcook - It can get gummy.

Title: Shallot Jam
Description: Recipe adapted from Veronica Laramie

Ingredients.Name: large shal!ots (the two halves of one bulb equal one shal!ot), thinly sliced (preferably with a mandoline)
Rice wine vinegar or white wine vinegar

Instructions: Place all the ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Cook over low heat until the shallots are translucent and
slightly crunchy, and the liquid is thick and syrupy, about 30
minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool. Cover and
refrigerate until ready to use.

Title: Meyer Lemon Marmalade
Description: Use ½ pint jars.
Instructions: Rinse the lemons and pat dry. Halve the lemons crosswise and juice them, reserving the juice. Using a spoon, scrape the pulp and seeds from the halves. Using a sharp knife, slice the peels 1/8 inch thick.

In a large, heavy saucepan, cover the strips with 8 cups of cold water and bring to a boil; boil for 1 minute. Drain the strips and rinse under cold running water. Blanch two more times; the final time, drain the strips but do not rinse them.
Return the strips to the saucepan. Add the reserved juice and the sugar. Simmer over moderate heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar, then skimming any foam, until the marmalade sets, about 30 minutes.

Spoon the marmalade into 5 hot 1/2-pint canning jars, leaving 1/4 inch of space at the top, and close with the lids and rings. To process, boil the jars for 15 minutes in water to cover. Let stand at room temperature for 2 days before serving.

Title: Fig Honey Jam
Description: I use my home grown Mediterranean pink fig - with green skin. Any variety will work as long as they are ripe and sweet. If your figs are not very sweet, you may need to add a couple tbsp. of water to keep them from sticking.

Ingredients.Name: Lemon juice - Meyer lemon if possible
Honey - mild to medium flavorful - too flavorful will overpower the fig

Instructions: Heat the figs with the pectin in a large (5Qt) heavy pan until just boiling. Let boil for two minutes, stirring to dissolve the pectin. Add the honey, sugar, and lemon juice and continue to cook at a slow boil until figs are tender and syrupy. This will depend on the ripeness of your figs. Taste the jam and add more sugar, honey or lemon juice if it needs it. The flavor of honey should mix with the honey sweetness of the fig but should not dominate.
When the jam is the proper consistency, pack into boiling hot jars and lids according to canning instructions. Can in the boiling water bath for 15 minutes.

I usually get 3 jars of 8 oz. plus a 4 oz. jar from this recipe. If you don’t have 4 oz. jars, just refrigerate in a covered dish and use within a few days or use it to make a delicious sauce for poultry!
*Trim off tough stem of bottom ends and any bruised parts. I use larger chunks because I like it that way.

Title: Blackberry Jam
Description: This is a slightly easier but seedier version. Delicious.
Instructions: Prepare jars per canning instructions.
Place blackberries and pectin in large non-reactive deep saucepan - approx. 5 qt pan. Use more of less pectin depending on how thick you like your jam. Also, use more if your fruit is very ripe.

Heat over medium high heat until the fruit begins to boil. Add sugar and continue cooking until sugar melts and sauce is boiling. Reduce heat to a strong simmer and continue cooking for approx. 10-15 minutes until fruit is desired consistency. Try not to stir too much or the blackberries will disintegrate entirely. Jam will thicken slightly when it cools.
Turn off heat and skim off foam. Place into prepared, hot jars and add hot, clean lids pursuant to canning instructions.

Title: Peach & Blackberry Jam
Instructions: Prepare jars per canning instructions.

*To prepare peaches: blanch for 1 minute in boiling water, remove and quickly immerse in very cold water. Drain. Slip skins off peaches, pit and slice into 1/2 inch slices. Measure 6 Cups after cutting.
Place peaches and pectin in large non-reactive deep saucepan - approx. 5 qt pan. Use more of less pectin depending on how thick you like your jam. Also, use more if your fruit is very ripe.

Heat over medium high heat until the fruit begins to boil. Add sugar and lemon juice and continue cooking until sugar melts and sauce is boiling. Reduce heat to a strong simmer and continue cooking for approx. 20 minutes until fruit is desired consistency. Add blackberries and cook for 5 minutes. Try not to stir too much or the blackberries will fall apart. Jam will thicken slightly when it cools.
Turn off heat and skim off foam. Place into prepared, hot jars and add hot, clean lids pursuant to canning instructions.

Title: Peach Jam
Description: I love to make this with white nectarines!
Instructions: Prepare jars per canning instructions.

*To prepare peaches: blanch for 1 minute in boiling water, remove and quickly immerse in very cold water. Drain. Slip skins off peaches, pit and slice into 1/2 inch slices. Measure 6 Cups after cutting.
Place peaches and pectin in large non-reactive deep saucepan - approx. 5 qt pan. Use more of less pectin depending on how thick you like your jam. Also, use more if your fruit is very ripe.

Heat over medium high heat until the fruit begins to boil. Add sugar and lemon juice and continue cooking until sugar melts and sauce is boiling. Reduce heat to a strong simmer and continue cooking for approx. 20 minutes until fruit is desired consistency. Jam will thicken slightly when it cools.
Turn off heat and skim off foam. Place into prepared, hot jars and add hot, clean lids pursuant to canning instructions.

Title: Santa Rosa Plum Jam
Description: You can use other plums, you just might need to adjust the sugar depending on the sweetness of the fruit and how much acid in the skins.

Ingredients.Name: Santa Rosa plums, washed, pitted and cut into sixths

Instructions: Prepare jars according to canning instructions.

Place plums and pectin into large deep saucepan, about 5 Qt. pan. Use more pectin if you like your jam thick. Also, if your fruit is very ripe, use more. Plums have a lot of natural pectin so if they are just barely ripe, it should thicken almost on its own. Bring to boil on medium high heat. Add sugar, stir well and continue to cook until it comes to a boil again. Reduce to strong simmer and cook approx. 20 minutes until jam thickens to desired consistency. It will thicken a little more when it cools. Turn off heat and skim foam. Pour into prepared, hot jars pursuant to canning instructions.

Title: Apricot Jam
Description: This jam tastes of summer - all fruit and not just sugar.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh apricots, pitted and cut into quarters

Instructions: Prepare jars per canning instructions.
Place apricots and pectin in large non-reactive deep saucepan - approx. 5 qt pan. Use more of less pectin depending on how thick you like your jam. Also, use more if your fruit is very ripe.

Heat over medium high heat until the fruit begins to boil. Add sugar and lemon juice and continue cooking until sugar melts and sauce is boiling. Reduce heat to a strong simmer and continue cooking for approx. 20 minutes until fruit is desired consistency. Jam will thicken slightly when it cools.
Turn off heat and skim off foam. Place into prepared, hot jars and add hot, clean lids pursuant to canning instructions.

Title: My Carnitas
Description: This is my version - a compilation and refinement of various recipes tried over the years.

Ingredients.Name: Sugar for each lb of pork
Salt for each lb of pork
Chile powder – guajillo, or even a mix is o.k.
Slice white peasant style bread, crusts removed
Sea Salt plus a bit more for the broth

Instructions: Cut pork into 4 or 5-inch chunks, and trim of excess fat. Rub the pieces of pork shoulder all over with salt and sugar plus 1 Tbsp of the Ancho Chile powder. Refrigerate overnight. This is super important to the flavor and crispness of the pork.

2. Heat the oil in a large dutch oven or roasting pan. Cook the pieces of pork shoulder in a single layer until very well-browned. Don’t move them around too much so they get very dark. Cook in two batches if the pan is too small for all the pork.

3. Once the pork is brown, remove all of it from the pan and drain the excess fat. I often blot it with paper towels to really get it all soaked up. Pour in a cup or two of water, scraping the bottom of the pan with a spatula or wooden spoon to loosen all the brown bits.
4. Heat the oven to 350 degrees.
5. Put the pork back in the pan and add enough water so the pork pieces are submerged in the water about 2/3rds of the way. Add the chile powders, bay leaves, cinnamon, cumin and garlic.

7. Place in the oven uncovered for 3 hours, turning the pork a few times during cooking, until much of the liquid is evaporated and the pork is beginning to fall apart. If the water is gone, and the pork is still a bit stiff, place back in the oven with another ½ cup water or a little more if super dry - for another ½ to 1 hour. Remove the pork from the oven and take the pork pieces out of the water and set them on a plate or into another pan.

8. Cool the pork and when you can handle them, shred them into bite-sized pieces. I like them about 1-2 inches. Discard any chunks of fat if you want the pork to be leaner and more dry. I like them super dry and crispy.

9. Return the pork back to the pan and into the oven again. This time, you’ll be stirring them and turning them periodically while they cook until all the liquid is gone and the pork is ultra carmelized and crispy. This can take another ½ hour to 1 hour depending on how dark you like it and how much moisture the pork contained to begin with.
Recipe
Mini Herbed Meatballs

This is inspired by a typical Spanish tapa. You can make these with lamb which would be typical or pork which is great or a mix of both! This is a lighter version. These are intended to be served as an hors d’oeuvre. If the meatballs are 1” or so, you get about 30 meatballs but I usually end up with between 24-30 depending on how many people I’m serving and what else follows.
Category
Meats
Servings

Let the turkey meat come to room temperature. Soak the bread in lukewarm water for 10 mins or til soft. Warm 2 Tbsp. oil in large skillet and saute ½ of the chopped onion, ½ the garlic and ¼ tsp. red pepper flakes. When translucent add to the turkey and stir to incorporate well. Squeeze the water out of the bread and break it into bits into the turkey meat. Mix well. Add the herbs, cumin, salt and several good twists of fresh pepper. Shape into small meatballs, about 1 to 1 &1/2" and place on a plate in the refrigerator to chill for 30 mins – this helps them hold their shape when cooked. Heat the oven to 350degrees when you put them in the refrigerator.

Heat the same skillet with the other 2 tbsp. oil and saute the meatballs in batches on medium high until browned on all sides. Remove to a small baking dish. To the hot skillet, add rest of the onions, remaining garlic and red pepper and saute til translucent. Add the broth, tomatoes, and the saffron. Add salt and pepper to taste. Cook scraping up the brown bits until the flavors are blended, adjust seasoning, and let simmer about 10 mins to reduce slightly. Pour over the meatballs so that there is about 1” of liquid around them. Add a little more broth or water to make sure there is enough. Place in the oven and cook about 20 mins to 30 mins depending on size of the meatballs til cooked through.
Serve with mini forks or large toothpicks from the baking dish while hot from the oven.

Title: Provencal Lamb Stew
Description: This is from Food and Wine magazine and is perfect.

Ingredients.Name: Trimmed boneless lamb shoulder, in 1” pieces
Salt packed, rinse well and debone
French cured with herbs works well but any
flavorful plain green olive will work o.k.

Instructions: Season the lamb with salt and pepper generously. Put 3 tbsp. of the oil in a large dutch oven non-reactive pot, and heat until hot but not smoking. Add the lamb and brown over medium high heat until well browned about 12 minutes. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

Add the shallots, anchovy fillets rosemary and approx. 4 of the garlic cloves. Stir over medium high heat until the shallot softens. Add the potatoes and toss. Cook about 2-3 minutes until the potatoes begin to brown on one side. Add the rose wine and reduce a bit while scraping up all the browned bits. Add the lamb and accumulated juices, the olives and 2 Cups water and bring to a boil. Cover and reduce to a simmer over moderately low heat until the lamb is tender, approx. 50 minutes. In a small bowl, mash the remaining chopped garlic and add the remaining 2 tbsp. olive oil and the chopped basil. Stir into the stew just before serving. Taste for salt and pepper and adjust seasoning as needed.

Title: Carnitas
Description: This is a basic recipe for carnitas or pulled pork. Sweet and salty and perfectly rich and wonderful. So many things you can do with it.

Ingredients.Name: Bone in pork butt or shoulder
Sea salt per pound of pork

Instructions: Heat oven to 250 degrees.

Rub in salt and sugar all over the roast. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Place in roasting pan. Roast for 6 hours plus a little if needed. After about three hours, turn the pork over and baste often with the juices, until the pork is deep golden brown and falling apart. When cool enough to manage, pull apart with 2 forks, pulling out the fat, separating the meat into beautiful shreds of succulent pork.

Title: Duck Carnitas
Description: A Rick Bayliss recipe

Ingredients.Name: Large duck legs (you need 2 1/2 to 3 pounds )
Ripe avocado, pitted, flesh scooped from the skin
Rich-tasting pork lardor duck fat if you have it

Instructions: Marinate the duck. Lay the duck legs in a 13 x 9-inch non-aluminum baking dish. Sprinkle with half the salt and oregano, then drizzle with half the lime juice. Flip them over and sprinkle with the remaining salt and oregano; drizzle with the remaining lime. Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours, turning a couple of times. Cook the duck. Heat the oven to 300 degrees. In a large (4-quart) saucepan, melt the lard. Remove the duck from the baking dish and pat dry on paper towels. Rinse and dry the baking dish. Fit in the duck legs. Pour the lard over the duck, making sure the legs are completely submerged. Scatter the garlic cloves over the duck legs and nestle them into the lard. Slide into the oven (you may want to do this on a rimmed baking sheet to avoid spills), and bake for about 2 hours until the duck is very tender. Cool to lukewarm.Serve the duck carnitas. Remove the duck from the lard. Pull off the skin and set aside. Pull the meat from the bone into large pieces. Discard the bones. Spoon 2 tablespoons of the lard into a very large (12-inch) skillet (preferably nonstick) and set over medium-high. When hot, lay in the skin and cook, turning frequently, until very crisp, about 5 minutes. Remove to a drain on paper towels. Add the meat and cook, turning regularly, until browned and crisping in spots, about 7 or 8 minutes Scoop into a serving platter. Coarsely crumble the duck skin over the top and serve with the Tomatillo-Avocado Salsa and warm tortillas.

Salsa: Roughly chop half of the tomatillos and scoop them into a food processor with the cilantro and green chiles. Measure in 1/4 cup water and process to a slushy, coarse puree. Roughly chop half the avocado, add it to the processor and pulse until it is incorporated into the salsa. Scrape into a serving dish. Scoop the onion into a small strainer and rinse under cold water. Add to the salsa. Finely chop the remaining tomatillos and add them, too. Finally, chop the remaining avocado into 1/4-inch pieces and stir them into the salsa. Taste and season with salt, usually about 3/4 teaspoon

Title: Veal Meatballs w/ Artichokes, Tomatoes & Green Olives
Description: This is adapted from Paul Bertolli's recipe. It is a great winter dish.

Ingredients.Name: Cherry tomatoes or small fresh ripe tomatoes cubed
Green olives, mild, pitted, coarsely chopped
Fresh flat leaf parsley, finely chopped
Chicken broth, non-fat, low sodium if using canned
sea salt and freshly ground pepper
Serve with Fresh Egg Noodles tossed with butter and cheese

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350.

Warm 1 Tbsp olive oil in skillet and add onions and salt and pepper them lightly. Cook about 8 minutes on medium heat until translucent. Adjust heat to keep them from browning. Meanwhile, put the veal in a large bowl and add the parsley, parmesan, eggs and bread crumbs. Blend well with hands until thoroughly incorporated. Add one/third of the onions to the mixture and mix well. Season the mixture with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp. pepper. Form the veal into small meatballs - makes 16-18 small balls. Set aside on plate.
Trim artichokes of outer leaves and trim stems. Cut into quarters, remove choke if any, and put in acidulated water while working.
Heat remaining oil in heavy duty skillet and brown the meat balls in batches if necessary. When browned on all sides, remove to a plate until all are done.
In a large baking dish with at least 3" sides, add the remaining onions in a layer at the bottom. Set the browned meatballs on top in a single layer.

In a large bowl, combine the drained artichokes, tomatoes, garlic, olive, sage and lemon juice. Season with a little salt and pepper and then distribute veggies around the meat in the baking dish. Pour broth over the dish and cover the dish tightly. Bake for one hour.
Serve alongside fresh egg noodles, cut fettuccine or papparadelle style. Toss the noodles with butter and parmesan.

Title: Braised Sour Orange Pork
Description: The flavorings in this are adapted from Cuban style dishes. This is traditionally served with rice.

Ingredients.Name: Large oranges, Seville style if available or 1 Cup fresh orange juice
Pork shoulder, de-boned and cut into 1 ½” pieces, trimmed of excessive fat/sinew
2 Lemons – juiced if not using Seville oranges

Instructions: Preheat oven to 325.
Marinate Pork in all ingredients except onion for a minimum of 3 hours or overnight in the fridge.
Remove pork from marinade and pat dry. Pour marinade into deep casserole with lid that can go into oven.

In a large skillet, heat olive oil til hot but not smoking. Add the pork and saute on high heat to brown the meat on all sides. If the pan is crowded and the meat gives off a lot of liquid, do the browning in two batches. When all the meat is browned, toss the onions into the skillet and toss quickly to pull up brown bits from skillet and until the onions just begin to go translucent. Toss the meat and onion mixture into the marinade and cover and put in the oven.
Bake for 3 hours. Test to see if the meat is very tender. If not, continue cooking – perhaps as much as another ½ hour.

Title: Braised Short Ribs
Description: This is a café Chez Panisse recipe that I have modified somewhat. It is classic and delicious especially during the winter and served with roasted vegetables or mashed potatoes.

Ingredients.Name: Beef short ribs, cut 2 inches thick – see below
Leeks, whites/pale green pts. Washed well and roughly chopped
Zest of ½ lemon, finely chopped

Instructions: Have the butcher slice the ribs into roughly square chunks, including a bone on each. Trim excess fat and season generously with salt and pepper. Refrigerate 4-6 hours or overnight.

Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Arrange the short ribs bone side down in a roasting pan and roast until lightly browned, about 20 minutes. Meanwhile, saute the onions in the olive oil in a very large skillet. Add the leeks and carrot and cook until they are all softened. Add tomatoes, garlic, thyme, parsley and bay leave and saute for several minutes until the herbs release their fragrances.

In a large baking dish (not metal), pour n the vegetables and spread into a nice thick layer. Lay the ribs over the veggies with the bone up. Pour in the wine and add broth to cover the ribs. Cover the entire pan tightly with foil and return to the oven for about 20 minutes, until the braising liquid is simmering well. Reduce the temperature to 350 and loosen the foil.
Cook for 1 ½ hours more and test for doneness. The meat should be nearly falling off the bone and if you insert a knife or skewer into the meat, it should not encounter any resistance.

Pour off braising juices and turn the ribs bone side down. Return to oven at 425 without foil and let ribs brown again for about 10 minutes until fully glazed. Meanwhile, strain the braising liquid, pushing down on the solids to extract all the juices. Reheat the cooking juices.
Remove the ribs to a serving dish and pour the juices over them. If using the Gremolata, chop the garlic finely and mix with the parsley and lemon and then scatter over the ribs.

Title: Chili -
Description: This is a recipe that I adjust regularly depending on what I have in the fridge – adding more veggies, more meat, or more beans – each time creating something slightly different. I like to serve this over brown rice – it cuts the richness and extends the chili for a couple nights.

Ingredients.Name: Cup fresh corn or frozen - optional
Tsp. red pepper flakes or 1 fresh jalapeno, seeded and chopped
Sea salt and Fresh ground pepper
Grated cheddar, cilantro and lime slices for garnish - optional

Instructions: Heat the olive oil in a very large deep skillet. When hot and the ground beef crumbled and stir until you break up the meat. Add ½ tsp. chili powder and the red pepper flakes or jalapeno. Stir so the powder and spices mix well with the meat. As the beef looses its pink color and begins to caramelize a little, add the onion and garlic and reduce the heat to med-med/low. Saute until the onion is translucent. Add the green pepper and sauté until just beginning to soften. Add the cumin, ancho chili powder if using, the tomatoes and all the beans. Sprinkle generously with salt and pepper. Cover, leaving the lid slightly ajar and sauté for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then. Taste the chili and add more spice and more salt and pepper if its too mild. If the chili is too thin, you can leave the lid off while you continue cooking. If too thick, you can add a little water to keep it loose enough. Continue cooking for about another ½ hour to an hour until the flavors meld and the spices have infused the meat and vegetables. Usually the longer the better. Add the corn in the last five minutes if using. Serve hot and garnished with fresh grated cheddar, chopped cilantro and lime.

Title: My Pork Ribs
Description: I use this recipe for either baby back or St. Louis style ribs. Either works but you might need to adjust the time to ensure you cook them completely – tender and much of the fat rendered out.

Ingredients.Name: Baby back ribs or St. Louis Ribs
Red pepper flakes or more to taste

Instructions: Chop the garlic with about ¼ cup of leaves removed from the stems of the herbs. Continue chopping with 1 tsp. of the salt and the orange zest if using. Rub the mixture into the entire rack of ribs. Sprinkle with the red pepper, several liberal grindings of black pepper and more salt – about another ½ tsp. The salt carries the flavors of the aromatics into the meat. Don’t worry, it will not be too salty as the pork will render off the fat and much of the salt with it. Don’t be afraid to add more red pepper flakes if you like it a little spicy. Let rest 4 hours at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.

Place the pork with its rub into the oven in a large roasting pan. Roast for one hour until dark golden brown all over and until much of the fat is puddled in the pan. If the ribs are very fatty, remove the pan at about the 1 hour mark, pour off fat, and continue cooking for about another half hour. The meat should be very tender and the visible fat should be very crispy. The ribs can get very dark. If using the St. Louis ribs, they will definitely need longer to cook than the baby backs. Serve immediately.
This dish is rich and wonderful. Serve it with a simple salad.

Title: 4 Hour Roast Pork

Ingredients.Name: 4lb pork loin roast, bone in (do not trim off fat)
plump, fresh cloves garlic, peeled and minced
Freshly ground white pepper to taste
large bunches of fresh thyme sprigs

Instructions: 1. Preheat the oven to 275F.

2.Season the pork all over with sea salt, white pepper, and the 2 tsps thyme. In a large heavy-duty casserole that will hold the pork snugly, heat the oil over moderate heat until hot but not smoking. Add the pork and sear well on all sides, about 10 minutes total. Transfer the pork to a platter and discard the fat in the casserole. Wipe the casserole clean with paper towels. Return the pork to the casserole, bone side down. Set it aside.

3. In a large, heavy skillet, combine the butter, carrots, onions, garlic, celery, and sea salt to taste. Sweat--cook, covered, over low heat without coloring--until the vegetables are soft and cooked through, about 10 minutes. Spoon the vegetables around and on top of the pork. Add the chicken stock to the casserole. Add the bunches of thyme, and cover.

4. Place the casserole in the center of the oven and braise, basting every 30 minutes, for about 4 hours, or until the pork is just about falling off the bone. Remove the casserole from the oven. Carefully transfer the meat to a carving board and season it generously with sea salt and white pepper. Cover loosely with foil and set aside to rest for about 15 minutes.
5. While the pork is resting, strain the cooking juices through a fine-mesh sieve into a gravy boat, pouring off the fat that rises to the top. Discard the vegetables and herbs.

6. The pork will be very soft and falling off the bone, so you may not actually be able to slice it. Rather, use a fork and spoon to tear the meat into serving pieces, and place them on warmed dinner plates or a warmed platter. Spoon the juices over the meat, and serve. Transfer any remaining juices to a gravy boat and pass at the table.

Title: Veal Meatballs w/ Sage
Description: From Food and Wine Magazine. Serve with medium bodied Sangiovese.

Ingredients.Name: crustless day-old bread, cut into 1 inch cubes (approx. 1 Cup)

Instructions: In a small bowl, soak the bread in the milk until softened, about 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the veal with the scallions, garlic, salt and pepper. Squeeze the bread dry and add it to veal.
With you hands, mix the ingredients thoroughly. Shape into 30 meatballs and transfer to a baking sheet.
In a large skillet, melt the butter, and add the sage leaves. Make sure they lay flat and cook over high heat until crispy, a couple minutes. Remove from skillet and place on plate.

Dust the meatballs in the flour lightly. Shake off excess. Add the meatballs to the skillet which should still be hot, and cook over medium high heat until browned all over and cooked through. Transfer to a plate and keep warm covered with foil. Add the wine to the skillet and simmer scraping up the browned bits until almost evaporated. Add the stock and simmer until slightly reduced about 2 minutes. Transfer the meatballs to a serving dish or platter. Pour the sauce over and garnish with the sage.

Title: Abaccio a la Romana
Description: This is a Mario Batali recipe

Ingredients.Name: Lamb shoulder or leg cut into large cubes
sea salt and fresh ground black pepper
Anchovies, salt packed, soaked in milk for 10 min

Instructions: In a large non-reactive deep pan, heat the olive oil. Toss the lamb with salt and pepper.

Add to hot pan and brown well until caramelized. While meat is browning, Combine rosemary leaves, anchovies chopped, garlic and vinegar. Add to lamb, scraping up the browned bits. Add the wine when the vinegar evaporates. toss the lamb to coat and let moisture evaporate. Add a little more vinegar if this goes too quickly and lamb isn't cooked. When the lamb is cooked, add fresh chopped ;mint and lemon zest. Taste for salt and serve immediately.

Title: Roast Pork Loin with Spinach
Description: This is a variation on a traditional Italian dish. To serve a larger group, double recipe and use two roasts.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh spinach, with tough stems removed, rinsed and drained well.
Imported prosciutto, preferably from Parma, thinly sliced
Chicken stock, low-sodium, non-fat, if using canned
Freshly grated parmesan cheese, preferably Reggiano
Sea Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Instructions: Heat 2 tbsp. olive oil in 9-10" nonstick skillet. When hot, add garlic and shallot and saute for a couple minutes until both are translucent but not brown. Add spinach and cook until just wilted, turning over in the oil, approx. 3 minutes. Remove from heat and using a slotted spoon set spinach in a colander to drain.
Place drained spinach in a medium bowl and add parmesan cheese and stir until well incorporated. Add a couple pinches of salt and a few grindings of pepper to taste.

Butterfly the roast by slicing down the center of the roast until 1 1/2 " from the bottom. Open flat on a work surface. Cut kitchen twine into 3 or 4 lengths that will easily wrap around the roast and lay under roast perpendicular to the crease. Remove all excess fat from prosciutto and arrange slices, overlapping across the roast. Using your hands, mold spinach into a small log along the crease in the roast. Fold the roast around spinach and use the twine to tie tightly. A little stuffing may squeeze out but close the slice as tightly as possible so you don't lose too much when cooking.

Heat 1 Tbsp. olive oil in ovenproof deep sided skillet. Brown the roast on medium high heat on all sides, about 10 minutes. Move roast to a platter and pour off excess fat. Return to heat and add 1 Cup stock scraping up any browned bits stuck to the bottom. Return roast to platter and set in oven. Roast for 40-45 minutes until thermometer reads 145 degrees. Check the roast periodically and add a little water to the pan so there is always moisture in the pan. Remove from pan and cover with foil, loosely to rest for approx. 15 minutes while you finish the sauce. Remove fat from the pan juices by skimming or other method and return skillet to heat. When hot, add the wine and scrape up any browned bits remaining. Add the rest of the stock and bring to a boil. Mix the flour with a little water to form a loose paste. Add the flour to the pan juices and whisk until incorporated. Reduce heat and simmer until beginning to thicken. Add any juices which have collected under the resting roast. Untie the roast and slice into thick 1 " slices. Arrange on platter and pass the reduced sauce.

Title: Boeuf a la Bourguignonne
Description: Simple, unsophisticated but delicious! This is best served with a simple starch like golden potatoes, steamed and dressed in extra virgin olive oil and sea salt, perhaps with a little parsley.

Ingredients.Name: Beef chuck cut into large pieces, not cubed like stew but portion sizes, about 6 or more oz each
Large yellow onion, peeled and chopped
Chanterelles or other fresh mushrooms, gently cleaned and sliced
Bouquet garni - of parsley, thyme, peppercorns
Bottle good quality Burgundy or Calif. Pinot Noir

Instructions: Marinate beef for at least 24 hours - Place beef, wine, onion, carrots, garlic and bouquet garni in large non-reactive bowl or pot. Cover tightly and refrigerate. Remove from refrigerator 1 or 2 hours before preparing.

Remove beef from marinade. Pat dry with paper towels. Reserve marinade. In a large pot or deep skillet, brown the salt pork until crisp and golden. If it renders a lot of fat, blot with paper towels before adding meat. Add ;meat and brown on all sides. Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle in flour to absorb fat and cooking juices. Stir for several minutes. Add marinade and 2 Cups water. Bring to a boil and scrape up all the brown bits adhering to the pan. Reduce the heat until it simmers gently. Cook until meat is tender, approx. 3 hours. The meat should be very tender and the sauce thickened. In a small skillet, heat olive oil and toss in the mushrooms and saute until tender. Sprinkle the mushrooms over the meat right before serving.

Title: Osso Bucco
Description: This is a warm wintery dish - made special by the addition of the "gremolata" sprinkled on at the last minute. This is a simplified version of Marcella Hazan's traditional Italian recipe.

Ingredients.Name: Veal shanks cut in about 2" sections of bone If very large use 4, 6 if smaller
Fennel bulbs, green parts trimmed, and washed,
Homemade beef or chicken broth (o.k. to use canned low-sodium)
Sea Salt and Pepper to Taste

Instructions: Brown the meat on all sides in the butter and oil in a large heavy duty casserole in which all the shanks fit easily. Chop all the veggies including the 2 cloves garlic in a food processor. When the meat is brown, remove it to a platter and season with salt and pepper. If more than a couple tablespoons of fat remain, skim off leaving a heavy coating in the bottom. Add veggies to pan while still hot. Cook 2-3 minutes until just translucent. Add wine and over high heat reduce wine til almost gone. Add the meat and any juices from the platter. Add 1 Cup stock and the tomatoes. Meat should almost be submerged. If not add more broth. Add lemon zest strips and 1 Tbsp of parsley. Cover, reduce heat so that meat cooks at slow simmer. Cook approximately 1-1/2 hours until meat is tender. Chop (in mini processor is o.k.) garlic, lemon zest and parsley very fine. Sprinkle over the osso bucco just before serving.

Title: Grilled Beef w/ Smokey Rub

Ingredients.Name: Sea salt, chunky, not fine (or kosher)
Lbs. beef – tenderloin, eye of round, or rib eye roast

Instructions: Chop garlic fine and mix with dry ingredients – rub all over meat and refrigerate tightly covered for at least 12 hours. Remove from refrigerator and scrap off excess rub. Heat grill and cook on a fairly hot fire for 25 minutes, turning it about every 6 minutes. If using tenderloin or a cut that is less than about 5” thick, it may cook in less time. The beef should be about 120 degrees for medium rare. Allow steak to rest for 10 minutes. Slice and drizzle with the olive oil.

If roasting, preheat oven to 500 degrees. Rub with the olive oil and roast in a roasting pan until the roast reaches 120 degrees. This takes about 25 minutes as well. Let it rest for at least 10 minutes and up to 30 minutes loosely covered with foil. Slice and pour any of the accumulated juices over it.

Title: Pork Tenderloin w/ Balsamic
Instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet (non-stick is best) over high heat. Add the tenderloin and brown on all sides, approx. 2 to 3 minutes per side. The loin should take about 12-14 minutes total. You may need to reduce the heat to cook until it is done without smoking the oil or burning the meat. Cut a small slice into the loin to ensure it is pink but not raw. Toss the balsamic and rosemary into the skillet and cook until it coats the meat. Salt and pepper generously.

Title: Skirt Steak – Grilled or Broiled
Instructions: Marinate the steak in the ingredients, except the salt and pepper, for 3 hours at room temperature. Heat grill or broiler. Remove from marinade and pat dry. Salt and pepper generously. Grill for about 1-2 minutes on each side over a medium hot fire. Each side should be caramelized and just beginning to be blackened on the edges. Let rest for about 5 minutes covered loosely in foil.

Title: Pork Loin Braised In Milk
Description: This is a traditional recipe from Marcella Hazan. It is a surprising hit with everyone.

Ingredients.Name: pork loin in one piece, with some fat on it, securely tied
Freshly ground pepper, 3 or 4 twists of the mill

Instructions: 1. Heat the butter and oil over medium-high heat in a casserole large enough to just contain the pork. When the butter foam subsides add the meat, fat side facing down. Brown thoroughly on all sides, lowering the heat if the butter starts to turn dark brown.

2. Add the salt, pepper, and milk. (Add the milk slowly, otherwise it may boil over.) Shortly after the milk comes to a boil, turn the heat down to medium, cover, but not tightly, with the lid partly askew, and cook slowly for about 11/2 to 2 hours, until the meat is easily pierced by a fork. Turn and baste the meat from time to time, and if necessary, add a little milk. By the time the meat is cooked the milk should have coagulated into small nut-brown clusters. If it is still pale in color, uncover the pot, raise the heat to high, and cook briskly until it darkens.

3. Remove the meat to a cutting board and allow to cool off slightly for a few minutes. Remove the trussing string, carve into slices 3/8 inch thick, and arrange them on a warm platter. Draw off most of the fat from the pot with a spoon and discard, being careful not to discard any of the coagulated milk clusters. Taste and correct for salt. (There may be as much as 1 to 11/2 cups of fat to be removed). Add 2 to 3 tablespoons of warm water, turn the heat to high, and boil away the water while scraping and loosening all the cooking residue in the pot. Spoon the sauce over the sliced pork and serve immediately.

Title: Roast Pork w/ Fennel
Description: This is great with just the fennel but I also like to reduce the amount of fennel and add some root vegetables such as parsnips, carrots, and turnips.

Ingredients.Name: Fennel bulbs, green parts trimmed, and washed,
Sea salt & Fresh ground black pepper
*Optional root vegetables, sliced in small pieces. Parsnips, carrots, turnips are all good.

Instructions: Preheat oven to 400*

Chop garlic and mix well with zests and salt. Rub pork with 1 Tbsp oil and then rub in the garlic mixture, coating all sides. Grind fresh black pepper all over generously. Put pork in roasting pan and roast for 15 minutes fat side up. While pork is roasting, blanch fennel in boiling salted water for about 5 minutes and drain. Toss with remaining olive oil, lemon juice and then salt and pepper. Add additional root vegetables if using and toss. After the first 15 minutes of cooking, remove roast and put vegetables around roast. Return to oven, reduce heat to 325* and roast for another 45 minutes or until 140* on a meat thermometer. Cover loosely with foil and rest for 10 minutes on a cutting board or large platter. Discard fat from pan, add wine and cook on top of stove scraping up brown bits and until the liquid reduces by half. Add any juices from the pork. Serve.

Title: Spicy Curry Noodles
Description: This can be made with any protein but is best with chicken, shrimp or fish

Ingredients.Name: Samal oelek chili sauce – to taste
Chow mein noodles (egg is best, cooked)
Cooked shredded chicken – white or dark o.k.
Fresh herbs, torn into pieces: Mint, basil, and cilantro

Instructions: 1. Lightly toast the ground spices in a small pan over low heat until fragrant.
2. Trim the lemon grass of the long tough green parts, and crush the stalk really well with the side of a knife or smash with the edge of a small pot until fragrant.

3. In a deep saute pan or pot that can hold all the stock heat on high and add oil until hot but not smoking - add shallots, garlic, ginger, and lemongrass. Add the spices and stir until the onion and garlic are translucent and the oil is absorbed. Lower the heat, and add the coconut milk, chicken stock, and 1 oz chili sauce. Stir until everything is incorporated. Bring the sauce to a boil, and season with salt. Taste and add more chili sauce to the desired heat. Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring well regularly to ensure nothing sticks to the bottom and burns.

4. In a pot of boiling water, blanch the noodles and sprouts. Portion the noodles and sprouts into six serving bowls. Add the chicken to the noodles, and pour the hot curry sauce over them. Finally, garnish each bowl with herbs and lime. Serve with additional chili sauce too.

Title: Pork Sugo ala Delfina

Ingredients.Name: Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Instructions: 1. Cut the pork shoulder into 4 pieces. Season the pork shoulder and spareribs with salt and pepper, and sear in a heavy bottomed pot using canola or other neutrally flavored oil. When golden on all sides, remove the pork, and set aside. 2. To the pot, add the onions, carrot, celery, garlic, and herbs, and cook until lightly caramelized. Add the tomato paste, cook for 2 minutes, and deglaze with the wine.3. Return the seared pork and ribs to the pot, add chicken stock, and bring to a simmer. Cover and transfer the pot to a 325-degree oven to cook until tender, approximately 2 hours. Remove from the oven and let cool, ideally overnight.4. Once cool, remove the pork from the liquid, discard the ribs, and pick the pork shoulder into large chunks. 5. Using a food mill, mill the liquid along with all of the vegetables and herbs. Return the resulting sugo to the saucepot, bring to a simmer, and reduce to the desired consistency. Pour over the picked pork meat, and cool quickly.6. To serve, warm the pork sugo in a pan with the butter, chopped parsley, and chile flake (if desired). Concurrently drop the pasta in boiling, lightly salted water. When the pasta is almost fully cooked (approximately 2 minutes), drain the pasta, and add it to the pan containing the pork sugo. Cook the pasta in the sugo for another minute, and finish by stirring in some grated Parmigiano. Transfer to a serving plate, and serve immediately, offering more Parmigiano to grate over the top of the pasta.

Title: All’Amatriciana
Description: Classic recipe. Use pancetta if you can’t find guanciale but the flavor is much improved with the guanciale.

Ingredients.Name: Guanciale, sliced ¼” wide and then into ½”
Pasta – Spaghetti, Pici, Bucatini, or other toothsome pasta
Pureed tomatoes, preferably San Marzano canned or other richly flavored tomatoes (fresh in season)

Instructions: Heat oil in large skillet over medium heat until hot but not smoking. Add the guanciale and cook until just beginning to turn golden brown all over about 5 minutes. Grind in several grindings of black pepper and add garlic, carrots and onions and cook until soft about 5 minutes. Add the chile flakes and toss well, continuing heating for about 1-2 minutes. Add tomatoes and cook for about 20-30 minutes until flavors meld and sauce thickens somewhat. Taste and season with salt.

Cook Pasta according to instructions until al dente. Reserve ¼ cup cooking liquid. Drain and toss into the sauce. Heat for about 1-2 minutes until the sauce coats the pasta well. Toss in ½ the cheese and serve in warmed bowls.
Serve additional cheese along side.

Title: Artichoke & Chestnut Pasta

Ingredients.Name: Homemade chicken or other poultry stock
1 Cup of peanut or other veg. oil
Cold press virgin olive oil - best quality
Sea Salt and fresh ground pepper
Dried semolina pasta, such as spaghetti or linguine – whole wheat is also good

Instructions: Prepare Chestnuts - Cut a slit along both rounded sides of each chestnut through the brown skin under the shell. Heat enough veg. oil in a small saucepan to cover the chestnuts (approx. 1 1/2 inches deep) on high heat until very hot but not smoking. Drop 6 chestnuts carefully into the hot oil and cook until the shells explode open - approximately 1-3 minutes. Be careful, the oil will splatter as the shells open. Remove the chestnuts with a slotted spoon to paper towels to drain. Repeat with the remaining 6 chestnuts. When cool enough to handle, remove the shells and the outer brown skin. In another small saucepan, heat approx. 1 cup of the broth and add chestnuts. Bring to gentle boil and then simmer partially covered until the chestnuts are tender - approx. 20 minutes. Check the broth periodically and add enough to keep the chestnuts in liquid. Do not let dry out. Drain the chestnuts and cool.

Prepare Artichokes - Cut stem off at base of choke. Snap back the outer leaves leaving the small tender leaf at base. Continue snapping back until you reach the tender yellow leaves. Cut off tops of remaining leaves approx. 1 - 1 1/2 inches above the heart. Rub cut pieces with lemon to retard discoloration. Cut artichoke in half and scoop out the fibrous center or "choke". Immediately drop the artichoke into a bowl of cold water with the juice of at least half a lemon to retard the discoloration. Continue with all the artichokes.

Prepare Pasta - Bring a large 6 qt. saucepan of water to a boil. Meanwhile, in a 9 or 10" saute pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat until fragrant, and add the garlic. While the garlic is cooking, quickly slice the artichoke hearts into 6 wedges per half and add to the garlic as soon as it is translucent.

Toss the artichokes in the oil and continue cooking over medium heat until the artichokes are tender - approx. 10 minutes. If they get a little golden, that is o.k. just don't let them get too dark or burn. When the artichokes are almost tender, slice the chestnuts (approx. 4 slices per) and add to the artichokes. Toss in well. Add about 1/2 cup of the stock and bring to a gentle boil. Add the dried spaghetti to the pot of boiling water and cook until it test done "al dente". Drain. Check the artichoke sauce and add more stock - turn up to high until it boils. There should be enough stock to coat all the pasta. Taste for seasoning and add salt, pepper and the chopped parsley. Toss the pasta into the saute pan with artichokes & chestnuts or in large warmed bowl. Cover and let rest for one minute. Serve with fresh parmesan cheese.

Title: Spaghetti All'Ubriaco
Description: Gina di Palma’s recipe
Instructions: 1. Add the water and red wine to a 6-quart stock pot and place it over medium-high heat. Season the liquid generously with kosher salt and cover the pot to bring it to a boil.
2. In the meantime, peel the garlic and slice it. Place the butter and olive oil in a sauté pan large enough to fit the pasta and place it over low heat to slowly melt the butter.
3. When the water and wine come to a boil, add your spaghetti; stirring as needed to engulf the pasta in the liquid. As the spaghetti cooks, stir it often to prevent it from sticking.
4. Add the garlic to the pan and wait for it to come to a sizzle. Add the optional peperoncino for some heat, if you like and stir the garlic, keeping the heat low to prevent it from scorching
5. When the garlic is toasted pale and sizzling, add the additional ½ cup of red wine and a generous splash of the pasta cooking water to the pan and turn up the heat until the liquid simmers.

6. Test the spaghetti for doneness; when it is al dente, transfer it to the sauté pan along with the parsley. Keep cooking the spaghetti in the juices, tossing and shaking the pan until the liquid is absorbed.
7. Serve immediately on warm plates. The pasta is delicious without grated cheese, but you can grate a bit of Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano over the top if you like.

Title: Fregola w/ Saffron & Potatoes
Description: From Gina di Palma

Ingredients.Name: Olive oil plus some for finishing (Extra Virgin)
Med. Waxy potatoes, peeled, and cubed ¼” approx. 8 oz.

Instructions: 1. Heat the oil over medium heat in a large, heavy, deep sauté or sauce pan with a tightly fitting lid. Add the shallots and smashed garlic and sauté briefly, moving them around the pan with a wooden spoon. Season with a pinch of salt and add the potatoes to the pan, coating them with the oil; sauté the potatoes for a minute, moving them around the pan often.

2. Add the broth and water to the pan, followed by the saffron threads, bay leaf, thyme sprigs, chili flakes, salt and pepper. Allow the mixture to come to a simmer, then lower the heat slightly and cover the pan.

3. After five to seven minutes, test the potatoes with the tip of a paring knife. They should begin to turn tender, cooked about halfway. Add the fregola to the pan and stir, bringing the liquid back to a simmer. Cover the pan and continue to cook the fregola, stirring frequently as the liquid evaporates, for 10 to 12 minutes.

4. Uncover the pan and test the fregola for doneness, remove and discard the bay leaf and thyme, and adjust the seasoning. If necessary, you can add more water to pan as the fregola continues to cook, a few tablespoons at a time. When the fregola is almost completely tender, add the frozen peas and lemon juice to the pan and simmer for three more minutes, stirring until the peas are tender, the fregola cooked and the liquid almost completely evaporated.

Title: Basic Pasta Dough
Description: This is a classic Italian recipe - 1 extra large egg for 1 cup flour.
