Instructions: Mound 3 1/2 C flour in the center of work surface. Make a well and add the eggs and olive oil. Using a fork, work your way around the well blending in the flour into the eggs. As you expand the well, keep pushing the flour up to maintain the well. When about half the flour is incorporated, you can hold it together and begin kneading. Remove any shaggy bits once you have a cohesive mass of dough. Continue kneading for 6-8 minutes after the mass comes together. Re-flour the surface as you go as needed to keep the dough from sticking. The dough will be somewhat sticky and it should be elastic. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Divide dough into several sections - usually about 8. Starting with one section, flatten so it will fit into the largest opening of the pasta maker. Run through and then fold into thirds. Run through again and repeat procedure 3 times. Lay the flattened dough over kitchen towels so they don't touch. Narrow down the opening and thin the pasta moving from one sheet to the next. Narrow down and continue until the pasta is the thickness you like it. Then run them through the cutting tool to the width you prefer.

Title: Roasted Fennel Pasta

Ingredients.Name: Canned Italian tomatoes, drained and lightly crushed

Instructions: Preheat the oven to 350*
Wash fennel. Trim off tops down to the white bulb. Trim bottom and any brown spots. Slice in quarters. Remove core and thinly slice each quarter. Save the greens.

In a large non-reactive roasting pan, toss the fennel with the onion, garlic, red pepper flakes and the olive oil until well coated. Salt and pepper. Roast for 20 minutes. Add tomatoes and bake for another 30 minutes. Meanwhile, boil water for the pasta and cook til al dente, finishing about the time the veggies are done. Reserve a little of the pasta water. Toss the pasta with the veggies and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Let rest a couple of minutes and if too dry, toss with a couple Tbsp. of the pasta water. garnish with the green feathery fronds of the fennel and serve with grated parmesan if you wish.
* I like to use thick pastas like bucatini or pici if I can get it but fettuccine works fine.

Title: Pasta with Greens

Ingredients.Name: Olive oil, plus more for dressing
Spinach or Arugula, cleaned and stemmed

Instructions: Heat water in a large saucepan or stockpot to boiling. Toss in pasta and 1 teaspoon salt and stir. While the pasta cooks, make the sauce. In a large skillet, heat olive oil and add the bacon. Cook until the bacon is no longer raw, beginning to brown. Add about ¼ cup of the pasta cooking water. Keep this simmering and adding more water if necessary until pasta is done. Drain and reserve more of the cooking liquid -- toss into the skillet coating all the pasta with the olive oil bacon sauce and add more water if too dry. Add all the greens and toss quickly until they are wilted. Add more water if necessary to keep loose. Then add a little more olive oil and some fresh pepper. Serve immediately with cheese on the side.

Title: Pasta Marinara
Description: During tomato season, you can substitute fresh tomatoes for an extra special fresh summer dish.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh basil, chopped and/or other fresh herbs
Garlic cloves, finely diced or more if you like
Olive oil, extra virgin plus a little for dressing

Instructions: Heat a large amount of water in a large saucepan or small stockpot. When water boils, add the pasta and add about 1 tsp of salt. Add the pasta and stir well. Cook for 10 minutes or as directed for the pasta. While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil and add the garlic in a sauté pan until translucent. Add the red pepper and then add the tomatoes. Heat until the sauce bubbles and add the herbs, continue simmering the sauce until pasta is ready. If it is too watery, raise the heat and reduce til thickened. Add sea salt to taste. Drain the pasta and toss into the skillet with the sauce. Cook for one to two minutes tossing to coat the pasta well. Remove from heat and drizzle fresh olive oil over and serve with cheese on the side.

** Substitute fresh tomatoes if in season. You will need about 6-8 tomatoes depending on the size. Blanch the tomatoes in boiling water for a minute or two and then cool under cold water. Slip off the skins as soon as you can handle them. Cut into 1/4s and squeeze out seeds gently. Chop roughly and substitute for the canned tomatoes.

Title: Bolognese

Ingredients.Name: canned Italian tomatoes, roughly chopped, with their juice

Instructions: 1. Use a heavy stainless steel or enameled cast-iron casserole, the deepest one you have. Put in the chopped onion, with all the oil and butter, and saute briefly over medium heat until just translucent. Add the garlic, celery and carrot and cook gently for 2 min.

2. Add the ground beef, crumbling it in the pot with a fork. Add 1 teaspoon salt, stir, and cook only until the meat has lost its raw, red color. Add the milk and on medium heat, toss the meat continuously in the milk until it evaporates. Add the wine, turn the heat up to medium high, and cook, stirring occasionally, until all the wine has evaporated.

3. Turn the heat down to medium, add the tomatoes and stir thoroughly. Add the nutmeg. When the tomatoes have started to bubble, turn the heat down until the sauce cooks at the laziest simmer, just an occasional bubble. Cook, uncovered, for a minimum of 21/2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. Taste and correct for salt and some fresh ground pepper.

Title: Cacio e Pepe (Pasta w/ Pecorino and Pepper)
Description: This makes 4 first courses or 2-3 larger portions.

Ingredients.Name: Whole wheat pasta, spaghetti or linguini

Instructions: Heat a large pot of water for the pasta. Gather together all the other ingredients. While the water is coming to a boil and is very hot, take some water from the pot and put in large pasta bowl to warm it well. In a small skillet, heat peppercorns until fragrant and place in a dish towel. Smash into uneven bits using the bottom of a saucepan. When water reaches a boil, add pasta and a teaspoon salt. Cook until al dente. Drain the pasta and add it to the pasta dish and toss in the pepper and a little of the pasta water - until it is creamy and all the strands are coated. Toss in the pecorino and toss really well. Serve immediately mounded on small plates or directly from the pasta bowl. Garnish with chopped parsley.

Ingredients.Name: Salt packed anchovy, boned, rinsed and soaked for a few minutes in warm water, and chopped

Title: Turkey Brine
Instructions: Remove giblet bag from turkey, along with any extra internal fat and pin feathers. Rinse well under cold tap water. Combine sugar, salt and 4 quarts of water in a large bowl. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Add remaining brine ingredients except for the remaining 1 1/2-1 3/4 gallons water. Double-bag two heavy-duty, unscented trash bags (not made of recycled materials), then put them in an ice chest that is large enough to hold the turkey. Place turkey in bags, pour in brine and remaining 1 1/2 gallons water -- there should be enough liquid to completely cover the bird. Press out air in bags; tightly close each bag separately. Keep turkey cold by piling bags of ice over and around the closed bags which will also help keep the turkey submerged. Brine for 12-24 hours.

Title: Turkey Burgers
Description: This came from Food and Wine and is a Spike Mendelsohn recipe, modified slightly by me.

Ingredients.Name: Sea salt and Fresh ground black pepper
Granny Smith or other tart apple, chopped fine

Instructions: In a skillet, heat 1 tbsp. oil, add the onion and cook over medium heat until very tender and just golden, about 25 minutes. While the onions are cooking, add 1 tbsp. oil to another skillet and heat over medium heat. When hot, but not smoking add the celery, apple, scallions and cook until tender about 5-8 minutes. Put into a medium large bowl along with the turkey and chipotles (use one if you like it mild, use two if you want it spicy). Stir in the parsley, 1 tsp. lemon zest and 2 tsp. salt and ¼ tsp. black pepper. Mix together well and shape into 4 patties. Wipe out the skillet used for the celery/apple mixture and add the last 1 tbsp. oil and heat until moderately high heat. Add the patties and cook about 10 minutes total, turning once. Moderate heat so they don’t burn.
If using, add 1 tsp. lemon zest, juice and thyme to the mayonnaise and stir well. Spread on the top of each bun. Set the burgers on the bottom bun and then top with the onions.

Title: Quail – Simple Grilled
Description: This is great with roasted polenta, warm beans or bitter greens.

Ingredients.Name: Herbs such as thyme and/or sage

Instructions: Heat a charcoal grill until it is glowing hot coals but no flames. While the grill is heating, rinse quail and pat dry. Rub with olive oil and fill the cavity with a few sprigs of herbs. Salt and pepper liberally.
When the fire is ready, grill quail about 4-6 minutes per side. Quail should be well done, not medium rare.

Title: Rabbit Braised in Red Wine ala Calabria

Ingredients.Name: Sea salt and fresh ground pepper
Bottle red wine, preferably hearty & rich

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In a large bowl, mix wine, vinegar and sugar and mix until sugar is dissolved.

Rinse rabbit, pat dry and salt and pepper liberally all over. Dredge in flour. Heat olive oil in large deep skillet that holds all pieces. When hot, but not smoking, add the rabbit pieces and brown on all sides until golden. Moderate heat so it doesn’t get too dark. Remove pieces to large 13x9 inch ceramic baking dish. Add garlic to hot skillet and brown lightly. Add the wine mixture and scrap up all the brown bits. Pour over rabbit and sprinkle herbs over the top. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 45 minutes. Remove foil and turn heat up to 450 and then cook another 25 minutes until reduced, browned and bubbly. Serve with crusty peasant bread.

Title: Chicken Fricassee with 2 Vinegars

Ingredients.Name: fresh farm chicken (3-4 lbs), cut into 8 serving pieces, at room temperature
freshly ground white pepper to taste

Instructions: 1. Liberally season the chicken on all sides with sea salt and white pepper.

2. In a deep skillet, combine the oil and butter, and heat over moderate heat. When the fats are hot but not smoking, add the chicken, skin side down, and brown until it turns an even golden color, about 5 minutes. Turn the pieces and brown them on the other side, 5 minutes more. Carefully regulate the heat to avoid scorching the skin. (This may have to be done in batches.) When all the pieces are browned, use tongs to transfer them to a platter.

3. Pour off and discard the fat in the skillet. Off the heat, add the two vinegars and deglaze the pan. Add the wine. Add the shallots and cook, covered, over low heat for 15 minutes. Transfer the chicken pieces to a large warmed platter and cover with aluminum foil to keep warm.

4. Add the tomato sauce and the stock to the skillet; stir to blend thoroughly. Add the cream and cook, uncovered over medium heat for 5 minutes. Return the chicken to the skillet, cover, and cook over low heat, turning the pieces from time to time to absorb the sauce, for about 10 minutes. Taste for seasoning, and serve.

Title: Chicken Marbella
Description: From Silver Palate

Ingredients.Name: head of garlic, peeled and finely pureed
capers with a bit of juice
coarse salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Italian parsley or fresh coriander (cilantro), finely chopped

Instructions: 1. In a large bowl combine chicken quarters, garlic, oregano, pepper and coarse salt to taste, vinegar, olive oil, prunes olives, capers and juice, and bay leaves. Cover and let marinate, refrigerated, overnight.
2. Preheat oven to 350F.
3. Arrange chicken in a single layer in one or two large, shallow baking pans and spoon marinade over it evenly. Sprinkle chicken pieces with brown sugar and pour white wine around them,
4. Bake for 50 min to 1 hour, basting frequently with pan juices. Chicken is done when thigh pieces, pricked with a fork at their thickest, yield clear yellow (rather than pink) juice.

5. With a slotted spoon transfer chicken, prunes, olives and capers to a serving platter. Moisten with a few spoonfuls of pan juices and sprinkle generously with parsley or cilantro. Pass remaining pan juices in a sauceboat.

6. To serve Chicken Marbella cold, cool to room temperature in cooking juices before transferring to a serving platter. If chicken has been covered and refrigerated, allow it to return to room temperature before serving. Spoon some of the reserved juice over chicken.

Title: Rabbit w/ Mustard & Favas
Description: This is my rustic version of a recipe by Joel Robuchon. I've kept the ideas the same but simplified it for the home cook who wants a great weekend meal. JR's version is more elegant and refined and perfect for guests or when you have more time for the details.

Ingredients.Name: Large fresh rabbit - 4 lbs or 2 smaller ones - cut into pieces (8 each)
French Dijon Mustard - imported best quality
Fresh fava beans, shelled, blanched and skinned
lightly smoked bacon or pancetta, julienned
Each - chopped minced parsley and fresh thyme
Fresh chanterelle mushrooms, cleaned and sliced
Chicken stock (fresh is best but canned is o.k.)
Fresh spring onions - white ends with about 2" of green (retain greens for another use)

Instructions: Heat a large skillet with the butter and olive oil. Coat each piece of rabbit in the mustard and generously season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with thyme leaves. When the skillet is hot but not smoking, add the rabbit and reduce to medium low. Cover and cook about 15 minutes per side until the rabbit is browned and tender.

While the rabbit is cooking prepare the onions and bacon. In a skillet, heat the butter and sugar and add the onions. Cover and sweat on medium low heat for 15-20 minutes until the onions are tender and the butter and juices are caramelized. Pour in a bowl scraping well. In the same skillet, add the butter and the julienned bacon. Heat over medium heat until the bacon is cooked and golden but not crispy or dry. Remove from heat and save.

When rabbit is cooked, remove to a plate or large platter and cover. Increase the heat under the skillet and add the chicken stock and deglaze, scraping up all the browned bits. Cook until reduced by about 1/3. Add back the rabbit and coat all over with sauce. A few minutes before serving, add the bacon and onions and blend to combine well. Heat until hot and toss in the fresh favas, let them warm for a minute. Taste for seasoning and add salt and pepper if necessary. Pour into serving dish and sprinkle with the fresh herbs.

*** Optional - For a special treat when chanterelles are available, saute them in the olive oil while the onions are cooking. When tender, about 3 to 5 minutes, remove from heat and reserve. Add to the rabbit right before the herbs by sprinkling over the rabbit. Do not stir into sauce.

Title: Duck confit
Description: This is a classic confit. It keeps well in the fridge for about one month. Just pull out a couple legs at a time for a quick meal or cook it all for a small dinner party. Don't forget you need at least one, preferably two weeks to age the duck in the fat plus two days to marinate the duck before cooking.
Instructions: Trim excess fat off duck legs, make a small incision at base of leg and cut tendon but leave skin intact. Sprinkle each leg liberally with salt, the thyme and bay leaves, and crack/grind fresh pepper over each. Cover and refrigerate overnight.

Melt the duck fat in a large, wide, heavy saute pan at least 3" deep. Slip the legs into the hot fat gently to prevent splattering. They should be completely submerged. Adjust and add more fat if necessary. Simmer very slowly, do not boil, the fat for about 1 and 1/2 hours.

Remove the legs to a large glass or ceramic dish. Ladle the fat over the duck until it is completely covered by approx. 1 inch of fat. Cool and then cover and refrigerate. Use one week later for best results.

To serve, remove ducks from fat, scraping off excess fat. Heat a skillet on medium high heat and saute the ducks skin side down until the skin is crispy and well browned about 5 minutes. Turn the ducks and cook for about 4 or 5 minutes more until ducks are heated through and they have thrown off most of their fat . Drain quickly on paper towels and serve.

Title: Steamed Chicken
Description: This makes a tender and moist meat to be used for all purposes when pre-cooked chicken is called for.

Ingredients.Name: Sea salt, coarse or Kosher salt

Instructions: Wash chicken and clean interior. Rub salt all over the chicken, set on a plate and cover tightly with plastic wrap. Keep refrigerated for 3-4 days. Wash off all salt and set on a small pie plate that will fit in the pot you plan to steam it in. Set in a steamer or on a rack in a large pot with a couple inches of water. Bring to a boil and set chicken over water, not in. cover and let steam for 45 minutes. Check juices in the pan - should be clear and cooked. Skin will yellow. This is the moist and tender chicken to use in salads or sliced simply with a green sauce or for delicious sandwiches.

Title: Mustard Chicken
Description: This is a recipe adapted from a recipe by Lydie Marshall that I found in a magazine. It is good with a simple starch like homemade noodles/pasta or potatoes.

Ingredients.Name: Plain Yogurt (whole milk makes a creamier sauce but low or nonfat is o.k.)
Free-range fresh chicken, approx. 4 lbs., cut into 8 parts and trimmed or all fat

Instructions: Preheat oven to 400*

In a large baking dish, mix the yogurt and mustard. Add salt & pepper and thyme. Turn the chicken in the mixture until well coated. Bake uncovered for 45 minutes or until chicken is golden brown Remove chicken to a platter. Blend the sauce in a blender or food processor to make smooth and serve immediately in a sauceboat on the side.

Title: Duck with Cherries
Description: This recipe is from a Saveur Magazine article on duck from Sonoma County and the Bay Wolf Restaurant in Oakland.
Instructions: Preheat oven to 375*

Heat stock and 1 Cup wine in a large pot and keep at a simmer. In a saute pan, melt duck fat and saute shallots until just browned 5-7 min. Add 2 Cups stock and 1 Cup of the bing cherries and 1/2 C of the dried cherries, thyme and pepper. Simmer until reduced by half, approx. 15 minutes. Add 2 more cups of stock and reduce by half again. Repeat until all stock is used and it is thick and velvety. This takes about 2 hours total.
While the stock is in its first simmer, set duck legs, seasoned with salt and pepper, skin side up on a rack set in a backing dish in the top third of oven. Roast for 1 hour and pour off fat.

Bring remaining wine, cherries and dried cherries to a boil in a saucepan. Pour over duck and return to oven. Roast for 1/2 hour more until the duck is golden red. Remove duck from braising liquid. Strain out cherries and add to reserved sauce. Re-warm sauce if necessary and spoon over duck.

Title: Roast Duck
Description: This recipe is so easy and it renders all the fat from the duck leaving it tender with crispy skin.
Instructions: Preheat Oven to 300*
Rinse duck w/ cold water and pat dry. Remove any extra fat in cavity or around opening. Season cavity w/ salt, rub w/ garlic and stuff cavity with a handful of thyme branches.

Pierce duck skin all over with a sharp knife - do this carefully so you don't cut the flesh. The slits will allow the fat to drain off so cover the whole duck. Place duck on a rack in a shallow roasting pan with the breast up. Roast for 1 hour and remove duck and re-pierce the skin. Pour off fat from pan and turn duck breast side down. Return to oven and roast 1 more hour. Repeat piercing, turning and return to oven again. Repeat whole procedure for 2 more hours so duck cooks with the breast up every other hour.
Remove duck from oven after four hours and turn heat up to 350*.
Season duck skin all over with salt and pepper and roast one hour more. Let duck rest 20 minutes before carving.

Title: Roasted Rabbit in Mustard Sauce
Description: This recipe is based on traditional burgundian rabbit with wine sauce - but it is simple and delicious.

Ingredients.Name: 4-4 1/2 lb. rabbit, cut up 6 or 8 pieces

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375%.
Season rabbit pieces generously with salt and pepper.

Melt butter and oil together in large oven-proof skillet over medium heat. Place rabbit into pan and coat with butter/oil mixture. Add onions to skillet. Roast rabbit for approx. 30 minutes until lightly golden brown. Cover with lid or foil and roast for another 20 minutes.

Place skillet on top of stove. Turn off oven. Remove rabbit and onions to a platter or shallow open dish. Cover with foil and return to still warm oven. Pour wine into skillet and turn heat to medium-high, and deglaze all the brown bits on the bottom of the pan. Continue cooking and stirring until liquid reduces about 1/4 to 1/3. Whisk in mustard and 1/2 cup crème fraiche or sour cream. Taste and adjust seasoning. Add more sour cream/crème fraiche to taste. Simmer very gently for a couple minutes and pour over the rabbit. Serve immediately.

Title: Coq au Vin
Description: This is a traditional coq au vin which would be made with rooster or capon in France - use capon if you can get it. It is also traditional to serve this with toasted "croutons" of French bread.

Ingredients.Name: Large Roasting chicken - cut into 10 pieces
Leg thigh combinations cut into 4 pieces
Fresh wild mushrooms (chanterelles & shitakes) or white mushrooms if you can't get the wild -- clean them gently with a brush and slice.
Large yellow onions - peeled and chopped
Sea Salt and Fresh Pepper ground
Bouquet Garni of parsley, thyme, black peppercorns tied in cheesecloth

Instructions: Marinate Chicken at least 24 hours in advance of cooking:

Combine chicken, onions, shallots, carrots, garlic and bouquet garni in large non-reactive bowl or pot. Pour wine over and mix around so all the chicken is coated with wine. Cover tightly and Refrigerate.
Prepare Chicken:

Remove chicken from marinade and dry well. Heat oil in very large casserole or deep saute pan with lid over medium high heat. Add chicken a few pieces at a time and brown on all sides - approx. 10 minutes each batch. Remove to a large platter or bowl. When the chicken is done, remove all but 2-3 Tbs of the oil and return to the heat. Add the flour, stirring constantly for 2 minutes. Return chicken to casserole and add cognac. Remove from heat and ignite the cognac - carefully. Return casserole to heat, add marinade and scrape up the browned bits and flour. Reduce heat to low and simmer, partially covered for about 1 1/2 hours or longer until the chicken is tender.
Prepare Sauce:

Remove chicken from pan. Strain sauce through a sieve and remove bouquet garni and solids. Return sauce to casserole. Put 1/2 cup of sauce in small bowl and stir in cocoa powder. Whisk into the sauce in casserole. Reduce heat to low and return chicken to the casserole. Cover partially and cook gently. In a small saute pan, saute pork over medium heat until golden and fat is rendered. Remove to paper towels. Remove all fat but 2 Tbs in the pan and add the mushrooms. Cook over medium heat until the mushrooms are golden. Drain and add mushrooms and the salt pork to chicken and serve.

Title: Rabbit w/ Parsnips
Description: This is a take on a Mario Batali recipe which originally came from a winery in Chianti – I’ve modified it slightly.

Ingredients.Name: Vin Santo is the best but you can substitute some other dessert wines – just don’t make it too sweet – you can balance it with some regular white wine
Tomatoes – canned o.k. – chopped – but use fresh if you have them
Chicken stock – homemade is best but if you use canned, just use low sodium

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.

Season the rabbit well with salt and pepper. Dredge the rabbit in the flour. In a large heavy bottom casserole heat the olive oil and when hot, add as many rabbit pieces as fit comfortably and cook until golden brown on all sides. Repeat with remaining rabbit, setting the cooked ones aside.

When the rabbit is all browned, add the leeks and parsnips to the pan stirring well and cook until also lightly browned. Add the wine, tomatoes and chicken stock and bring them to a boil, add the rabbit, submerging in the liquid. If you need more liquid, add a little more stock or water. Cover with foil or a tight lid and put in over for about 1 hour and 15 minutes or until the rabbit is falling off the bone. Check the rabbit after about 45 minutes and add a little liquid if it looks a little dry.
Remove rabbit from pan into serving dish and adjust seasoning of the sauce and pour over the rabbit.

Title: Duck Breasts Sautéed
Description: These are wonderful just plain but you can also dress them with a little balsamic, or any number of simple glazes.
Instructions: Trim the fat from the breasts. Cut the skin in several place with 1 inch slices through the fat but not into the flesh. Salt and pepper generously. Heat a skillet preferably non-stick and place the breasts skin-side down. Cook for 10 minutes on one side and then 3 minutes on the other. The skin should be deep golden brown and crispy. Let rest for a few minutes covered loosely for foil and serve.

Title: Roasted Chicken w/ Bread Salad
Description: This is Judy Rodger’s famous dish from Zuni Café. The best chicken dish ever.

Ingredients.Name: Whole chicken, preferably organic or free range and not frozen
Frisee, head, cleaned very well and cut into 2 inch slices across the leaves
Head lettuce such as red leaf, cleaned and shredded
Loaf of country style French bread
Garlic cloves, peeled and chopped fine
Green onions, trimmed and sliced thinly, white part and a couple inches of green

Instructions: The chicken is best if you can clean it and salt it the day before, but if you don’t have time, don’t worry.
Take the chicken out of the fridge at least 3 hours before cooking it, clean it and salt it liberally outside and inside.
Heat oven to 475 degrees. Use a large deep skillet or pot with plenty of room around it for the chicken. It needs to be able to go on the stove top as well as in the oven.

While the oven is heating, cut the crusts off the loaf of bread and cut into about 4 or 5 large chunks. Coat lightly all over with oil and place on a baking sheet. Place in the oven and toast for about 5 minutes, turn over and cook until the edges are beginning to get dark. Remove from oven and let cool until you can handle it. Tear the bread into uneven sizes catching all the crumbs into a large baking dish.
In a small sauté pan, toast the pine nuts over medium high heat until they begin to get golden. Remove from heat and reserve.
Place the currants in a small dish and add the 1 tsp of red wine vinegar. Add 1 Tbsp. hot water. Let plump for 15 minutes. Drain.
Toss the pine nuts with the bread and then add the plumped currents sprinkled all over.
In the small sauté pan, heat 1 Tbsp. olive oil and add garlic and green onions. Cook until the garlic is translucent. Then toss the garlic and green onions with the bread mixture.

Pat the chicken dry inside and out with paper towels. Heat the large skillet for the chicken until quite hot and add the chicken. This prevents the skin from sticking. Put the skillet in the oven in the center rack. Cook for 20 minutes.
Be careful of splattering hot fat while you remove the chicken and turn it upside down (breast side down) in the skillet and return to the oven. Cook for 10 minutes.

Remove again and flip breast side up. Cook again for 10 minutes. If the chicken is particularly large, you may need to cook it a few minutes longer. Remove and put the chicken on a plate and cover loosely with foil so that it will keep warm.
Place the bread salad in the oven while the chicken rests.

In a small bowl blend the remaining olive oil with the white wine vinegar until it is fully blended. Add a little salt and pepper. Toss in a large bowl with the frisee and lettuce leaves. Test for seasoning and add more salt and pepper if needed.

Drain the fat from the skillet but keep the golden bits in the bottom. Place back on the stove and add about ¼ cup water mixing and melting the brown bits over high heat. If it begins to stick to the bottom of the pan, add more water to keep it from burning. When the chicken has rested for 5-10 minutes, cut the chicken into wings, drumsticks, thighs and cut each breast into 2 pieces. Arrange the salad on a large platter. Toss the hot bread salad in with the lettuce and place the chicken around the edge. Sprinkle the cooking juices from the chicken around the salad and bread.
Serve with the remaining cooking juices from the chicken.

Title: Chicken w/ Pancetta & Olives
Description: This is super easy and delicious. You can also use solely legs and thighs and make this for a crowd. It is a Gourmet magazine recipe from Tony Oltrani.

Ingredients.Name: chickens, 2 ½-3 lbs each, cut into 12 pieces each
coarse salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Slices pancetta (1/4” thick) cut into 1” pieces

Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 450F.
2. In a large bowl combine chicken pieces,oil, thyme, rosemary, pepper flakes and salt, rub into chicken and set aside.
3. Arrange chicken skin side up in a single layer in a large (17 x 11 in) sheet pan with deep sides or a baking dish. Sprinkle the pancetta over the chicken and scatter garlic around the pieces.

4. Roast approx. 20 minutes or until the chicken begins to brown. Pour wine around the chicken and roast 8 min. more. Scatter olives over the dish and bake for about 15-20 minutes more until skin is entirely golden and the chicken is cooked through. Let rest for about 10 minutes before serving.

Title: Summer Peach & Bacon Salad
Description: This is easy to adjust for size of group. It’s my re-working of a recipe by Linton Hopkins

Ingredients.Name: Cayenne Pepper + more if you like it spicy
Sweet yellow onion sliced into thick 1” sliced rounds
Olive oil for brushing on fruit and onions
Mixed Herbs – Mint and parsley plus other bright flavored summer herbs such as chives, sorrel, cilantro, etc. – chopped well.
Ripe peaches that are still firm – cut into wedges about ½”
Champagne vinegar or other mild lt.vinegar
Sea salt and fresh ground pepper for the sauce

Instructions: Preheat oven to 325.

In a small blender or food processor, blend the cottage cheese, buttermilk and yogurt til smooth. Mix in the herbs, 1 tsp vinegar and then salt and pepper to taste. At this point, you can either leave the herbs suspended in the white dressing which is pretty or you can blend again to fully incorporate. The dressing is then a lovely pale green. Adjust the acid by adding a bit more vinegar if needed.
Line baking sheet with parchment. Lay bacon slices on parchment and bake for 25-30 mins until golden and fully cooked. Let cool.

While the bacon is cooking, light the grill for the onions and peaches. Brush the onions with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Place on the grill in a medium hot area and cover, turning (and moving frequently to prevent burning) until browned and softened, about 10 mins. Transfer to a plate. Then brush the peaches with a little oil and grill peaches until golden grill marks on both sides, about 2 mins. Transfer to plate with onions. Cool.

In a large bowl, toss the onions, peaches and bacon broken into 2” pieces. Drizzle with the dressing and serve. You can also toss this together with the dressing gently to coat. It’s prettier with the dressing drizzled over though.

Title: Marinated Zucchini Salad

Ingredients.Name: Sea salt (flaky – finishing salt) best quality

Instructions: Chop the walnuts very coarsely into about 4 pieces each. Cut the mozzarella into about 1/4s for bocconcini or about the same size. Blend the first 3 ingredients together and toss with about 1 Tbsp. of olive oil. All the salad should be lightly coated and fragrant with the oil. If not, add more until you taste it and it has a good olive oil flavor but isn’t too oily – so taste as you go. Chill for at least one hour together.
Before serving, add the chopped parsley and season with the salt and pepper. Mound gently in the center of a plate to serve.

Title: Fava Bean & Pecorino Salad
Description: This is a traditional Italian dish mostly used as an element on an antipasti platter. It is also good as a small side dish to grilled meats.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh unshelled fava beans (about 2 cups shelled)
Pecorino - soft, and cut into small cubes about the size of the fava beans
Red Wine vinegar - very high quality

Instructions: Shell beans. Blanch and remove the inner skin. In a large bowl, toss the beans with the remaining ingredients. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve in small portions - the cheese makes this a rich dish.

Title: Winter Salad w/ Smoked Trout

Ingredients.Name: Ruby grapefruits or substitute 4 blood oranges
Course sea salt & fresh ground pepper
White wine, champagne or other light vinegar
Smoked trout, torn into small pieces or cubed

Instructions: Slice peel off grapefruits and slice out each section between membranes. Catch all juices into a small bowl. Put grapefruit slices in another bowl. In the bowl with the juice, stir in the vinegar and shallot. Let macerate for 30 minutes. In another bowl whisk olive oil with crème fraiche. Break apart cleaned endives and slice large leaves into two or three smaller pieces on a diagonal. Just before serving, whisk the crème fraiche into the juice mixture with a pinch or two of salt and then toss 1/2 of the dressing with the endives. Arrange Mache leaves decoratively over the endives in bowls or on small plates. Season greens with salt and pepper. Arrange grapefruit and then sprinkle trout pieces on each. Drizzle each with the remaining dressing.

Title: Summer Melon & Tomato Salad

Ingredients.Name: Summer tomatoes, preferably early girl or green zebra
Sea salt and fresh ground pepper

Instructions: Heat a small skillet with the cumin until fragrant and beginning to darken. Put into bowl for salad. Add the vinegar and 1 tbsp of the oil and the jalapeno. Stir and let rest. Heat the pine nuts in the same skillet until they get golden. Chop fine and set aside. Cut melon into ½ inch cubes and same with the tomatoes. Toss into the cumin vinaigrette. Chop the cilantro and sprinkle over the salad and toss gently. Taste and add a little more olive oil, salt and pepper to taste.

Title: Caesar Salad
Description: The freshest simplest Caesar...always good! And no egg.

Ingredients.Name: Salt pack anchovy, best quality, bone removed, and rinsed well.
Extra virgin olive oil, plus a little more to taste
Parmesian Reggiano for grating over the salad

Instructions: Wash and trim lettuce. Tear into oversized pieces and place in a large open salad bowl.

In a mortar and pestle or a mini processor, chop/grind the anchovy with the garlic. Add 2 Tbsp. olive oil and process or blend until beginning to emulsify. Place in a small bowl and add the juice of the 1/2 lemon, the vinegar and the remaining oil. Taste and add a little more oil if too acidic.
Toss lettuce with dressing and sprinkle with salt and pepper and toss again.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Using a vegetable scraper, scrap curls of parmesan all over the salad.
Crumble croutons over salad. Serve.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh tuna steaks, preferably 1" or more thick
French filet beans or blue lake beans, washed and tipped, cut into 3-4" lengths
Small-Medium size Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed clean
Extra Virgin Olive Oil, best quality for dressing
large Chiogga beets or other veggie

Title: Sorrel Sauce
Description: I grow my own sorrel in the garden. It is great because it grows no matter how little attention I give it. One plant grows enough to keep us in sorrel all year. This is great over salmon or other rich fish.

Ingredients.Name: Sea salt and fresh ground pepper

Instructions: Wash sorrel and remove center stem. Cut into ribbons. Chop shallot. Heat butter in saute pan and add shallot. Cook until wilted and then add the sorrel. Cook about 5 minutes until wilted and beginning to get tender. Add white wine and turn heat to high to reduce wine until it is still moist but almost gone. Add cream, reduce heat to medium low and bring back to simmer. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

Title: Tarragon Oil
Description: Use this to flavor fish or grilled chicken.
Instructions: Put herbs and oil in a blender and pulse for about 10 seconds until blended. Add pinch of salt and vinegar and pulse again briefly. Strain through a fine mesh sieve and discard solids. Store in refrigerator for no more than 1 day or freeze.

Title: Carmelized Salmon

Ingredients.Name: Fresh Salmon filets, preferably wild, cut into 3 or 4 portion sizes
Jalapeno chili, thinly sliced (seeds removed if you don’t want it too spicy)

Instructions: Marinate the Salmon: Blend the garlic, lime, soy, 1 Tbsp. oil, honey and tahini or seeds. Place the fish with ½ the marinade in a zip lock bag, seal and let marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes. Remove fish from marinade.

Preheat broiler. When hot, pour the remaining oil into a medium skillet just big enough to hold the scallions and fish, lay the scallions in one layer and broil for about 3 minutes until just beginning to char. Lay fish on top of scallions, drizzle with the ½ the remaining marinade and broil for 6 minutes. Remove from oven, drizzle with the remaining marinade and top with the chili slices. Broil another 2 minutes or until the fish is nicely carmelized and the edges charred. Sprinkle with extra sesame seeds if desired. Serve immediately.

Title: Shrimp in Fish Sauce Caramel
Description: Adapted from Food and Wine magazine. Super easy and delicious. Serve with fresh or cooked greens.

Ingredients.Name: Fish Sauce – Any Asian type o.k. - good quality ones are best

Instructions: *Note – Clean shrimp, leaving on the tails and shells. It is also o.k. to remove the shells if you prefer but leaving the shells on keeps them a bit more succulent.

In a small skillet or saucepan, heat sugar and 1 Tbsp. water over medium high heat until sugar dissolves. Continue cooking, watching carefully until sugar is carmelized to a nice amber color – swirl pan to ensure evenness. Remove from heat and immediately add the fish sauce, soy sauce and 2 Tablespoons of water. Stir until caramel is incorporated and set aside.

Heat a large skillet over high heat til very hot and add the ½ the oil, ½ the garlic and ½ the pepper flakes. (You may need a bit more oil if your skillet is very large.) Toss in ½ the shrimp and season with salt and pepper. The shrimp should be in an even layer. Cook quickly over high heat and turning the shrimp to cook evenly. Lower heat a bit if the garlic begins to get dark. When the shrimp is cooked, they should be a little crispy too, remove from pan scraping into a large bowl or onto a plate. Repeat with the remaining oil, garlic and pepper and shrimp.
Return all shrimp to skillet, on medium high heat and add the fish caramel sauce – toss to evenly coat with the sauce and to make sure all shrimp are heated through.
Serve.

Serve over bitter greens such as watercress, arugula, or chicories. Also delicious served with sautéed spinach or chard and sprinkled with fresh herbs such as mint, basil, and cilantro (a mix is great).

Ingredients.Name: Halibut fillet pieces about 4-5 ounces each

Title: Grilled Paella
Description: This can be done in the oven or on the stove too but it will lack that lovely smokey taste. You’ll need to adjust cooking times for each method. The best thing about this is how easy it is to adjust for the number of people. All the prep can be done in advance and then it cooks very quickly on the grill.

Ingredients.Name: Cherry tomatoes, cut in half, per person or chopped fresh tomato
Chicken Stock per person – or water*
Optional – White wine – substitute up to 1 Cup for stock
Fresh sweet peas, shelled, per person
Red pepper flakes or a little more if you like it spicy (this is also a question of how spicy your chorizo is)
Chorizo per person, small cubes or slices, or more if you prefer the added flavor
Clams or mussels per person, cleaned
Large fresh prawns per person, deveined & shelled – save shells
Red Pepper, sweet, chopped, per person
Fresh squid per person, cleaned, and cut into pieces
Olive oil per person – adjusted to size of pan

Instructions: De-sand the clams in 1 Tbsp. salt per quart of water for 3-4 hours.

Clean and prep the shrimp. Reserve shells and add to the stock in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil and then reduce to simmer and cook for 15 minutes to extract the flavors. Strain and reserve the stock in the saucepan.

Prep all the vegetables and have ready in small dishes as the paella comes together quickly. When ready, heat the charcoal until the coals are very hot but beginning to ash around the edges. Meanwhile, rewarm the stock with the saffron and wine, if using.

Place the paella pan on the grill with the oil and heat til just beginning to sizzle. Add the chorizo and stir until the chorizo oil flavors the olive oil. Add the onions, peppers and garlic. Cook briefly until the onions are translucent. Add the rice and stir to coat with the oil and continue stirring for a couple minutes until you can see the edges of the rice turning a bit translucent absorbing the oil. Add the stock to the pan and stir for a minute or two. The stock mixture should boil, and after that, stop stirring. If the fire is a little too hot, move the pan off the heat a bit and cover the grill to dampen the fire. Turn the pan every few minutes so it doesn’t cook too unevenly if it isn’t centered. When the rice is almost cooked but there still is some liquid in the pan, you’re ready to add the clams or mussels. If the rice dries out too quickly from too hot a fire, just add an 1/8 cup of water at a time to maintain the liquid so the rice will continue to cook. When it’s ready, tuck the clams or mussels around into the rice. Cover the grill. When they are almost completely open, about 3 mins., tuck the shrimp around the clams, sprinkle the peas on top, and cook until the shrimp are no longer translucent but nice and pink. You may need to turn them. If using, add the squid and cook for one minute until it is just cooked – don’t overcook or it will be tough. Another good way to do this is to put the squid on some foil on another part of the grill over hot coals to cook really quickly and then toss on top of the paella. The rice should caramelize on the bottom of the pan but not burn, so watch it carefully. Let it rest for about 5 mins. And sprinkle with parsley.

Title: Ginger Shrimp Stir-fry

Ingredients.Name: Fresh Ginger, cut into ¼” long fine julienne
Steamed white or brown rice for serving
Subtitute Chinese chili garlic sauce for the fresh garlic and chili flakes – about 1 tsp.
Large shrimp, feet removed and deveined

Instructions: In a small bowl, put in cornstarch and then whisk in the soy sauce, white wine and ¼ Cup chicken stock.

In a large heavy skillet, heat oil until hot and add the ginger and fry for about 1 minute. Add garlic and chili flakes and toss until garlic is tender. Add the snow peas and cook for about 1 minute, until just beginning to cook through. Add the shrimp and continue to toss over the high heat until the shrimp is almost cooked about 1 minute. Add scallions and toss for about 1 minute. Add the cornstarch mixture and mix well. Cook until the shrimp are fully cooked and the sauce is thickened and glistening. If too dry, add a little more of the stock and toss another minute or so. Serve immediately.
** If you prefer not to handle the shrimp and get messy, use the medium shelled shrimp but you’ll need to cook it about half the time, being careful not to overcook.
Serve with steamed rice.

Title: Shrimp Steamed for Salpicon
Instructions: Cut the lime in half and juice it into about 3” of water in the bottom of a medium large saucepan (3.5-4 qts). Put the lime skins, pepper, chili and bay leaves in the water and boil for about 5 min until the water is fully flavored with the spices. Add the shrimp and boil gently for about 2-3 minutes until the shrimp is just barely cooked through. Strain and let cool until just luke and then cover and chill in the fridge until cold, about 1-2 hours or overnight.

Title: Grilled Shrimp & Chorizo
Description: This can be done as an cocktail hors d’oeuvres using little skewers or as a first course using a couple to a skewer.

Ingredients.Name: Medium large shrimp – about 20-25 per pound, peel and devein
Sea Salt and fresh ground black pepper
Skewers – if using bamboo, soak in water for 30 minutes before putting on the grill

Instructions: Prepare the grill to hot but not flaming coals.

Slice the chorizo into ¼ - inch disks. Wrap the shrimp around the chorizo and secure with a skewer. Continue until all are wrapped. You can put several on a larger skewer or use cocktail size skewers. Drizzle the olive oil over the shrimp and season with salt and pepper.Grill for about 1 minute per side or until shrimp is opaque.
You can also get good results by roasting – heat oven to 400 degrees. Place skewers on a baking sheet and place in hot oven.Bake for 7-9 minutes, until shrimp becomes opaque.

Title: Cod Basquaise
Instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy bottomed pan. Add onion and sweat until tender over medium-low heat. Add garlic and continue cooking until tender; add the ham and peppers. When the peppers are soft, add the tomatoes and simmer, stirring often, over low heat for 20 minutes. Add the red wine and reduce over medium heat until most of the liquid had evaporated. Stir in the chopped parsley and season to taste with salt, pepper and Espelette pepper. This can be done the day before.Heat a griddle or a griddle pan until very hot, add the canola oil. Season the codfish on both sides with salt and pepper. Add the codfish to the griddle or pan and sauté until the fish is golden brown on the bottom along with the thyme and garlic, about 6-8 minutes, lowering the heat if necessary to prevent from burning. Turn the fish over and finish cooking the fish for another 2-3 minutes, until a metal skewer can be easily inserted into the fish and, when left in for 5 seconds, feels just warm when touched to the lip.
Meanwhile, heat the basquaise until hot. Spoon basquaise onto plates, place sautéed cod in the center and serve immediately.

Title: Sicilian Baked Cod
Description: This is a recipe from Gina di Palma.

Ingredients.Name: Cod fillet or other firm white fish, cut in 3 -4 portions
Black olives, oil cured, cracked and pitted

Instructions: 1. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

2. Cut the onion into quarters, then cut the quarters crosswise and separate the layers to create wide, square slices. In a sauté pan, heat 1 tablespoon of olive and add the onion. Season with salt and pepper, and sauté over low heat until the onion has wilted and started to turn translucent; be careful not to let it brown. Add the red wine vinegar to the pan and shake it briefly, then transfer everything to the bottom of a medium-sized baking dish.

3. Wipe the pan with a paper towel to clean it, then place it back over low heat and add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil. Add the anchovy paste and stir with a wooden spoon to dissolve the paste into the oil. Dump the breadcrumbs into the pan and stir to completely coat them with the oil. Transfer the breadcrumbs to a small bowl to cool slightly.
4. Wash the herbs, pat them dry, and finely chop them. Add them to the bowl with breadcrumbs, and season everything with a small pinch of salt and a few grinds of black pepper.

5. Lay the portioned fish on top of the onions and season with a bit more salt and pepper. Distribute the breadcrumb-herb mixture evenly on top of the fish. Add the white wine or water to the pan and scatter the olives around the dish.

6. Bake the fish for 15 to 20 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fish; it should be cooked through but still moist; check the pan after 10 minutes and add a bit more water or wine if necessary.
7. Serve immediately, with the some of the onions, olives and pan juices spooned alongside the fish.

Title: Squid Saute w/ Sweet Tomatoes
Description: This is great served with grilled bread or broiler toasted peasant bread.
Instructions: IF the squid is large or thick, cut into ¼ inch rings. If small and thin, the pieces can be more like ½”. Heat a large skillet and add the olive oil. When very hot but not smoking, add the squid and toss for about 1 minute until just opaque. Remove to a bowl and add the garlic and tomatoes to the skillet and sauté for a few minutes or until the tomatoes pop and render some juice into the pan and the garlic is cooked. Add the squid back and toss quickly. Sprinkle with the parsley and serve immediately with grilled bread or broiled toasts.

Title: Salmon w/ Lime Sauce
Description: This is a recipe from the Fredy Girardet cookbook from the mid-1980's.

Ingredients.Name: Fresh salmon filets, cut into 4 slices, approx. 2" wide

Instructions: Heat oven to 350 degrees.
Make two large pouches for salmon by taking a 2' length of paper for each and fold in center toward you. Lay salmon on bottom piece and cover with top piece.

Melt butter and remove from heat. Add grated zest and ginger. Drizzle over the salmon. Fold the pouches by starting at one side and folding over edges to seal working from fold to the open end. Fold the other side in the same way and twist the open end tightly shut. It will look a little like a heart. Place in oven on a baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes.

While the salmon is cooking, make the sauce. Heat 1/2 Tbsp. of the butter in a small skillet and saute the shallots until just translucent. Add the lime juice and 2 Tbsp. Port and cook until reduced by half and a little thick. Add the cream and bring just to a boil. Lower heat and gently whisk in remaining butter. Season with salt, pepper and cayenne. When the fish is done, and you are ready to sauce it, add the ginger.
Open the pouches and slip the fish with its juices onto a plate. Drizzle a little sauce over each fillet and around the plate. Drizzle a little bit of Port over each and serve.

Title: Christmas Roasted Crab
Description: I like the crab flavor to stand out so I don't usually use the garlic although it is traditional. Garlic lovers will adore it though.
Instructions: In a large soup kettle, that holds about 2 gals or more of water. Bring to boil, add the salt, lemon juice and vinegar. Drop in 2 crabs one at a time and cook for about 10 minutes after the water returns to a boil. Remove and repeat with remaining crabs. Drain and let cool. Crack and clean crabs.

Preheat oven to 500*. Place crab pieces in large roasting pan and pour the butter, lemon juice and oil over them tossing to coat. Add garlic if using. Roast 10-15 minutes until hot and shells are very shiny. Baste with the juices and serve immediately.

Title: Lemon Beurre Blanc Scallops

Ingredients.Name: Sea Scallops, fresh, about 18 or 3 per person

Instructions: Garnish:

Cut the white and tender green parts of the leek into 2" pieces. Split and rinse well. Julienne the leeks into the finest ribbons. Fry in the oil until crispy. Drain on paper towels. Cover and hold for no more than a few hours.
Shell peas and blanch in boiling salted water until tender about 1 1/2 min. to 2 min. Drain and cool quickly with cold water to stop cooking.
Beurre Blanc:

Heat 2 tsp. of oil in small saucepan. Add shallots and cook over low until tender. Add lemon juice and wine and cook until reduced to about 2 tablespoons. Strain and discard solids. Return to heat and add cream. Bring to a boil and remove from heat immediately and whisk in the cold butter, a tablespoon at a time, until fully incorporated. Return to a very low heat and keep warm. Stir in vanilla and season with salt and pepper.
Scallops:

Remove the foot of the scallops and dry well. Heat a large, heavy skillet over high heat. Add a thin coating of olive oil to pan. Season scallops with salt and pepper and add to the very hot pan but not smoking. Do not move scallops until they are brown, about 2 minutes. Turn over and cook again for 2 min. Don't overcook.
Assemble by putting a small amount of sauce on plate. Add scallops, sprinkle peas around scallops and top them with the leeks. Use flavored oil for extra flavor.

Title: Oil Poached Halibut
Description: In winter, you can substitute or add root vegetables to the potatoes. In summer, you can add fresh chopped herbs to the finishing and sprinkle with sweet peas just gently steamed over the entire dish.

Ingredients.Name: Sea salt and fresh ground pepper
Yellow finish or Yukon gold potatoes

Instructions: Smash and chop garlic. Clean and trim fennel, and slice into ¼” slices lengthwise. Trim some of the best fronds from fennel and reserve a few for garnish and a couple for the veggies. Halve the tomatoes.
Clean and slice potatoes in ¼ inch slices. In a medium pot, boil gently with a few pinches of salt until tender about 10 minutes. Drain and reserve covered to stay moist in a wide, deep dish.

In a large pot or deep skillet, at least 3 inches deep, layer the fennel, sprinkle over the garlic and a few fennel fronds. Nestle the tomato halves around the fennel cut side up. Pour over the oil so it just covers or comes up to the top of the veggies. Tuck the zest and bay leaf around and sprinkle the sugar and a couple pinches salt and pepper over the veggies. Poach the veggies in the oil on medium simmer for 10-15 minutes or until tender. Transfer with wire or slotted spoon over the potatoes, cover with foil and keep warm.

Salt and pepper the fish. Add the fish to the oil, and lay a piece of parchment over the fish and poach very gently for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let fish continue to cook for about 10-15 minutes until completely cooked and still warm.
Lay the fish over the veggies, and discard oil. Sprinkle fresh chopped fennel fronds, fresh cracked pepper and a few sprinklings of good sea salt, preferably fleur de sel. Serve.

Title: Petrale w/ Lemon & Butter

Ingredients.Name: Lemons, juiced to make about 3-4 tbsp.
Chopped parsley or capers for garnish

Instructions: Rinse the filets and pat dry. Dredge the sole in flour and salt and pepper generously. Heat the oil in a large skillet preferably non-stick and sauté the sole over medium high heat until just beginning to brown but no more than about 2 minutes, flip over and cook another 2 minutes or until completely cooked through. Add the lemon juice and butter and coat all the fish with the juice and butter. Sprinkle with parsley or capers and serve immediately.

Title: Halibut with Bitter Greens

Ingredients.Name: Halibut filets cut into 1 ½” wide slices each
Head frisee or other bitter green like escarole, washed and torn
Green onions, white parts and about 2” of the green part sliced
Fennel bulb, sliced fine and then chopped fine
Meyer lemon or ½ regular lemon, cut into quarters, and seeds removed

Instructions: In a small bowl, combine the chopped fennel with the juice of the lemon. Let set for 15 minutes.

Place 2 tbsp. oil in a large non-stick sauté pan and heat over medium heat until hot. Dry the halibut filets and sprinkle with salt and pepper and then add to the hot skillet. Cook for 4 minutes on medium until the filets are partially opaque. Turn the halibut and cook for about 3-4 more minutes until cooked through but no more. Remove to a plate and add the rest of the oil to the hot skillet. Add the garlic and green onion and sauté quickly until tender. Add the greens and coat the greens with the garlic and green onions until just wilted. Sprinkle with a little salt and pepper. Divide the greens on plates and then top each with a filet. If you do this quickly, the fish will still be hot. Top the filets with a teaspoon of the fennel and lemon juice. Serve.

Title: Slow-Roasted Salmon

Ingredients.Name: Freshly ground white pepper to taste

Instructions: 1. Preheat the oven to 275F
2. Run your fingers over the top of the salmon fillet to detect any tiny bones that remain. Use tweezers to remove them. Cut the salmon into four equal pieces.

3. Place the salmon in an ovenproof dish that will hold the fish snugly. Using a pastry brush, brush the salmon on all sides with the oil. Place the baking dish in the center of the oven and roast until the fish is a bright pinkish orange and flakes easily, 17 minutes. Remove the dish from the oven, and trim off and discard any white milky portions or darkened edges around the fish. Using a wide spatula, transfer the fish to a small rack set on top of a plate, and allow it to drain.
4. Serve at room temperature, with Sorrel Sauce.

Title: Linguine w/ Clams
Description: This is my version of a classic. I love the addition of tart green tomatoes but if you don’t have them, try tomatillos or an acidic red tomato or leave it out all together.

Ingredients.Name: Dried linguine, preferably high quality imported
Small Green Tomatoes, cored, seeded and chopped

Instructions: Heat Water for boiling pasta while preparing sauce.

Heat oil and add onion and garlic in a saucepan large enough to hold all the clams and cook over high heat until onion is soft and garlic translucent. Don't let them brown. Add saffron and heat for l min. Add the wine and reduce heat til it simmers gently. Simmer until liquid is reduced by about 1/2.
(Add linguine to boiling water and cook til al dente while completing the sauce. Drain)
Add tomatoes and clams and cover. Cook until all the clams are opened - about 5 minutes. Toss any that don't open.
Pour over cooked linguine. Cover and let rest a couple minutes. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.
*Note - Soak clams in salted water (1T. per quart of water) for 3 hours to rid clams of sand.
If you can't use green tomatoes, you can substitute tomatillos or regular fresh red tomatoes.

Title: Spanish Shrimp
Instructions: Warm olive oil in a 9" skillet and add the garlic and hot pepper flakes. Heat until garlic begins to soften but not darken. Raise heat to high and add shrimp and toss to coat with oil. Add juice, sherry, paprika and cook until shrimp is just cooked through - all pink. Sprinkle with parsley and salt and pepper. Serve right in the skillet. Serve with warm, crusty bread to soak up the juices

Title: Smokey Tomato Soup

Ingredients.Name: Cans or Boxes of diced tomatoes, preferably Pomi
Spanish Parika – Pimenton de la Vera dulce
Bread cubes, crust removed and ¼” cubes

Instructions: Remove any tough stem ends from the tomatoes. Puree in food process or blender until smooth. Set aside.

In a large non-reactive saucepan – 4+ qt. size – heat the olive oil and red pepper flakes over medium heat until the pepper flakes begin to blacken. Remove from heat immediately and strain out the flakes. Return the oil to the pan. Add the butter and heat over medium heat until the butter foam subsides. Reduce to low-medium and add flour. Stir to make a roux and cook for 3 minutes, stirring well to incorporate the flour into the fats. Add the paprika and stir to incorporate. Cook for another 2 minutes. Add the vinegars and the broth and heat on medium until simmering. Simmer very gently for about 20 minutes. Taste and add salt and fresh pepper to taste. Simmer a few more minutes and taste again. You may want to add a little more seasoning at this point.
Prepare garnishes while soup simmers.

Heat 1 Tbsp. of oil in a small non-stick skillet (10”) over medium heat and while heating chop chorizo into ¼” cubes and add to the hot oil. Cook for about 2 minutes until the sausage is beginning to crisp. Remove to a small bowl with the oil. In the same skillet, heat the remaining 2 Tbsp. oil and add the bread cubes to the hot, but not smoking oil. Stir or toss until the cubes are golden but not black. Drain on paper towel and toss with some salt while still hot.
Serve the soup: To each bowl of soup, sprinkle a few chorizo pieces with a little of the oil, top with a few bread cubes and a generous sprinkle of cilantro.

Title: Tortilla Soup
Description: This is an easy and quick dish if you have left-over chicken on hand.

Ingredients.Name: Guajillo chilis (or substitute 2 pasilla for the 3)
Mexican mild cheese cut into cubes about ½”
Spinach leaves, washed and stemmed if large
Fresh tortilla chips, broken into small pieces

Instructions: In a dry skillet, toast the chilis over medium heat until beginning to brown and they begin to get soft and their spicy scent is apparent. Use tongs to keep them from browning by frequent turning. While still hot, remove stems and seeds and cover with the warm water and let sit for 30 mins. Remove from the water and place in blender and pour in water. Blend until a puree.

Heat the oven to 425 degrees. In a small ceramic dish, place the tomatoes and garlic in the pan and place into the oven. Roast until the tomatoes begin to color and the garlic is soft. Peel the garlic and add the garlic and tomatoes to the blender and puree. This should be fairly smooth but thick sauce.
To the ceramic dish that you roasted the tomatoes and garlic in, add a little chicken stock and scrap up the juices and browned bits.

In a large deep skillet, cook the onion in the oil until tender. Add the puree, and chicken stock from the pan and the remaining. Heat until simmering and cook for about 15 minutes and then add the chicken. Cook for about 5 minutes more until the chicken is hot and the flavors have melded. Toss in the spinace leaves.
Garnish with the avocado, cheese and tortilla chips.

Title: Spring Pea Soup

Ingredients.Name: Yellow or white potatoes, peeled and chopped
Chopped chives or other herbs for garnish

Instructions: Bring stock to a boil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add potatoes to stock, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add scallions; cook for 5 minutes. Add peas, increase heat to medium, and cook until just tender (to keep fresh pea taste), about 5 minutes.
Purée pea mixture in a blender or food processor. Press through a strainer using a spoon. Return briefly to heat. Season with salt, pepper, and chives.

Title: Sorrel Soup
Description: This soup is easy and delicious. You can lighten it by reducing the amount of cream to 1/2 Cup.

Ingredients.Name: Chicken stock, prefer homemade but canned low sodium is o.k.
Sorrel leaves, stems removed and cut into ribbons
Sea salt and fresh black pepper

Instructions: Heat butter in a heavy pot - large and non-reactive. Add onions and potatoes when melted and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Add the sorrel and toss to blend well. Add stock and increase heat to medium high to bring stock to simmer. Simmer for 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
If you like your soup with texture, add the cream now and bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

Creamy variation - take soup in batches to a processor or blender and puree until chunky and not entirely smooth. Be careful that it doesn't rise up and burn you. Return to pot and return to a just bare simmer. Season with salt and pepper and serve. Do not boil the cream.
* This is also good cold.

Title: Chestnut Soup
Description: This is my version of a classic chestnut soup. The brandy offsets the richness of this dish which is a great holiday time first course. Because it is rich, follow with lighter courses or simple roasted meats.

Ingredients.Name: Roasted, shelled and skinned chestnuts or vacuum packed imported
Small shallots, peeled, and thinly sliced into rounds
Large fennel bulb, greens removed, white bulb chopped well (retain fronds for garnish)
Chicken stock, defatted or non-fat canned

Instructions: Coarsely chop chestnuts.

Cook leeks in butter in a 5-quart heavy pot over moderate heat, stirring, until softened. Add wine and simmer until almost all liquid is evaporated, about 1 minute. Stir in fennel, broth, chestnuts, and water, then simmer, covered, 20 minutes. Stir in half-and-half and cool mixture slightly.

Purée mixture in batches in a blender until smooth, transferring to a bowl (use caution when blending hot liquids). Return soup to pot and bring to a simmer, thinning with water if desired. Season with salt and pepper.

For garnish: heat olive oil til hot but not smoking. While oil is heating, toss shallots with flour and shake off excess. Add the shallots to hot oil and cook until crispy and golden. Drain on paper towels.
Serve soup topped with shallots and a few snips from the fennel fronds.

Title: Wild Mushroom Broth
Description: Serve with parsnip custards.

Ingredients.Name: Chicken wings or chicken bones with some flesh
Mushrooms - combination of field and oyster mushrooms, cleaned and stems removed.

Instructions: Preheat oven to 450*
Place wings and/or bones in a roasting pan and season with salt. Bake for 40 minutes or until deeply brown.

In a small bowl, cover the mushrooms with the boiling water and soak until soft, about 15-20 min. Gently rub the mushrooms to remove any grit and transfer them to a plate. Let the soaking liquid settle and pour off liquid leaving the dirt at the bottom.

In a large saucepan, heat the oil over medium high heat and saute the onion until just beginning to brown, about 5 minutes and then add the mushroom stems and about half the caps. Add the porcini and their liquor and stir in about 3 pints of water. Bring to a boil and add the chicken wings and bones.
Use 1 Cup of water to deglaze the roasting pan, getting up all the browned bits, and add to the saucepan. Simmer for about 2 hours. It should have reduced to about 5 Cups of water total.
Skim the fat off the broth.
Re-heat and season with salt and pepper.
In a skillet, saute remaining mushrooms in butter until golden.
To serve, float the mushrooms in the broth.
For a special dish, serve with parsnip custards.

Title: Parsnip Custards for soup

Ingredients.Name: Parsnips, peeled and cut into thick slices

Instructions: Preheat oven to 325*
Butter 6 1/4 cup ramekins.
In a medium saucepan, steam the parsnips with a little water until very tender, about 30 minutes.

Puree parsnips in food processor or blender until smooth. Strain through a sieve and add eggs, milk, cream and salt and pepper to the custard and pour into the ramekins. Set the ramekins in a larger baking dish and pour boiling water around them about half way up the sides. Cover the entire pan with foil and bake for approx. 45 minutes until they are set. Gently invert the custards onto a spatula and transfer to soup bowls and ladle broth around them.

Title: Roasted Yellow Pepper Soup
Description: This is my version of Cibreo's famous yellow pepper soup.

Ingredients.Name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil, plus a little for garnish
Sea salt, fine, plus more to taste
Small yellow potatoes - Yukon, cleaned and cut into quarters.
Baguette, sliced thin and then cut into tiny cubes
Chicken broth, homemade and de-fatted or non-fat canned

Instructions: Pre-heat oven 375*
Core and cut peppers into about 8 pieces per pepper.
Line a non-stick backing sheet with a thin layer of 1 Tbsp. olive oil.
Scatter peppers over oil and drizzle another Tbsp. over the peppers.
Roast 30-40 minutes until the skins of the peppers are golden and beginning to blacken in spots.
Cool slightly and remove the majority of the skins, particularly the blackened bits. Leaving some skin is o.k.

In a large saucepan, heat 2 Tbsp. of oil and add the shallots, cook until translucent, and add the peppers and the broth and the water. Turn heat to high and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to maintain gentle simmer and add salt and a few grindings of fresh pepper. Add the potatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes. Remove potatoes from pot and drain in colander. As soon as they are cool to the touch, remove skins and return potatoes to pot. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Puree peppers in broth with potatoes. Add water if too thick.
Return to saucepan and gently re-heat. Taste for seasoning and add salt and pepper if necessary.
In a small saute pan, heat 2 Tbsp. of oil and toss in the baguette cubes. Cook until crisp, adding a little more olive oil if needed to make sure the cubes get very golden and crisp.
Put soup into wide bowls, garnish with a drizzle of oil and a few of the bread cubes.

Title: White Gazpacho

Ingredients.Name: Fresh sweet baguette or other French style bread
Seedless Green Grapes - about 6 per person

Instructions: Remove crust from a piece of baguette about 6-8" long and soak in 1 Cup water about 1 minute. Squeeze dry and discard the water.
Mash garlic with salt in a mortar.

Blend almonds with garlic/salt paste in a food processor until they are as smooth as possible. Add bread and 1 T. vinegar and the Sherry, and pulse til incorporated. With motor running, add oil in a thin stream then add ice water and blend well. Force solids through a very fine sieve, pressing out all the liquid. Discard solid.
Transfer liquid to a ceramic or glass container and chill until very cold. Taste for seasoning - add more salt and vinegar as necessary.
Serve in chilled bowls and garnish with tiny cubes of skinless cucumber and the grapes sliced in half.

Title: Butternut Squash Soup
Description: This is easy, healthy and delicious.

Ingredients.Name: Chicken broth (or 2 cans of low sodium, non-fat broth)
Low fat sour cream for garnish (or whipped cream)
Fresh herbs or parsley if you have them
Sea salt and fresh ground pepper

Instructions: Preheat oven to 350%

Cut squash in half lengthwise and place on a piece of foil on a baking sheet, cut sides down. Roast for 45 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the thickest part goes easily through. Remove from oven and when cool enough peel off the skin.

In a large pot, heat the oil or the butter and sauté the onions until transparent. While the onions are cooking, puree the squash in a blender or whip with a beater, adding broth to keep it loose. Add the onion and puree again. When smooth, add to the onions and then add the rest of the broth until it is thick but soupy, not saucy. Add water until you get the right consistency if you need to. Heat the soup on medium heat until it just begins to simmer and reduce to maintain no more than a simmer and cook for about 20 minutes. Taste and add salt and fresh ground pepper until it balances the sweetness of the squash. Serve with a small dollop of sour cream or even whipped cream, with some chopped parsley or other herbs. It is also good with croutons or crispy breadcrumbs sautéed in olive oil. I also like to finish it with a few sprinkles of fleur de sel.
Note – if you don’t have a blender (which purees better than a food processor, you can just chop the onions finely and have a more textured soup.
Also, for flavor variation, you can add a pinch or two of curry powder or a pinch of ground ginger.

Title: Minestra
Description: My version takes on qualities of whatever is left over in the fridge. It is really about not cooking the veggies too long and keeping the flavors bright. It is always best with fresh broth, but don’t hesitate to use canned if you just don’t have the fresh.

Ingredients.Name: Leeks (substitute one large onion if you don’t have leeks)
Stalks celery and some of the leaves, sliced
Fresh fennel, core removed and sliced thin
One starch – either brown rich, white beans, or faro

Instructions: If you are using white beans, you will need to cover them with boiling water and soak for 1 hour. Drain the beans and add to a pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes. Add ¼ tsp. salt and then continue to cook for 30 minutes more or until tender.

In a large soup pot, put the bacon and olive oil over medium heat and sauté until bacon is golden. Add leeks and turn heat to low and sweat the leeks until just tender. Add the celery, fennel and carrots and sauté for about 3 minutes. Add the chicken broth. Add the by leaf and thyme. Simmer for 20 minutes gently until the veggies are tender. Add the beans if using, or add the brown rice or the faro and cook for another 30 minutes. Adjust seasoning with more salt and pepper. !0 minutes before serving, add the greens and cook until tender.
Serve with parmesan cheese and croutons or toasted bread slices.

Title: Chicken Broth
Description: If you use a carcass from a roasted chicken dinner, the soup will have more flavor. To give it real deep flavor, roast the carcass with the veggies until golden, then make the broth.
Instructions: Put the chicken carcass (from roasted chicken or other cooking method – it doesn’t matter) in a large heavy pot (4 qts or larger). If you want to use fresh chicken, you can remove all meat for another use except the wings which you can throw in whole. Cover with cold water – you should use about 2 ½ qts or a little more to cover the chicken. Quarter the onion, slice the celery and the carrots in 2 inch chunks and add those. Turn the heat to high and add the bay leaf, parsley, salt and pepper. Bring to the barest boil and reduce the heat so that the soup simmers gently. Simmer for one hour. Skim off the scum that collects on the surface at least several times. Taste the broth, and check for flavor. Add more salt if you need it. If the flavor is too weak, continue to cook for approx. another ½ hour. Remove from heat and cool. Remove the bones and drain in colander, pressing on the solids to press out the flavors. Place in fridge and chill overnight or for at least a few hours. Skim fat entirely off the top.

If you want to make the broth really flavorful, put the carcass in a roasting pan, add the vegetables and roast in a 350 degree oven for about 40 minutes until everything is golden brown. Then place in pot with cold water…it gives a richer taste but takes a little longer.

Title: Chipotle Roasted Carrots
Description: My variant on a Food & Wine recipe

Ingredients.Name: Baby carrots (2 to 3 bunches), tops discarded, carrots scrubbed
Nonfat Greek yoghurt with freshly grated lemon zest to serve along side the carrots
chipotle chiles in adobo, minced, plus 1 teaspoon of adobo sauce from the can

Instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°. Toss the carrots on a rimmed baking sheet with the chipotles, molasses and 2 tablespoons of the olive oil; season with salt and pepper. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, until the carrots are crisp-tender and browned. Transfer the carrots to a plate and let them cool completely.
On the plate, toss the carrots with the 1 teaspoon of adobo sauce. Serve or garnish with the yogurt.

Title: Vegetarian Chili
Description: This is delicious and easy and if you serve it with brown rice, a nicely complex carbohydrate and protein meal.

Ingredients.Name: Can (14 oz.) fire roasted tomatoes, diced
Medium yellow onions, peeled, cut into quarters and then sliced
Chipotle chilis in adobo (from a can) chopped
Small red peppers, washed, cut in cubes ½”
Medium zucchini, washed, cut in ½” cubes
Ears, fresh sweet corn or substitute 1 cup frozen if you can’t get fresh
Can (14 oz) of low-sodium kidney beans
Grated sharp cheddar or queso fresco
Brown rice for soaking up the juices

Instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet until hot, add onions and let them caramelize a bit before reducing the heat to medium. Add the red peppers and zucchini and cook until they both begin to soften and maybe caramelize a bit (so don’t stir). Then, add the beans, tomatoes and the spices, including a liberal amount of salt (about ½ tsp to start). Cook on medium low heat until the beans begin to soak up the flavors and all the veggies are tender, about one hour. Add a little water to keep it from sticking and to keep a nice most saucy glaze. The stew is best if you let it rest at this point with the lid on (off the heat) for about an hour. Before serving, add the corn and reheat for about 5 minutes until the corn is cooked. You may need to add a bit of water to keep it juicy. Adjust the salt.
Serve with brown rice, and top it with chopped cilantro, grated sharp cheddar or Mexican queso fresco, and some fresh lime juice squeezed over.

Title: Summer Tomato Puddings

Ingredients.Name: Summer firm ripe tomatoes, halved lengthwise
Fresh chopped herbs, such as basil, thyme and parsley
Bread, rustic country, such as Levain, cubes
Grated Italian mild cheese, such as mild pecorino, fontina, or teleme

Instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.Butter a 3-quart shallow baking dish (about 13 by 9 inches).
Toss tomatoes in a bowl with herbs, 1 tablespoon oil, 3/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Arrange tomatoes, cut sides up, in a large heavy 4-sided sheet pan.

Cut off and discard 1/4 inch from top of garlic head to expose cloves, then put on a sheet of foil and drizzle with 1 teaspoon oil. Wrap garlic in foil and roast in pan with tomatoes until tomatoes are browned but still juicy and garlic is soft, 50 to 60 minutes. (Leave oven on.) Cool garlic to warm, then force through a medium-mesh sieve with a rubber spatula, discarding skins. Reserve purée.
While garlic cooks, toss bread cubes in a large bowl with remaining oil until coated, then spread out in a large 4-sided sheet pan and bake until golden brown, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool in pan.
Reduce oven temperature to 350°F.

Whisk together milk, cream, eggs, garlic purée, 2 teaspoons salt, and 1 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Stir in cheeses. Transfer bread to baking dish, then pour egg mixture over bread and add tomatoes, pushing some down between bread cubes. Bake until firm to the touch and golden brown in spots, 50 to 60 minutes.

Title: Mushroom Bread Puddings
Description: Makes a great side dish to grilled or roasted meats.

Ingredients.Name: Bread (brioche or challah, cut in ½ inch cubes
Fresh wild mushrooms, chanterelles, oyster, etc., trimmed and cleaned

Instructions: 8 (6-ounce) ramekins
Preheat oven to 350°F with rack in middle.
Bake bread cubes in 1 layer in a large shallow baking pan until golden-brown, about 10 minutes.

Cut mushrooms lengthwise into 1/4-inch-thick pieces. Cook shallot in butter in a 12-inch heavy skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften, about 3 minutes. Add mushrooms, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper and cook until liquid mushrooms give off has evaporated, about 15 minutes. Add parsley and garlic and cook, stirring, 2 minutes. Remove from heat.

Whisk together half-and-half, eggs, cheese, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper in a large bowl. Stir in mushrooms and bread cubes until coated well and let stand 10 minutes for bread to absorb some of egg mixture.
Meanwhile, butter ramekins, then put a round of parchment in bottom of each and butter parchment.
Spoon mixture into ramekins and bake on a baking sheet until firm to the touch, 30 to 35 minutes. Unmold puddings and discard parchment.
Notes: Pudding can be baked in a buttered 2-quart shallow baking dish (not lined with parchment). Pudding can be assembled (but not baked) 2 hours ahead and chilled, covered.

Title: Grilled Chard w/ Sweet Peas
Description: This works equally well with Favas and even Edamame.

Ingredients.Name: Red Swiss Chard or Rainbow, separate leaves and stems*
Sea Salt and Fresh Black Pepper to taste
Charcoal grill, prepared for direct heat grilling
Fresh herbs, chopped (use marjoram, oregano, thyme – whatever is fresh)

Instructions: Trim the stems. Blanch in boiling salted water for about 2-3 minutes until just beginning to be tender. If the stalks are very tough or wide, you can cook a minute or two longer. Drain and run under cold water to stop cooking. Dry on towels.
