This can be done a few hours in advance. Just cover once dry.

When the fire is hot but not flaming, toss the stems with half the olive oil and arrange on the grill if they are large. If not, use a grilling sheet or pan with holes in it on top of the grill. Grill quickly, lid off, until the stems get lightly charred on the edges and a little golden along the middles. Remove from heat onto a plate.

In a medium saute pan, heat remaining oil. Add the hot pepper and garlic and cook until garlic is translucent. Add the chard and toss until coated with the oil. Add the sweet peas and cook for about 2-3 minutes over medium heat until they begin to get tender. Toss in the herbs, sprinkle with salt and pepper and serve.

Title: Swiss Chard Gratin

Ingredients.Name: Pinch or two of red pepper flakes
Cheese - grated - either parmesan reggiano or gruyere

Instructions: Wash chard well and separate stems from leaves. Trim stems and cut into tidy batons about 3 " in length x 1/4". Blanch in boiling salted water with the bay leaf for about 4 minutes. Drain well in colander. Slice leaves into ribbons crosswise.

Title: Parsnip Custard
Description: Serve this with the Wild Mushroom Broth or as a side dish to roasted meats. The recipe calls for 1/4 cup ramekins but I substitute espresso cups which are a little smaller so they need a little less cooking time.

Ingredients.Name: Parsnips, peeled and cut into thick slices
Sea salt or a little more to taste, if necessary

Instructions: Preheat to 325*
Lightly butter ramekins no larger than 1/4 Cup; or a glass baking dish that is 8" square or 8" x 12" max.
Steam the parsnips in a small amount of water for about 25 minutes in a medium saucepan. Cool slightly.

While the parsnips cook, blend the eggs lightly in a medium mixing bowl. Add the milk, cream, salt and pepper and blend well. Add the parsnips when cool and blend with custard. Strain through a fine sieve and poor into the ramekins or baking dishes and set them into a larger baking dish with enough water to reach about halfway up the sides of the ramekins. Cover with foil, not too tightly and bake for about 45 minutes for the ramekins and about an hour for the larger baking dish. They should be set in the center.
These can be made one day in advance, stored in the refrigerator and heated in a microwave for serving.

Title: Roasted Tomatoes

Ingredients.Name: Firm tomatoes – best to use full flavor summer tomatoes – off season, use romas

Instructions: Preheat oven to 300 degrees.
Line a baking sheet(s) with parchment (or foil).

Cut tomatoes in half and place cut side down. Drizzle with about 1 Tbsp. of olive oil. Roast for 30 minutes. Sprinkle with salt and roast for another 30 minutes or until the skins are brown on top and shriveled. Remove from oven and cool until you can slide the skins off. Place the tomatoes in a bowl and drizzle with oil until covered with a thin film.
Use these to make the best pasta sauce, to add to soups, or toss into winter salads or make a rich bruschetta. They freeze well and will keep in the fridge covered in oil for about a week.

Title: Ratatouille
Description: This can easily be expanded by tossing in more veggies. You can’t make a mistake. Try not to cook it too long or it turns into a mushy mess. If that happens, toss it with pasta as a sauce.

Ingredients.Name: Yellow onion, quartered and then sliced
Zucchini, cut into ¼ in. slices
Can (14oz) whole peeled tomatoes or 6 fresh tomatoes
Parmesan or other dry aged cheese grated

Instructions: In a large heavy non-reactive pot, add ½ the oil and heat until the oil forms a slick over the bottom of the pan. Add the eggplant and toss so it is lightly coated with oil. Cook until it begins to turn transparent and then add the onions. If it sticks, add a little more oil. Toss until the onions begin to soften and then add the red peppers. Again, toss gently and cook until they begin to soften and add the zucchini, garlic and toss with the balance of the oil, if you have any left. Cook until the zucchini is hot and add the tomatoes crushing them as you add them. Add the salt and the basil. Cover and cook until all the veggies are cooked through and tender and the flavors are melding. Serve with a little cheese sprinkle over the top for serving.

Title: Potatoes with Fleur de Sel

Ingredients.Name: baby potatoes (fingerlings or small Yukon Gold), rinsed
unsalted butter ( or substitute extra-virgin olive oil)

Instructions: Place the potatoes in a large pot. Add the butter, garlic if using, and coarse sea salt. Cover and cook over the lowest possible heat, turning from time to time, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork and are browned in patches, about 20 minutes. ( The cooking time will vary according to the size of the potatoes.) Using a slotted spoon, transfer the potatoes to a serving bowl. Serve, passing a small dish of fleur de sel at the table.

Title: Simple Sautéed Greens
Description: I like this best with Swiss Chard but it is also good with spinach and other greens, although cooking time will vary.

Ingredients.Name: Bunches of Swiss Chard - green, red or rainbow
Extra Virgin Olive Oil plus extra for garnish

Instructions: Wash and trim stems from chard.

In a large saute pan, heat the olive oil and add the shallot. Cook over high heat until translucent and add the garlic, stir well and cook until the garlic is fragrant. If using the red pepper, add now, and just heat through. Stir. Add the chard, with the little bit of water still clinging to its leaves from washing. Toss with the hot oil and coat well. Continue cooking until limp and tender, about 5 minutes, reducing the heat if necessary to keep from browning. Usually, the greens throw off a lot of water so you can cook them on fairly high heat. Toss with sea salt and fresh ground pepper. Drain off some of the liquid, if the greens threw off a lot.
Serve with a drizzle of fresh olive oil, best quality and a sprinkling of salt.

Title: Roasted Vegetables
Description: This is one of those recipes that adjusts easily to number of people and to different vegetables. Just increase the oil enough so that all pieces are very lightly coated. To make it really special, add fresh baby artichokes.

Ingredients.Name: Butternut squash (save other half for another use)
French fillet beans or very small green beans
Extra Virgin Olive Oil - good quality

Instructions: Preheat Oven to 400 degrees.

Seed, trim and cut the butternut squash into small cubes, about 1/2 inches square. Cut off green fronds down to the bulb of the fennel. Wash the fennel well and cut into 8-10 wedges, depending on size of bulb. Toss butternut squash and fennel with about 2 Tbs. of the oil. Place in large ovenproof casserole, or gratin dish (9x13 is best). Place in oven for ten minutes. Meanwhile cut onions into 8 wedges each and toss with about 1 Tbsp. oil. Add to squash/fennel at the end of the first ten minutes. Toss green beans with garlic and oil. Add to the mixture in the oven. Cook at 400 for another 10 minutes. Salt and pepper generously and toss ingredients well. Reduce oven temp to 350 and continue cooking about twenty (20) more minutes. Test the squash by piercing with a fork or knife. If soft, the veggies are done, otherwise, continue cooking til tender and the tips of the green beans are brown. The onions should also be caramelizing quite a bit. Serve hot and adjust salt and pepper.

Title: Golden Scallop Potatoes

Ingredients.Name: Comte Cheese (You can substitute Gruyere or even Parmesan)
Homemade chicken stock (or substitute low fat, low sodium canned broth)

Instructions: Preheat oven to 375*.
Butter a large gratin or baking dish, approx. 9x13".

Peel potatoes and slice thinly, about 1/8" in a processor or mandolin. If not using immediately, cover with cold water and then drain and dry thoroughly with towels before proceeding. Otherwise, toss potatoes immediately in a large bowl with the flour.

Arrange the potatoes in layers in the prepared dish. After one layer, sprinkle with about 1/3 of the cheese and dot with about 1 Tbsp. butter in small pieces. Continue layering until the top layer has cheese and butter on top.
heat the stock in a saucepan on the stove and pour over the potatoes. It should just cover them. Add a little water if it doesn't.

Bake the potatoes about 1 1/2 hours until the potatoes are tender and the top beautifully golden. If you don't plan to serve it right away, stop cooking at about 1 1/4 hours. Reduce oven temp to about 300 and you can hold it this way for about 1/2-1 hour. Check it so it doesn't get too dry. Serve hot.

Title: Peach Cobbler Loaf

Ingredients.Name: Peaches, pitted (no need to peel), each cut into 8 wedges
Unsalted butter, melted (cold is fine before melting)
Plain unsweetened Greek yogurt or sour cream

Instructions: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a loaf pan with parchment, letting it hang over two sides, and spray any unlined spots with nonstick spray. Set the pan on a larger sheet pan to catch any drips.
Toss the peach wedges with the lemon juice, cinnamon, and 1 tablespoon of the brown sugar in a bowl; set aside.

In a large bowl, whisk the melted butter with the granulated sugar, remaining brown sugar, and lemon zest. Mix in the yogurt (or sour cream), then beat in the eggs. Sprinkle the baking powder, baking soda, and salt over the top and whisk well. Stir in the flour just until it disappears.

For the streusel, mix the melted butter with the sugar and a pinch of salt in a small bowl, then stir in the flour until crumbs form (the mixture will look soft/pasty at first but clumps into crumbs as you work it).

Spread half the batter in the prepared pan. Arrange half the peaches over it in one layer. Spread the remaining batter on top, then arrange the rest of the peaches over that. Pour any juices left in the peach bowl over the top, then sprinkle with the streusel.

Set the pan (still on its sheet pan) in the oven and bake 60–70 minutes, until a tester inserted in the center and under the top layer of peaches comes out clean; it may need up to 5 minutes more. Tent loosely with foil partway through if the top is browning too fast. Cool on a rack.
Run a knife along any unlined sides and lift the loaf out using the parchment. Slice thickly to serve. Keeps well at room temperature for a few days, and many find it even better on day two or three.
